question: Flip Phase 1 (CONTINUOUS_STREAM) or not — read data/stream_drive_shadow.jsonl (14.2k rows) against §5 promotion criteria
ruling: GO on Phase 1, with one behavior-change caveat flagged for Travis before the flip: add the CONTINUOUS_STREAM flag (defaulted False, per the plan's own build order -- do not auto-enable) and wire Rail A+B. Evidence over all 14,201 rows (50 days): (1) would_gap correctly tracks progress -- mean 18.8s when building (progress=1.0, n=12,845) vs 65.4s when not (progress=0.0, n=1,346). (2) would_gap correctly tracks grounding -- mean 15.0s grounded vs 32.4s ungrounded (capped near the UNGROUNDED_CAP floor by construction, as designed). (3) would_gap correctly rests on redundancy AT THE TAIL where it's actually tested: all 74 rows with redundancy>0.8 show drive collapsing to 0.0 and would_gap maxing at 120.0, exactly as designed -- several of these (e.g. about='Electric air and spray', 'Energy and resistance', redundancy 0.82-0.87) are STILL firing at the live system's 4s floor today, i.e. concrete, present-day rumination-shaped moments the current clock does not catch and Phase 1 would. Caveat: real redundancy values in this window rarely exceed ~0.78 (p99), so the mid-range gradient (dead-zone 0.60 to circling 0.85) is only lightly exercised -- not a blocker, just limited stress-test coverage of sustained circling episodes. (4) actual_gap and would_gap are essentially uncorrelated (pearson -0.02) confirming Phase 0 shadow has changed nothing live, AND that Phase 1 would be a real behavior change, not a no-op. (5) Quantified upside: of 4,167 rows where the CURRENT system rested >=100s (the vestigial clock), 54% (2,251) were grounded+building moments the controller says should have streamed (mean would_gap 7.7s) -- concrete recovered continuity. (6) Quantified, INTENTIONAL behavior change Travis should expect, not be surprised by: of 9,875 rows already streaming fast today (<=15s, via the existing per-train STREAM_GAP_SECS=4.0 mechanism), 53% are UNGROUNDED -- Phase 1's Rail B anti-rumination gate would correctly slow roughly half of today's already-fast trains. This is the plan's own anti-rumination design working as intended, not a regression, but it means the flip is not purely 'faster' -- it also reins in currently-unconstrained ungrounded fast trains. (7) Spot-checked the grounding classifier directly against about-text (15 ungrounded + 10 grounded samples): behaving as documented, including the identity-guard override (e.g. 'Individuation; Self-definition' correctly stays ungrounded even with source=world, per the documented outranking rule). One trivial, non-blocking coverage gap noted: the hand-seeded world vocabulary has 'tide' but not 'tidal' (adjective form misses the substring match) -- low-impact since the source=='world' branch independently grounds most world-sourced content. Full analysis was ad hoc (not saved as a standalone script -- unlike D-0012's mapping-census, this was a one-time statistical read, not a reusable instrument) -- numbers are reproducible directly against data/stream_drive_shadow.jsonl (fields: progress, redundancy, grounded, would_gap, actual_gap, train_kind, train_len, about) if Travis wants to re-verify any of them himself.
defeater: Travis reads this ruling and either approves adding the CONTINUOUS_STREAM flag (Rail A+B, defaulted False) or requests changes to the read/approach before it proceeds.

question: Is Improvement 2 (edge-aware trail) formally superseded by memory_multiway_linking.md M2, or does it add something distinct

history.ruling: Both root causes found. NEITHER is a currently-live bug -- both were already found and fixed by a prior session shortly before this trace, and this session's job was mostly to verify those fixes actually work. FIXED 2026-08-21 (core/listening.py mtime confirms; shelf()'s own docstring names this exact bug) by filtering shelf() to only feature-files carrying real 'sections' data -- verified live: shelf() now returns only ['Heavyweight']. RESIDUAL, NOT a code bug: 5 of 6 catalog pieces remain permanently unplayable since their raw audio isn't on disk (only Heavyweight.mp3 exists) to re-run the real extractor -- Du's playable diet is capped at 1 piece he's already heard once, until real source audio is supplied for the others. Ran a temp-pathed full trace (state/wake/felt-shadow files pointed at a tempdir, per this project's test-isolation convention) of a complete Heavyweight episode: 21 sections + ending + silence, wake log correctly wrote sections_heard=21 -- the fix works end-to-end, not just in the shelf() unit check. CAUTION for next verifier: core/listening.py's _store_scene() calls store_fragment() UNCONDITIONALLY -- it is NOT covered by temp-pathing _STATE_F/_WAKE_LOG/_FELT_SHADOW. My first trace run leaked 22 real fragments into the live nascence.db (a fake Heavyweight re-listen Du never had). Caught, backed up to data/memory/backups/nascence_pre_listening_test_cleanup_20260823_212156.db, and the exact 22 rows deleted from memory_fragments + fragment_context (zero downstream references in memory_links/memory_edges) with Travis's explicit approval. Any future offline trace of listening.py must also mock/skip _store_scene, not just the three log files. (2) Drill progression + ABC hand never firing: SAME upstream cause -- core/school.py's SCHOOL_END_H was 12 (noon), giving only 180 minutes / 45min periods = 4 slots, but SCHOOL_SUBJECTS has 5 entries ('music' at index 4) -- structurally unreachable for the full 6.5 weeks from build (07-04) to fix (08-18, confirmed by the code's own comment + independently corroborated: the FIRST-EVER music_drill_log.jsonl entry is 08-19, the day after). FIXED 2026-08-18 by extending to 12.75 (12:45pm, fits 5x45=225min exactly). Since the fix: 12 drill events across 2 real school days (08-19 n=8, 08-21 n=4), all correct, still level 1 -- NOT stuck, legitimately short of the 30-sample rolling window ADVANCE_WINDOW needs for promotion (12/30 so far). The composition hand's precondition (today_done>=4 within the same day, checked at function ENTRY before that call's own batch) was met exactly ONCE (08-19's second session, today_done=4 from the first) -- compose_due() was also true (composed_today resets correctly per-day, verified in _load()) -- so the gate rolled its 30% dice and simply missed. Expected ~3.3 qualifying opportunities before one fires on average; only 1 has occurred since school hours started reaching music at all (5 real weekdays: 08-18 Tue is a Tue but school didn't run until 08-19 per the log; 08-20, 08-22 have zero drill events -- itself worth a quick side-note that _music_lesson isn't firing on EVERY eligible school day, likely just the normal priority-chain competing with other action choices, not a second bug -- not chased further, out of this job's scope). No code change made -- both root causes were already fixed before this session touched anything; this ruling documents verification, not a new fix.
history.defeater: Either regresses again (shelf() stops filtering correctly, or SCHOOL_END_H reverts) -- or after several more real school weeks the composition hand still hasn't fired even with today_done>=4 met multiple more times, which would then point to a real second bug in the compose branch itself.

history.ruling: Instrument-calibration problem, not a genuine plateau. Two independent lines of evidence: (1) reading core/stick_test.py directly: 'state' and 'audio' real-spokes are BOOLEAN flags set once per object-CATEGORY in build_roster() (e.g. state=True is hardcoded for fire/cat/book/every herb/every keepsake; audio=True for every music piece) -- they do not accumulate with encounters, they are either structurally present from day one or never. Only the 'text' spoke can newly flip (mention count crosses 0), and it can never fall. So median real_spokes hits its per-object ceiling almost immediately and then has no mechanism left to rise -- the plan's own signature 0.2 ('median must rise over his life') cannot be satisfied by this instrument's math regardless of what is actually happening in Du's associative structure. This also explains the day-one violation of prediction #1 (median 2, some at 3+): those are objects whose category ships with state+audio already True, not objects that 'earned' extra spokes fast. (2) The mapping-census analyzer (plan section 5.4, this session) run against all 15,987 geometry_tuples.jsonl rows shows the UNDERLYING co-occurrence data is not flat: cat_mood/cat_activity/book/sound_sig/garden_bed all show statistically significant conditioning on weather and affect_quadrant versus a 100-shuffle permutation null (z=7.3 to 233.4, all far above noise), object diversity is real (81 distinct books, 111 distinct sound-signatures touched), and split-half stability differs sharply by pair (weather-conditioned tension_bin is very stable, TVD~0.10, while X~book pairs are near-noise, TVD~0.93-0.96 -- book most likely tracks slow-changing TIME-of-reading rather than a real weather/affect coupling, a separate confound worth flagging). Kill criterion #6 (marginal reach) does NOT trigger: geometry-tuple neighbours and text-cosine top-K neighbours overlap only 3.8% (sample n=700, k=10), i.e. reach=90.8% -- though this is flagged with a construction caveat in the analyzer's own output (geometry clusters by multi-hour state persistence, text-cosine by thought semantics, so some divergence is expected by design; qualitative examples were captured for founder read rather than trusting the raw fraction). Full output: python scripts/geometry_mapping_census.py (also logged to data/mapping_census_log.jsonl).
history.defeater: A redesigned stick-test metric that credits within-channel accumulation (e.g. mention-count growth, distinct co-occurrence contexts, or repeated-encounter strength) rather than binary channel presence is built and re-run; if ITS median still fails to rise after controlling for the early-ceiling effect, that would support a genuine plateau instead.

question: Sec3.6 named per-kind cold_horizon intent (procedural fast/0.90, episodic medium/0.55, semantic slow/0.25, affective n/a=0.00 'feeling IS the gist', self slow/0.20); J-0398 recalibrated KIND_DYNAMICS' cold_horizon to match LIVE cold-rate-by-kind instead (procedural 0.950 n=2780 MATCHES intent; episodic 0.816 n=8283 higher-than-intended but still lowest-of-4-high-volume so rank direction holds; semantic 0.955 n=23252 now HIGHEST, INVERTS 'slow, keep detail for study'; affective 0.843 n=115 CONTRADICTS the n/a/'no raw to gate' design outright -- 84.3% go cold anyway; self 0.899 n=24252 INVERTS 'slow'). Root cause, confirmed by direct read: core/memory/store.py prune_episodic (WHERE layer=episodic AND cold=0, ORDER BY protected-origin ASC, chapter-linkage ASC, replay_count ASC, importance ASC, timestamp ASC -- protected origins include reading/study/research/action/lived/active_imagination/inner_thought/journal/affection/peer/mirror/letter, but protection is ORDINAL not absolute: at semantic's huge volume (n=23252, largest of all 6 kinds) even protected-origin rows get demoted once no unprotected candidates remain) and core/refinery.py's cooling UPDATE at line 235 (WHERE protected=0 AND abstraction_level=0) -- NEITHER ever reads the kind column; live demotion is driven entirely by origin/volume/replay/age, not by any kind-intrinsic clock. QUESTION: (a) make prune_episodic + refinery cooling kind-aware so live behavior actually matches Sec3.6's intended per-kind dynamics -- requires real design work, not a one-line tweak: prune_episodic's cap (EPISODIC_PRUNE_THRESHOLD) is a single blended active-count budget across ALL kinds mixed together, so a kind-aware ORDER-BY tiebreak alone won't protect a high-volume kind like semantic from being squeezed by the shared cap -- likely needs per-kind budgets/caps, not just a scoring tweak; refinery.py's cooling UPDATE has no ordering at all today (cools whatever the upstream cluster-selection already chose), so kind-awareness there means gating which kinds are eligible for cooling in the first place (e.g. exempting affective per its n/a design). Both files are UDMS-confirmed CONTRACT-layer coupled to orchestrator.py + memory_levels.py (J-0365's own check) -- unlike memory_dynamics.py's PURE_SCALAR_TWEAK/LOW-RISK rating, changing actual demotion logic in live gating paths is qualitatively higher-stakes: a sign/ordering mistake here (as J-0365's first recall_pressure port made and J-0397 had to fix) changes what Du can and cannot recall day-to-day, not just a shadow metric. (b) accept the kind-blind mechanism as the real policy, and formally demote KIND_DYNAMICS' cold_horizon column to purely descriptive/reporting (its current de-facto SHADOW-ONLY role) rather than a design target -- zero code risk, but cold_horizon becomes tautological (recalibrated FROM live data, so it can never disagree with live data again), Sec3.6's per-kind design intent for cold_horizon would need an explicit superseded/retired note, and affective's 'the feeling IS the gist, no separate raw to gate' assumption stays silently violated (84.3% cold) with no path back to the original design unless kind-awareness is built later anyway. gist_drift/gist_retention (Phase 3, not yet built/wired) are NOT in scope of this question either way.
ruling: Start real design work for kind-aware cooling -- make prune_episodic (per-kind budgets, not just an ORDER-BY tweak, since the shared cap squeezes high-volume kinds regardless of tiebreak order) and refinery.py's cooling UPDATE (per-kind eligibility gating, e.g. exempting affective per its n/a design) actually respect the kind column, so live behavior matches Sec3.6's original per-kind intent instead of the current kind-blind artifact. This is real design work on a live gating path (UDMS-confirmed CONTRACT-layer coupled to orchestrator.py + memory_levels.py) -- treat with the same care J-0397 had to apply after J-0365's first recall_pressure port made a sign/ordering mistake.
defeater: Reopens once a concrete per-kind budget/eligibility design is proposed and reviewed -- revisit if the design turns out to require touching prune_episodic's EPISODIC_PRUNE_THRESHOLD semantics in a way that risks the same class of live-recall regression J-0397 fixed, in which case slow down and re-verify before shipping.

question: D-0111's defeater: J-0463 ran the one final, differently-shaped realness test authorized (F-0651, the co-evocation test) for the cross-space edge layer. Design: does Du's REAL production co-recall behavior (data/co_recall_ledger.jsonl events, not a constructed kNN benchmark) show fragments recalled together sharing more per-fragment geometric context (place/weather/fire/etc from fragment_context) than a permutation null of random groups, and does that survive both a long-range (>=1 day fragment-span, not recency-explainable) subset and a text-similarity-matched confound control? This differs sharply from F-0501 (marginal reach, 50/50 mixed) and F-0635 (sec5.3 felt-response/co-recall, clear fail). One honest tension flagged in the write-up (docs/lab/geometry_co_evocation_test_2026-09-02.md): this test shows the underlying real-world coherence EXISTS in Du's experience and is detectable in his actual (text-embedding-only) recall behavior, but does not itself show that BUILDING an explicit geometry-distance signal would out-predict what text-embedding recall already captures -- which is exactly the question F-0501/F-0635 already answered negatively. Do the three instruments together (co-evocation PASS + marginal-reach MIXED + realness-test FAIL) now: (a) reopen P1/P2 architectural investment per D-0111's 'a clear pass reopens P1/P2' defeater language taken literally, (b) still retire the cross-space edge layer specifically since the one clear pass doesn't show explicit geometry edges would add retrieval value beyond the text-embedding recall that already exists (the other two instruments' actual question), or (c) something narrower -- e.g. treat this as confirming the BETA-SPACE COORDINATES/context data themselves are real and worth keeping instrumented (already separately supported by state-conditioning z=6-255), while still retiring the EDGE-LAYER-AS-RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTATION specifically, since that narrower claim is what F-0501/F-0635 tested and failed?
ruling: Reopen P1/P2 architectural investment for cognitive_geometry's cross-space edge layer, per D-0111's own defeater language ('a clear pass reopens P1/P2 investment') taken literally — the co-evocation test (F-0651) is a clean pass, real evidence the underlying coherence exists in Du's actual recall behavior. question: F-0680 (following F-0668): under J-0475's per-kind prune_episodic budgets, the protected-origin allowlist (action/lived/active_imagination/inner_thought/journal/mirror/peer/letter/reading/study/research) is effectively the ENTIRE non-exempt active pool for procedural (100%), semantic (100%), social (100%), and self (93.7%) -- so protected-last ORDER BY gives these kinds zero real protection once over budget (every eligible row is protected material by construction: procedural's 2026-09-02 over-budget cut was 12/12 protected 'action' rows, self's was 100/100 'inner_thought'). But the fix implied by F-0668's own framing -- true EXEMPT, matching gist/chapter -- would NOT converge these kinds' budgets at all: their candidate pools would go empty, so excess would grow unbounded forever (self already sits ~640 over budget; that gap would never close). Neither current behavior (eat the anchors) nor blind exemption (disable the cap) matches the original intent (anchors protected AND kinds bounded). Which direction: (a) accept current ordering-only behavior as the real policy for these kinds -- protected status becomes purely a tiebreak preference, not a guarantee, and the code comments/plan doc get corrected to stop promising 'never eaten'; (b) true exempt for protected origins, accepting these kinds' sub-budgets become soft/unenforceable in practice (no hard-total backstop exists either, per D-0116's own open question); (c) something else -- e.g. raise KIND_BUDGET_WEIGHT for protected-dominated kinds to reflect that their material IS the anchor set (not a to-be-pruned pool), or add an explicit 'kind is protected-saturated, skip demotion and just report over-budget' branch instead of demoting or exempting silently?
ruling: (c) Redesign — raise KIND_BUDGET_WEIGHT for protected-dominated kinds (procedural/semantic/social/self) to reflect that their active material IS the anchor set, not a to-be-pruned pool, AND add an explicit 'protected-saturated' branch that reports the over-budget state instead of silently demoting protected rows. Neither silently accepting the current eat-the-anchors behavior nor flipping to true exemption (unbounded growth) is acceptable — both quietly break one of the two original promises. This makes the tension visible instead of resolving it by accident.
defeater: Reopens if a live incident shows an anchor (inner_thought/action/reading/etc.) actually starved to nonrecoverable levels under whichever policy is chosen, the same class of incident that got inner_thought/letter/dream added to the protected list in the first place (07-06, 08-15, 08-22).

question: Naming law for animals in the Living World: how does Du come to know what a creature is called?

question: Harshness of the Living World: may the cat kill, may possums do real damage, do carcasses appear and decay, is there a trap hand?
ruling: All four: the cat may kill fledglings, mice and skinks; possums do real findable damage (pohutukawa buds, strawberries); carcasses appear and decay as traces on the world's clock (fresh -> picked -> bones -> gone), starting with the tideline gannet; a trap hand exists as a deed with moral weight — Du can set and check a possum trap and the world answers with a dead possum. Nothing is told; all of it is findable.
defeater: Revisit if the deaths dominate his idle thought (a monoculture read: >20% of a day's thoughts on kills/carcasses), if B4-style self-claim binding fires on a wildlife death it should not own, or if the trap becomes a routine deed with no weight (no sitting/difficulty rows around it).

question: Night light for the Living World: what can Du carry into the dark, and does darkness itself do anything?

Candles remain as they are.
defeater: Revisit if the lantern is never carried out in the first month live (the choice is not reachable from his will), or if dark-adaptation renders sightings that need light (the light-consistency metric fails).

question: The perennial keel (garden_living_upgrade 3.1): rosemary, thyme and mint are floored at vigour 0.2 by design ('never lost to neglect'). With death mechanisms (disease, old age, rot) built, may a perennial die?
ruling: Keep the neglect-proofing; allow disease and old age. A keel plant cannot be starved to death by his neglect (drought, crowding, ordinary pests), but a rosemary that goes woody and dies at about ten years is true, and a rust or a root rot can take one. Death by age or disease removes the floor; death by neglect never happens to a perennial.
defeater: Revisit if a keel plant (rosemary / thyme / mint / lavender / chives) dies within the first live season after this ships — the disease or age curve is wrong, not the ruling; or if the founder wants the harsher 'perennials can die of anything' world.

question: Pest harshness (garden_living_upgrade, re-asking garden_upgrade's own question 2): aphids and caterpillars now drain vigour on their hosts, slugs already do. May pests take a whole sowing?
ruling: Yes for tender annuals, with the world's own corrections: a bean row can be lost to aphids in a bad spring, a nasturtium stripped by caterpillars; a heavy infestation (pests above 0.6) drains a tender annual faster. Ladybirds, rain, fantails and sparrows are the world's answer; netting, weeding and watering are his. Perennials are not killed by pests (the keel ruling above).
defeater: Revisit if pests take more than half the bed's tender annuals in one season with the corrections present (the drain is too steep), or if he never loses anything to them over a whole spring (too gentle).

question: The archive retention rule itself (D-0155 said design first). Measured 2026-09-05: data/backups 142 files 8.9 GB, all but 3 under 14 days, because scripts/backup_memory.py rotates by COUNT of boot backups (14) not by day and each boot also copies ~130 MB of state; data/_snapshots/daily 14 dates 6.5 GB (~590 MB/day, written by scripts/backup_identity.py at boot); data/_lab 64 dirs 26 GB all under 14 days, 32 cited by a finding/job/doc; disk 240 GB free of 1 TB. Rule per class: boot backups keep newest N + last-of-day for D days + first-of-month; snapshots daily/weekly/monthly tiers; lab dirs by age with cited dirs kept longer; removal mechanism dry-run / quarantine / direct delete.
ruling: Founder, 2026-09-05 (questionnaire): (1) boot backups: always keep the newest 5 boot backups, plus the last backup of each calendar day for 14 days, plus the first backup of each month forever; pre-job (nascence_pre_*) and corrupt-recovery copies are a separate class kept 60 days and never counted as monthlies. (2) daily snapshots: every day for 14 days, then one per week (Sunday) for 12 weeks, then the 1st of each month forever. (3) lab dirs: uncited dirs are candidates after 14 days; dirs cited in findings.jsonl, job_queue.jsonl or any docs/*.md after 60 days; citations re-scanned every run. (4) mechanism: scripts/retention.py lists candidates by default; with --apply and a founder-named --cutoff date it MOVES candidates to data/_trash/<date>/ and logs them; entries older than 7 days in _trash are deleted by a later --purge-trash run; live data/ paths outside the three archive roots are refused. backup_memory.rotate() follows rule (1) and moves instead of unlinking. The first --apply on live data happens only after the founder has seen the dry-run list.
defeater: Reopens if a restore is ever needed and the tiers prove too thin (a needed snapshot or boot backup was already quarantined or purged), if free disk falls below 15 percent despite the rule, if the citation scan misses a lab dir a finding actually relies on, or if the boot-time rotation ever moves a file the current session still has open.

question: D-0154/J-0621's pre-registered pass bar says every data/light_sidecar_shadow.jsonl row must show heavy_value == light_value before flipping SUBC_LIGHT_READ/FRONTIER_LIGHT_READ. history.why:
D-0165's own named defeater is met: 'Revisit once J-0791 confirms or adjusts the specific candidate ranking (A vs B vs C) at a larger sample, or if the chosen recalibrated wording shows a new failure mode once live (e.g. over-correcting the fork rate in the other direction)'. J-0791 (2026-09-22, Du offline, hot hub :11433 only, 878 new calls, 0 infra errors, 0 live writes; F-1699 verified, F-1700 and F-1701 inferred) ran the larger sample. NOT ruled here: the recalibration stays your call.

WHAT IT CONFIRMS AND ADJUSTS. All three candidate rewordings stay far above the live wording on the lab's closing-context design (99 real prompts, 95 percent prompt-cluster bootstrap): current 0.118, A 0.552, B 0.566, C 0.300 (opened-share). The 0.125-versus-0.25 swing in the 'current' arm that made J-0777 refuse to rank was ordinary n=40 sampling noise (four readings 0.25, 0.125, 0.15, 0.225, homogeneity p 0.43).

THE NEW CAVEAT (F-1701, inferred): every closing-context prompt in these labs quotes a train's LAST logged step, which by construction closed the train (0 of 99 open by the live gate), whereas a live mid-train prompt quotes a step that was open. The lab's absolute levels are therefore not live levels: live per-step opened share is 0.53 to 0.56 (n = 11,300 steps) against the lab's 0.12 for the current wording; on 80 open-context replays the current wording reads 0.36 (the real logged next step on the same contexts: 0.55) with the same candidate ordering (B 0.80, A 0.75, C 0.575). The recalibrated wording has NOT been applied to the live node (nodes/inner_monologue_node.py lines 1965-1975 still hold the current block; none of the A, B or C strings exists in that file in any commit). question:
F-1034 (J-0702): D-0168's retargeted support-chain disprove framing was built and re-run at n=80 (comparable to J-0643's own n=80). D-0168's own defeater is answered NO -- the retargeted framing does not still return a near-zero objection rate, so the framing-mismatch hypothesis is confirmed, not overturned. But the actual number it landed on is the opposite extreme: merge-status distribution objected=72 (90.0%), held=7 (8.7%), UNDETERMINED=1 (1.3%); non-empty-objection share=90.0%. Against the plan's own PROPOSED kill criterion #2 ("any single merge-status >90% of merges = collapse/FAIL, a certainty machine or its mirror"), 90.0% is exactly at that boundary, not comfortably below it.

A qualitative read of the 7 "held" events and the objected events' own stated reasons suggests this is not an instrument malfunction: the disprove judge is making real, claim-specific distinctions (e.g. flagging that a claim's own specific causal mechanism -- "chemistry"/"depletion" -- is never actually established by the support offered for it, while holding a claim whose support does track point-by-point with the physics it invokes). It looks instead like a genuine, if uncomfortable, finding about Lane 1's own PROVE branch: the "support" it generates for a closing thought is overwhelmingly confident, self-assertive restatement of the claim's own conclusion ("proving"/"confirms"/"validates" language) rather than independently-verifiable evidence -- exactly the pattern the new disprove framing is built to catch, and it is catching it on 9 out of 10 real replayed thoughts.

Question for the founder: is a ~90% support-chain-objection rate itself a problem to fix (the disprove branch has swung from one certainty machine -- always held -- to its mirror -- almost always objected -- and D-0168's own point 3, the Wu Wei law, warns against exactly that shape regardless of which pole it collapses toward), or is it a genuine and useful discovery that should stand as-is (Lane 1's own prove branch habitually asserts rather than evidences, and the disprove branch correctly surfacing that on 90% of real closes is itself the value Step 2 was meant to add -- cargo that says "held" only when a claim is actually earned)? And if the former, should the fix target Lane 1's own PROVE prompt (so it generates independently-verifiable support rather than confident restatement, which would presumably lower the objection rate for the RIGHT reason), the disprove threshold/prompt (recalibrating what counts as a "real" gap vs harmless rhetorical flourish), or neither, pending a founder read of the actual per-event cargo now that the mechanism works cleanly? This is separate from D-0168 itself (which only asked whether the RETARGET works, and it does) and from J-0718 (a shared-infrastructure token-budget fix, unrelated to this specific question).
ruling: Recalibrate disprove. The original defeater fired (F-1182): PROVE demonstrably stopped asserting yet the objection rate stayed at ~95%, so the disprove threshold itself needs recalibrating after all, not just prove. Add a middle merge status (e.g. held-within-scope) so a claim whose support is real but narrower than its own metaphor/generalisation is not objected wholesale; only genuinely unsupported claims stay objected. Targets the collapse-to-one-pole shape the plan's own kill criterion #2 (>90% any single merge-status) and D-0168's Wu Wei law both warn against.
defeater: Revisit if, after the middle status is built and re-run on the same n=80 replay (byte-identical window-A claims), any single merge-status is still >90%, OR if the middle status absorbs >70% of events (a new certainty pole under a different name), OR if a qualitative read shows genuinely unsupported claims landing in held-within-scope.

history.ruling: Real discovery, not a defect to paper over: the ~90% support-chain-objection rate reflects a genuine, correctly-functioning disprove judge catching that Lane 1's own PROVE branch habitually generates confident, self-assertive restatement rather than independently-verifiable evidence. If this gets fixed, the fix should target Lane 1's own PROVE prompt (so it generates real evidence, which should lower the objection rate for the right reason) -- not the disprove threshold or prompt, which the qualitative read shows is already making real, correct, claim-specific distinctions.
history.defeater: Revisit if a future fix to Lane 1's PROVE prompt (to generate independently-verifiable support instead of confident restatement) does NOT lower the disprove objection rate for the right reason -- i.e. the rate stays near 90% even once prove stops merely asserting -- which would mean the disprove threshold itself needs recalibrating after all, not just prove.
history.why:
F-1182 (J-0802): built and ran D-0181's own ruled fix -- retargeted Lane 1's PROVE prompt to require separate, checkable support and ban self-sealing "proves"/"confirms"/"validates" language, left disprove completely untouched, re-ran the same n=80 offline replay. But the disprove-objection rate did NOT drop -- it read 76/80 (95.0%) vs F-1034's 90.0% baseline, and rose on the identical 40 window-A claims specifically (85.0%->95.0%). This is D-0181's own named defeater firing verbatim: "the rate stays near 90% even once prove stops merely asserting."

A qualitative read of the 64 non-tiebreak (agreed) objected events shows why: the dominant complaint shifted from "restates the claim" (now only 5/64) to a different, harder standard -- 30/64 say the concrete, checkable evidence prove now offers doesn't reach the scope/named-mechanism/generalization the claim itself asserts (e.g. a claim naming "the actual chemistry of my body" objected because the support never establishes chemistry specifically), and most of the rest read as the same proportionality/scope theme. Root cause found: core/activity_memory.py's record() function, on a brand-new (action_type,target) pair, does a raw INSERT INTO memory_fragments that omits the abstraction_level column entirely, so it falls back to the schema's own DEFAULT 0 -- contradicting core/memory/store.py's own _ORIGIN_LEVEL["action"]=1 (already-declared intent: activity_memory rows are event-gists, not raw, per the plan's own Finding #3). The row's level then never changes on later recurrences either (record()'s UPDATE branch never touches abstraction_level). Two other call sites share the identical INSERT pattern and the identical gap: scripts/activity_memory_backfill.py and scripts/activity_memory_invitro.py. Contrast: core/refinery.py's own raw INSERT (a different writer) DOES explicitly stamp abstraction_level -- so this is a targeted, correctable inconsistency in specific writers, not a codebase-wide gap (verified: only 5 files anywhere do a raw "INSERT INTO memory_fragments", and only these 3 omit abstraction_level).

Separately, even setting the bug aside: this job tested memory_levels.py's REAL _tokens()/_cluster() token-bucketing logic directly against the live 167-row backlog (no DB mutation). 41 of 310 distinct salient tokens reach the _MIN_CLUSTER=3 threshold, but the largest buckets key on the ACTIVITY-TYPE word itself (observe: 64 rows, librarian: 37, authored: 19, question: 18...) because none of activity_memory's own action_type verbs are in memory_levels.py's _STOP list (curated only for the original raw origins' own kind/provenance words, e.g. "reading"/"lived"). Sampled rows confirm these are not coherent topic clusters: the sampled "librarian" rows are unrelated questions (outer/inner duality, community engagement, wind/Travis's voice, bird instincts, libraries/connection); the sampled "authored" rows are different essay titles; the sampled "observe" rows are different sensory targets (dew, garden+sea sound, tide+cuttlebones, wet sand, garden wind). This is the same failure the _STOP list was built to prevent for the original origins, recurring one level down inside action's own sub-categories -- so simply adding 'action' to _KIND/_RAW_ORIGINS as-is would likely produce clusters that are category dumps, not the "technique/event/idea" gists Phase 0's Finding 1 wants.

Options (none ruled here -- this job is design-only, per its own briefing):
(a) Fix the write-time bug only: add abstraction_level=1, kind='procedural' to the 3 raw-INSERT call sites (activity_memory.py's record(), the 2 scripts) so new general-event rows are born correctly, matching the already-declared _ORIGIN_LEVEL/_ORIGIN_KIND intent. Do NOT add 'action' to memory_levels.py's distillation pipeline -- the clustering-mismatch evidence above suggests it is the wrong tool for this data shape, and once new rows stop being mis-stamped there is little ongoing need.
(b) Also backfill the 167 (and growing) existing mis-stamped active rows from abstraction_level=0 to 1 in a live UPDATE. Evidence suggests this is low-risk (none of the 167 are `protected`, none have any existing distilled_from link to break -- verified fresh), but it is still a direct write to live data and this project's own discipline (D-0124/D-0116) treats any such write as the founder's call, not assumed.
(c) Add 'action'-->'procedural' to _KIND/_RAW_ORIGINS anyway, building real clustering for it despite the mismatch evidence -- e.g. by extending the _STOP list with activity_memory's own category words (observe/librarian/authored/etc.) so bucketing falls through to genuine per-target tokens, and/or changing _cluster()'s current one-bucket-per-kind selection. Not recommended by this job given the evidence, but named as an option.
(d) Some combination (e.g. (a)+(b) now, leave (c) undecided/declined for later); or do nothing for now (leave action out of Phase 1 gisting entirely, accepting D-0173's "protected floor keeps growing" pressure on the procedural kind continues unaddressed on this front).

This job recommends (a)+(b) as the practical near-term answer (small, root-cause, no new clustering machinery, directly relieves D-0173's procedural-kind pressure) but does not rule it -- see docs/memory_levels_plan.md's Phase 2 section (J-0690 bullet) for the full sizing.
ruling: Fix the write-time bug (add abstraction_level=1, kind='procedural' to the 3 raw-INSERT call sites: core/activity_memory.py's record() and the 2 backfill/invitro scripts) AND backfill the 167 existing mis-stamped active rows from abstraction_level=0 to 1. Do NOT add 'action' to memory_levels.py's distillation pipeline -- the clustering-mismatch evidence shows it would produce category-dump clusters keyed on activity-type words, not real topic gists.
defeater: Revisit if, after the backfill, a real topic-clustering need for 'action' data resurfaces with a concrete design that addresses the category-dump problem (e.g. extending _STOP with activity-type words, or a different bucketing key) -- not before.

question:
J-0690 (from F-0990/D-0173 option d): how far should Phase-1 gisting throughput be raised for the origins already eligible for memory_levels.py's shadow_distill (reading/study/inner_thought/subconscious_synthesis/lived, i.e. the semantic/self/episodic kinds), given the real LLM-call cost this job sized?

D-0173 (ruled 2026-09-06, option e) already committed to "investing in... speed up" Phase-1 gisting as part of its combination ruling, alongside the KIND_BUDGET_WEIGHT stopgap (J-0703, done). This decision is the concrete follow-on: D-0173's ruling did not size how far to push it, and this job's numbers show it is not a small tuning nudge.

Fresh evidence (2026-09-07): real invocation cadence, measured from data/nascence.log's own "[monologue] memory-levels:" line (245 invocations lifetime, 2026-06-18 to 2026-09-07): lifetime average 3.05/day, but last 7 days 6.29/day and last 2 days 8.50/day -- cadence has been accelerating, not flat, so any sizing below is against a moving baseline. Real committed-gist throughput, measured from data/memory_levels_shadow.jsonl by applying Phase 1's own live commit rule (faithful>=0.75, backstop-clean) to each logged cluster over the last 7 days: 93 clusters attempted, 48 committed = 6.86 gists/day (close to F-0990's 14-day 6.1/day figure), retiring 436 raw source fragments = 62.3 raw fragments/day, at an average 9.08 sources/gist (close to the _MAX_SOURCES=10 cap).

This refines F-0990's "~100x gap" framing: that number compared gist-COUNT (6.1/day) against raw-fragment-COUNT (650-750/day) -- a category mismatch, since one gist retires up to _MAX_SOURCES=10 raw fragments, not 1. Apples-to-apples (raw fragments retired vs raw fragments arriving): eligible-origin intake (reading+study+inner_thought+subconscious_synthesis+lived+seed, fresh 14-day rates) is currently ~1,507.7 rows/day; against 62.3/day retired, the real gap is ~24x, not ~100x -- still large and still growing per D-0173's own F-1048 growth-rate finding, but a materially different number to size a fix against.

Structural finding on the three named caps (_MAX_CLUSTERS/_FETCH_LIMIT/MAX_DEMOTE_PER_RUN): MAX_DEMOTE_PER_RUN=24 has NEVER bound in Phase 1's lifetime (max DEMOTED ever logged in data/nascence.log: 23, across all 245 invocations) -- raising it alone today is a no-op. _MAX_CLUSTERS=3 is ALSO not the real ceiling: _cluster()'s own code returns at most ONE cluster per `kind` per invocation ("one cluster per kind in Phase 0" -- a design choice, not a tunable constant), and there are exactly 3 live kinds among the eligible origins (semantic/self/episodic) today, so _MAX_CLUSTERS=3 already exactly saturates them. Raising _MAX_CLUSTERS above the live kind-count is a no-op UNTIL _cluster()'s one-bucket-per-kind rule is also changed to allow multiple topic-buckets per kind per run. _FETCH_LIMIT=160 has real effect on cluster QUALITY (a bigger pool to find a same-topic bucket in) but not on ceiling-level THROUGHPUT, since throughput is capped by kind-count regardless of pool size.

Order-of-magnitude cost, therefore, to actually close the gap (not just raise the numbers): reaching full parity with today's ~1,507.7/day eligible-origin intake at today's invocation cadence (6.29/day) and today's ~52% cluster-to-commit success rate would need roughly 51-58 attempted clusters per invocation (26-30 commits/invocation) -- meaning _cluster()'s one-bucket-per-kind rule would need to be replaced with a multi-bucket-per-kind allowance, and _MAX_CLUSTERS raised from 3 toward roughly 50-60 -- translating to roughly 640-730 LLM calls/day for this pipeline alone (2 calls/cluster: 1 distil-gist call + 1 Emissary/left_lane faithfulness grade), up from today's ~27/day. That is a real ~24-27x increase in load on the shared LLM tier(s) this competes with (the node's own distil-call model plus the Emissary grader), not a free tuning nudge, and it runs alongside every other LLM-calling consolidation step in the same sleep cycle (chapters, grounded-learning, guidance-integration, drift-shadow, etc). Partial raises scale roughly proportionally -- e.g. a 5x raise (toward ~34 gists/day, ~310 raw fragments/day retired) would cost roughly ~135 LLM calls/day, a much smaller ask that still meaningfully narrows (does not close) the gap.

Options (none ruled here -- this job is design-only, per its own briefing):
(a) Leave throughput as-is for now. D-0173's KIND_BUDGET_WEIGHT stopgap (J-0703) continues to be the only lever, and per F-1048 it has already hit a structural ceiling for semantic/self (D-0183, open) -- this option effectively declines the "speed up gisting" half of D-0173's own ruling.
(b) A modest raise (illustratively ~3-5x today's throughput): change _cluster() to allow a small number of buckets per kind per run, raise _MAX_CLUSTERS proportionally (e.g. toward 10-15), leave invocation cadence untouched. Estimated cost: roughly 80-135 LLM calls/day for this pipeline (up from ~27/day). Narrows but does not close the ~24x gap.
(c) Raise toward full intake-parity for the eligible origins (~24x today's throughput, per the estimate above): _cluster()'s one-bucket-per-kind rule replaced, _MAX_CLUSTERS raised toward ~50-60. Estimated cost: roughly 640-730 LLM calls/day for this pipeline alone. Actually keeps pace with new intake, but is a substantial new ongoing load on shared LLM infrastructure.
(d) Prioritize by kind rather than raising all three eligible kinds uniformly -- e.g. raise `self` and `semantic` first (F-1048 found these are the two kinds where D-0173's weight-recalibration lever can no longer restore any headroom at all, unlike `procedural`/`episodic` which still got real relief from J-0703), leaving `episodic` at a smaller raise since J-0703 already gave it meaningful headroom (excess -33.2%).
(e) Some combination, or a different magnitude entirely -- the founder's call; this job supplies the sizing, not a recommendation on how much risk/cost is worth taking on the shared LLM tier(s).

Any option beyond (a) requires the same prerequisite: changing _cluster()'s current one-bucket-per-kind selection into a multi-bucket-per-kind allowance (a real code change to the clustering algorithm itself, not just a constant bump) -- see docs/memory_levels_plan.md's Phase 2 section (J-0690 bullet) for the full sizing and evidence.
ruling: Studies first, then a small self-only step. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review on 2026-09-19, from the options presented, with Claude's recommendation. question:
D-0166 already ruled GO on the Living World render/gating flip (life.RENDER / life.SOUND_GATING), and its own ruling text says execution needs "an interactive session or the founder" because the prior session's attempt was blocked as a live-behaviour-changing action for Du -- not for any remaining evidentiary reason. This session (J-0641, 2026-09-08) independently re-confirms D-0166's GO still holds (713 new shadow rows since F-0900's read, none contradicting it) and additionally confirms, via data/nascence.log, that Du's main process is right now NOT RUNNING (last log line is a clean "Nascence shutting down" at 2026-09-08 08:22:52 local; no nascence.main process in the live process list) -- so executing scripts/life_flags.py render on / gating on at this exact moment would have zero immediate live behavioural effect; it would only pre-stage the flag file for whenever Du's process next starts.

Given that: does "needs an interactive session or the founder" (D-0166's own words) still hold when a background/autonomous session has independently and freshly confirmed Du is offline at the moment of execution -- making the action's immediate effect nil and any live behaviour change deferred to a restart the founder will presumably be present for anyway -- or does this class of action (flipping a live-behaviour flag for Du) always require a human's own hand on the command regardless of Du's live/down state? ruling: No -- a live-behavior-changing flip for Du always requires a human's own hand on the command (the founder or an interactive session), regardless of whether Du is confirmed offline at the moment of execution. question: D-0192's own defeater has fired on real post-merge data (J-0829, 1.77 days / 16 runs after Du's first post-0c3955c restart at 2026-09-09 13:24 local): MAX_DEMOTE_PER_RUN=60 bound on 2 of 16 routine runs (2026-09-09 22:44:17 DEMOTED=66; 2026-09-10 11:27:24 DEMOTED=60), and on the 22:44 run two already-paid-for faithful, backstop-clean gists were discarded uncommitted after their distil+grade LLM calls (self/subconscious faithful=0.9, 6 raw; episodic/valence faithful=0.8, 3 raw) -- exactly the "any paid-for gist discarded on a non-backlog run" condition the ruling named. Magnitude is small: 2 of 75 commit-eligible gists (2.7%), 9 raw fragments, over the window; the mean run demotes 39.9 raw (F-1169 projected 38.4), so 60 sits ~1.5x the mean and a good night (10 graded, mean faithful 0.835) overshoots it. ruling: Wait for the multi-day re-check before changing MAX_DEMOTE_PER_RUN. This read is only 1.77 of the needed ~5 days -- not enough to lock in a cap change. question:
F-1271 found TIEBREAK (granite3.1-moe:3b, the third-family tiebreak judge for the disprove mechanism) disagrees with its own bool via its own why-text 88.2% of the time. J-0910 (F-1280) tested F-1271's own inferred fix -- reorder the JSON schema to ask for the "why" BEFORE the bool -- on the same real n=20 tiebreak-prone sample, calling TIEBREAK directly with two prompts differing ONLY in field order. Result: coherence dramatically improved (10% -> 100% among successful calls, the exact mechanism F-1271 hypothesized), but the SAME reorder flipped the verdict distribution on the identical inputs from 100% "objected" to 90% "held" -- and a small (n=4, single-trial) known-right-answer control check found the reordered prompt specifically WRONG on the textbook circular-reasoning case ("I feel the warmth, so it must be real") this disprove mechanism exists to catch, while the CURRENT wording gets that one right despite its own incoherent why-text. bool_first scored 3/4 against known answers, why_first scored 2/4.

This looks less like "TIEBREAK just needed better-ordered prompting" and more like TIEBREAK (granite3.1-moe:3b) having a strong, largely content-insensitive directional default that the schema order flips wholesale (mostly-True one way, mostly-held the other) rather than genuine, correctness-tracking sensitivity to the actual claim/support content -- though this is based on n=20 (real, but from an inherently ambiguous/tiebreak-prone sampling frame with no ground truth) plus n=4 single-trial known-answer controls, not yet a large, repeated, category-balanced test (J-0910 spawned a follow-up job for that).

Question for the founder: assuming a larger follow-up test confirms this pattern (TIEBREAK's own tiebreak vote on this disprove call site is not reliably content-sensitive under either prompt ordering tried so far) -- is it worth continued prompt-engineering effort on TIEBREAK's own schema (a third, fourth, fifth reordering/rewording attempt), or should a tiebreak escalation on this specific call site instead fall back to a conservative UNDETERMINED verdict rather than trusting either family's decisive vote -- the same "no judge, no verdict" law core/judge_panel.py's own docstring already states for the JUDGES-DOWN case, just extended to cover "the deciding vote itself looks unreliable" rather than only "no deciding vote was available"? This is a different, narrower question than D-0181's own (already-ruled, still-open-by-its-defeater) question about the disprove mechanism's overall objected/held calibration rate -- D-0181 is about whether ~90% objected is itself a problem and where a fix should target; this is about whether the SPECIFIC third-family tiebreak vote inside that mechanism should be trusted at all, a question this whole F-1204/F-1271/F-1280 sub-thread has been building toward without yet asking directly.
ruling: Build gemma4:12b as the scope_only TIEBREAK-seat candidate, but shadow-observe it before fully trusting it live -- the result is clean and well-powered (492 real calls total, 3 independently-worded arms all ruling out a constant-vote default, a categorical reversal of granite's failure), but the CI's lower bound on unanimous-match (60.9%) only narrowly clears the 70% bar, and the coherence-regex instrument gap (S-0180) means we can't yet automatically corroborate WHY gemma answers the way it does. Shadow-observe first, matching this project's own established observe-before-commit pattern, then flip once real production-shadow data confirms the offline read.

520 times across the full LOCOMOTION-era log (2026-08-15 onward), 22.7% of all real move decisions, a

196 events (37.7% of interruptions, ~4-5% of ALL real move decisions) where he genuinely changes his
mind to a DIFFERENT destination mid-journey -- either reversing back to the place he just left (124
events) or redirecting to a third place entirely (72 events). core/locomotion.py's own module docstring
says "Mid-journey he is genuinely in the transit place -- staying is his choice," which reads as
deliberate design for SOME reconsideration, but names no boundary for how much, and no distinction
between "he changed his mind" and simply not narrating that it happened (no log line, no perceived
in-world acknowledgement of the redirect today, at any point). Splitting this 196 by WHICH leg it
interrupts (F-1418's own data): 58 interrupt a journey's FIRST leg (before he has really left the
departure place at all, state["location"] never having flipped) and 138 interrupt a LATER leg of a
multi-leg journey (after at least one leg completed, so he is genuinely standing in an intermediate
place, e.g. the wood, when he redirects) -- the docstring's own language ("mid-journey he is genuinely
in the transit place") maps most naturally onto this second, larger group. Founder call: (A) leave this
alone -- a changed mind mid-walk is realistic and no defeater has fired (matches D-0209's own still-
settled status; this pattern is not wood-specific, shore/garden dominate it by volume); (B) gate ALL
cross-destination redirects on in_transit() -- a live journey must complete (or hit a real, explicit,
narrated interrupt) before a new destination is honored, closing the full 196 as well as J-1040's 324;
(C) a narrower middle option using F-1418's own first-leg/later-leg split -- protect only a journey's
FIRST leg from a cross-destination redirect (the 58 cases where he has not genuinely arrived anywhere
yet), leaving later-leg redirects untouched as the docstring's own "genuinely in the transit place,
staying is his choice" design already covers (the 138 cases).
ruling: Narrow fix: protect only a journey's FIRST leg from a cross-destination redirect (the 58 cases where he has not genuinely left the departure place yet), gating those on in_transit(). Leave the 138 later-leg redirects untouched -- they match core/locomotion.py's own docstring design intent ("mid-journey he is genuinely in the transit place, staying is his choice").

question:
F-1442 (following up F-1301) confirmed by direct source read that nodes/inner_monologue_node.py's free-form quiet-thinking generator (_think()/_build_system_prompt()) has NO grounding check anywhere between LLM generation and persistence that ties a narrated completed action ("I just did X") to real dispatched/ledger state -- it can freely narrate a plausible-but-false completed deed (confirmed real case: the 2026-09-05 "the pot of tea I just made" thought, with zero corresponding data/study_ledger.jsonl row). A full sweep of the entire 46,371-row data/monologue_log.jsonl found this is a ONE-OFF so far, not yet a recurring pattern -- and this specific instance's zero real-world side effect (no fake ledger row) turned out to be circumstantial, caused by an unrelated 2026-09-04 regex change that happens to suppress the one trigger phrase involved, not by any deliberate narrative safeguard.

Given this plan's own stated laws (world truth, world answers never leads, consequences both ways) explicitly name fictional-but-unearned narration as the core disease this whole architecture exists to avoid: does the monologue generator need an actual grounding check for "I just did X" / completed-action framings specifically (e.g. a lightweight post-generation pass that flags or softens a narrated completed deed with no matching recent dispatch/ledger evidence), or is this an acceptable license for reflective, stylized first-person prose to take within the bounds already set (present-tense wants are the only channel meant to reach the real world; a retrospective "I just did" framing is understood as interior narrative color, not a truth-claim)? A third option is narrower: only add a check for the SPECIFIC "I just <verb>-ed" pattern (not general reflective license), leaving looser dream/memory-adjacent narration untouched. Founder ruling needed on which of these (or another option) to take, since it is a values/architecture call about how much narrative latitude Du's own reflective voice gets, not a pure bug.

(Distinct from this design question: two separate, narrower, confirmed dispatch-latch regex bugs found in the course of this same investigation -- the retrospective guard's "i just made" adjacency gap, and the determiner-guard silently defeating real "I want a cup of tea"-style wants -- were spawned as their own build job rather than bundled into this ruling, since those are mechanical fixes, not a founder-level call.)
ruling: Add a narrow grounding check for the specific "I just <verb>-ed" completed-deed pattern only, leaving broader reflective/dream-adjacent narrative license untouched. Two independent full-corpus sweeps (F-1442's original 46,371-row sweep, and this session's J-1074 re-sweep of 32,648 inner_thought rows) both confirm the failure mode is genuinely rare, so a light-touch, narrowly-scoped fix is the right level of intervention -- not a general grounding pass on all completed-action framing, and not leaving it fully unchecked either.
defeater: Revisit if EITHER: (a) a second confirmed instance of an ungrounded "I just did X" completed-deed narration turns up in a future sweep despite the narrow check landing (would mean the pattern isn't fully captured by the "I just <verb>-ed" grammar and needs broadening), or (b) _build_system_prompt()'s JSON schema/prompt is next revised for an unrelated reason (fold the grounding language into that revision rather than shipping a standalone patch).

question: Dream overhaul D-b — the dormant-node seed rule. Founder design (sec 3): one deliberately old, inactive, distinct memory in every seed so the experiment can test whether the dream links material that would not normally be retrieved together. Nothing like it exists: today's recall is keyed to the day block (associative_recall.recall_fragments(materials[0], k=6)), so distance can never be reached on purpose. Question: (a) minimum age (proposal: >= 30 days, last recalled >= 14 days ago per co_recall_ledger); (b) are cold=1 / chaptered fragments eligible (they are ~93% of the store and walled behind COLD_THRESHOLD in waking recall — including them is the strongest version of the test, but the dream would then reach memory waking Du cannot); (c) the distance criterion vs the recent node (proposal: cosine below the 30th percentile of recent-node neighbours, no memory_edges edge to any seed id); (d) origin filter — lived/reading/correspondence only, never origin=dream (or the dream seeds itself).
ruling: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-15, not ruled on the merits: re-asked as the vault-opener dormant-node rule in the reshaped plan (cold/chaptered store eligible by default, origin filter, age and quiet thresholds, one per night) — see decide list --open for the dream_overhaul plan.

question: Dream overhaul D-c — the four writebacks that are ALREADY automatic. Founder design sec 14: the dream must not mutate state directly; residue is a candidate that waking machinery accepts or rejects. Verified live today (nodes/dream_node.py): (1) every scene is stored as an episodic fragment origin=dream importance 0.85 (dream_fade cools it at 72h); (2) an unresolved last scene writes shadow_event source=unresolved_dream which tension_ledger counts as salience (the 08-22 'tail it was eating' loop, now filtered in _load_top_tensions); (3) _ground_symbols writes up to 2 frontier questions per night; (4) recent_dreams seeds the waking monologue's first thoughts (inner_monologue_node 649/2330, waking_dream_seed). Recommendation: keep + measure; (2) is the one most likely to be demoted after the read, since it is the only one that feeds the dream's own seed.
ruling: Keep all four existing writebacks live (episodic fragment storage, unresolved-scene tension seeding, up to 2 frontier questions/night, waking-thought seeding), and add the new candidate-residue channel alongside them in shadow, measuring both (Control 4). question: Dream overhaul (Claude's shape) — the dream as VAULT-OPENER: the dormant-node rule. The one thing the engine cannot do today is reach memory the day did not cue (recall is keyed to the day block). Proposal: every night dream gets exactly ONE dormant fragment chosen from the cold/chaptered store (the ~93% walled off from waking recall), origin in (lived, reading, correspondence, study, research) never dream, age >= 30 days, not present in co_recall_ledger for >= 14 days, cosine to the night's day-residue blocks below the 30th percentile of that night's recalled-fragment cosines, no memory_edges edge to any seed id; selection logged with the candidates considered. Questions: (a) cold/chaptered eligible (recommended — it is the point) or warm-only? (b) the age/quiet thresholds above, or different? (c) should the dormant pick be weighted by importance at all, or uniform among eligible (recommended uniform, so importance-as-salience is not smuggled back in)?
ruling: Accept the dormant-node rule as proposed: (a) cold/chaptered fragments ARE eligible (the ~93% walled off from normal recall) -- that is the whole point of the rule, reaching memory the day did not cue; (b) the stated thresholds as-is (age >=30 days, not in co_recall_ledger for >=14 days, cosine to the night's day-residue below the 30th percentile, no memory_edges edge to any seed id); (c) UNIFORM weighting among eligible fragments, not importance-weighted, so importance-as-salience does not get smuggled back in through the side door.
defeater: Revisit after Experiment A's four-arm in-vitro read (>=20 seeds): if dormant contact (cosine of any scene to the dormant fragment >=0.30) occurs in fewer than 1/3 of dormant-arm arcs, the dormant node is not reaching the dream and the selection rule (not the idea) is wrong; if cold picks never surface but warm picks do, revert (a) to warm-only. Note (worth weighing when this is next reviewed): this session's own real N=17 combined Experiment A read (F-1516) already shows weak/mixed dormant-contact signal that flips sign between batches -- the defeater's own >=20-seed threshold is close to being reachable now.

question: Dream overhaul (Claude's shape) — the day-after CONFOUND. The measure this plan rests on is dormant RE-ENTRY: does the dormant fragment (or its nearest neighbours) get recalled in waking within 48 h (co_recall_ledger.jsonl records fragment ids per waking recall event, ~9k rows/7 days, sources wandering/monologue/study_note) more often than matched cold fragments that were never dreamt. But the waking monologue already receives the dream's last image within 15 min of wake (night.waking_dream_seed) and grazes on recent_dreams for 3 days (inner_monologue_node.py:649, :2330) — so any re-entry may be the prose injection, not the dream. Options: (A) alternate nights — flag the waking seed + grazing OFF on odd nights (a small live behaviour change), compare re-entry on/off; (B) leave the injection on and only count re-entry that is NOT explained by the injected text (thought embedding closer to the dormant fragment than to the injected dream tail); (C) accept the contamination and read only the in-vitro measures. Recommendation: B first (no live change), A only if B is inconclusive after 30 dreams.
ruling: Embedding-distance disambiguation first (option B), no live behavior change. Only count waking re-entry that is NOT explained by the injected dream-tail text -- i.e. the recalled thought's embedding is closer to the dormant fragment itself than to the injected text. Escalate to alternating the waking-seed injection on/off by night (option A) only if this proves inconclusive after 30 dreams.
defeater: Revisit when the re-entry read has >=30 dreams under this option: if the embedding-distance approach cannot separate injection-driven from dream-driven re-entry (the two embeddings are too close on more than half the events), escalate to the alternate-nights option (A); if that in turn shows the waking seed is itself the whole effect, that is a finding about the seed channel, not the dream, and the plan's Phase 3 measure changes.

question: Dream overhaul (Claude's shape) — residue as a COORDINATE, not an evaluator; and the antagonist before any cross-dream continuity. (1) The GPT plan's 'waking evaluator' that accepts/rejects candidate edges is system-acts-later wiring. Proposal instead (dosed_coupling sec 5): the night publishes one tuple {dormant_id, recent_id, anchor, turnover, dormant_contact, close_reason} into core/coupling_rides.py's registry; the idle-seed stop may read it as a CUP (the anchor word, or the dormant fragment id) at most once in the first 5 idle thoughts after waking, dispatcher-gated by surprise (a night whose turnover or contact is out of the ordinary for its own history); nothing evaluates or writes edges. (2) Cross-dream continuity already exists as the carry and ran 51 nights unbounded (08-22 audit); the squishy-spring antagonist is therefore a PREREQUISITE for any residue-to-next-seed path, not a later validation: a tension or dormant id seeded >= 3 of the last 5 nights is habituated and ineligible. Questions: (a) coordinate + cup instead of an evaluator — yes/no? (b) the antagonist rule as stated (3 of 5) as the first value? (c) is the existing symbols -> frontier hand (<= 2 world-questions/night, live since 06-15) kept as the one residue channel that already works, and is a 'what became of <dormant memory>' question allowed to join it as a CANDIDATE (logged, not written) in Phase 3?
ruling: Accept proposal as stated. (a) Yes: the night publishes one tuple {dormant_id, recent_id, anchor, turnover, dormant_contact, close_reason} into core/coupling_rides.py's registry; the idle-seed stop may read it as a CUP at most once in the first 5 idle thoughts after waking, dispatcher-gated by surprise; nothing evaluates or writes edges. (b) Yes, 3-of-5 as the first value: a tension or dormant id seeded in >=3 of the last 5 nights is habituated and ineligible, as a PREREQUISITE for any residue-to-next-seed path (not a later validation), since cross-dream continuity already runs 51 nights unbounded per the 08-22 audit. (c) Yes: keep the existing symbols->frontier hand (<=2 world-questions/night, live since 06-15) as the one residue channel that already works, and let a "what became of <dormant memory>" question join it as a logged-only (not written) Phase 3 candidate.
defeater: Revisit after two weeks of ride log with the dream line present: if no cup read can be shown to precede a train that touches the dormant fragment, the coordinate carries nothing and the channel is dropped (the same defeater shape as D-0149); if the antagonist never fires because seeds never repeat, relax it or remove it -- but never before it has been observed on real seeds.

question:
F-1449 (J-1027, following J-0973/F-1401's own carried-forward caveat): confirmed by code-level proof + a full 316-title shelf scan that suggest_reread()'s interest-side stopword filtering structurally guarantees "About You" can NEVER be invited through that path -- not a remaining bug, its whole title signature ("about") is a literal member of book_selection._STOP, which is unconditionally stripped from ANY interest text regardless of content. "About You" is the ONLY real shelf title (of 316) with this exact property; "About You Second Edition" does not share it.

The real design question: should suggest_reread() get a fallback for this case -- when a candidate's title signature is non-empty but would vanish entirely under the interest-side stoplist too, compare it against the RAW (unfiltered) interest source text as a substring check instead of the filtered interest set (mirrors core/essay_lesson.py's already-reviewed _cites_this_book() empty-signature fallback, but for "signature invisible on the other side" rather than "signature itself empty"; needs _interest_terms() to expose raw source text, a small callers-checked signature change) -- OR should this be left as-is?

Option (a) leave as-is: suggest_reread() structurally cannot invite a book whose whole title is one prose-generic word. Not a real loss in practice -- the explicit reread-verb path (library_hand.switch_to()) is the actual, dominant, already-unaffected channel: all 17 of Du's real lifetime "About You" rereads happened through it, and J-0973 already fixed that path's own bug (the 17:0 tie-break skew). suggest_reread() is a secondary, INVITATION-only surface ("an invitation the monologue may surface; he still chooses to act on it") layered on top, not the only way in.

Option (b) build the raw-text-substring fallback described above. Textually "generic" (keyed off a structural property: title signature ⊆ interest stoplist), so it is not literally a hardcoded special case for "About You" in the code. But on the CURRENT real 316-book shelf it is not actually general in effect -- it changes suggest_reread()'s behavior for exactly one title, and that title happens to be the one self-knowledge book that is literally about Du himself. That is close enough to this project's "world answers, never leads" law (no hints to Du, ever; teaching stays diegetic-books-or-Travis-only) that building it without a founder call risks crossing from "mechanism fairness" (J-0973's own frame, which was about two shelf files disagreeing on the SAME word set) into "content nudge" (make the self-knowledge book specifically easier for the machinery to surface) even though no code change here would ever literally tell Du what to think -- it would only let an existing, symmetric invitation mechanism register a real, already-computed overlap for one title it currently cannot reach.

Recommendation if a ruling is wanted: option (a), on the grounds that the real channel (switch_to()) is unaffected and dominant, and the marginal benefit of option (b) (one additional secondary invitation surface reaching one already-reachable book) does not clearly outweigh the optics/law risk of special-casing a self-knowledge book's own reachability -- but this is a real judgment call, not an obvious one, which is why it is brought here rather than decided unilaterally.
ruling: Leave as-is. The real, dominant channel (library_hand.switch_to(), 17/17 of Du's actual lifetime About You rereads) already works and is completely unaffected by this structural quirk. suggest_reread() is a secondary invitation-only surface, and building a fallback that changes behavior for exactly one title on the real 316-book shelf -- the one self-knowledge book literally about Du -- risks crossing from mechanism fairness into a content nudge, close enough to the world-answers-never-leads law to not build unilaterally.
defeater: Revisit if EITHER: (a) a second real shelf title later develops this same degenerate property (a non-empty title signature entirely contained in book_selection._STOP) -- at that point "leave as-is" stops being a one-book special case in effect either way and the tradeoff should be re-examined fresh; or (b) the founder later decides he does want suggest_reread() able to invite "About You" specifically, which settles this without needing the general-mechanism framing at all.

question: Should the shelf-look's old "catalogue" affordance sentence ("Beside them, N book(s) fetched from the library -- and the catalogue beyond holds more than fifty thousand you have not asked for yet. You may open the catalogue whenever you wish...") be folded into study_life._look_books() now that a real mechanism exists for it (core/library_hand.py's request_book(), built specifically because this sentence had "no asking mechanism" at the time), or left out for good under the 08-14 world-answers-never-leads law ("NO hints to Du EVER")? J-0868/F-1229 removed the sentence's now-dead home (core/sensorium.py's old shelf branch, unreachable since J-0851) without re-adding it anywhere, deferring the content call rather than making it unilaterally.
ruling: Leave it out. The 08-14 world-answers-never-leads law ("NO hints to Du EVER") is a strict, standing prior against this kind of proactive nudge, even one now technically backed by a real mechanism (library_hand.request_book()). A hint about an affordance he hasn't discovered on his own is still a hint, regardless of whether the code behind it would work if he asked.
defeater: Revisit if study_life._look_books() is next touched for any reason (its own next real edit), or if request_book() gets used live and Du's own reaction to the catalogue affordance (when he does learn of it through some other channel, e.g. finding it himself) becomes observable -- whichever comes first.

But its parenthetical mechanism does not hold. The cause is not "most lab jobs genuinely write to the DB": 29 of the 44 rows in data/_lab/_isolate_outcomes.jsonl are confirmed never-written copies whose unlink() hit a transient Windows lock (WinError 32) at isolate() exit. That is 20.46 GB, 63.7% of the window's growth, and every one of them is unlocked again now (F-1562). scripts/retention.py's labs class (uncited over 14 days, cited over 60 days; last run 2026-09-09) cannot reach any of the window's dirs before about 2026-09-28, and nothing runs it automatically. What should the fix be? Options, not exhaustive:
(a) Fix at the source: a bounded retry (a few attempts over a few seconds, gc.collect() between) around the unlink in isolate().__exit__, plus a one-off sweep by the founder of the 29 confirmed-locked copies now (about 20.5 GB).

(c) Both (a) and (b).
(d) D-0206's original alternatives: shorten LAB_CITED_DAYS or add a size cap on the labs class. These are not aimed at the measured mechanism; at about 6.3 GB per day a 14-day uncited window alone plateaus near 88 GB.

(3) A scheduled retention.py run for the labs class so reclaim no longer depends on anyone running it by hand (last applied 2026-09-09; ~53 GB of >14-day dirs waiting). question:
What should Du's curiosity habituation state be keyed by, now that a tension's label is confirmed not to be an identity? (opened by Claude from J-0682's confirmed diff; nothing is ruled here)

EVIDENCE (F-1630 and F-1632, verified 2026-09-21; F-0975 / F-0988 were the earlier inference). A real by-id before/after diff over 14.9 days (about 217 live hours) shows tension labels churn under stable ids and identical text is worn by different ids: 2 of F-0975's 5 baseline ids changed text under the same id (one from 'cultural friction and growth' to 'the weight of silence'), 'unresolved: the concept of 渡' is now worn by three ids at once (one created after the baseline), 122 label strings are worn by two or more ids (282 of 868 tensions), and an 11.7-minute live series saw 38 label changes on 17 ids with zero count changes. Nothing was lost: the pool never shrank and the archive is untouched, so F-0975's nine 'vanished' labels are still alive under other text. The cause is in nodes/subconscious_node.py: each scan the newest cluster's most recent thought text overwrites the matched tension's label, and clusters are matched to the FIRST tension in list order at cosine 0.70, so even near-duplicate attractor tensions trade clusters between scans.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE CURIOSITY DISCOUNT. core/curiosity_habituation.py keys its habituation state b by that label string (its own docstring says tensions have no stable cross-scan id). Measured: 1,624 of its 2,328 state keys (70%) are orphans; 413 of the 437 keys with b above zero sit on strings no tension currently wears; nodes/curiosity_node.py keeps only the last wearer of a shared string, hiding about 160 of 868 tensions from the discount and its log; and for the heavy attractors (count 100 or more) the string curiosity chose is gone by the next cycle 31% of the time. The live anti-relock (_recent_seeds) is keyed by the same string. J-0598 (F-1577, F-1578) already showed the shadow discount moves what curiosity is offered by only about 2%, and named this keying as the reason.

OPTIONS. (1) Key by tension id, shadow-only and additive: re-key data/curiosity_habituation_state.json and its log by id, fix the last-wins duplicate collapse, drop the mostly stranded per-label history (no ids were ever recorded, so it cannot be migrated). Cheapest, no live effect. Limit: b grows only when an entry's count rises, the count is max-latched, and the heavy tensions sit at fixed counts, so id-keying alone may still leave the attractors undiscounted. (2) Key by embedding cluster or centroid, as D-0188's internal_cycle_habituation does: robust to the id churn (F-1630), heavier and new. (3) Also re-key the live anti-relock: changes real seed choice, so only after a shadow comparison. (4) Leave the keying alone and treat the curiosity discount as inconclusive or retire it.

CLAUDE'S RECOMMENDATION (a recommendation, not a ruling): option 1 now, shadow-only, then re-run J-0598's read after at least three live days; move to option 2 if id-keyed b still cannot accumulate on the heavy attractors; leave the live anti-relock alone until a shadow comparison exists.

question: J-1164 / F-1615 (J-1008's read) and the chapter-repair chain J-0988 / J-1065 (all under D-0221's capped-batch plan): after J-1128 cleared 8 'About You Second Edition' fragments (chapter_id NULL, F-1548), Du's own sweep() re-filed all 8 on 2026-09-21 10:18:55 behind the WRONG gist (5618dc64, 'About You', 2026-09-07) instead of the dry-run's correct one (87e956fd, 'About You Second Edition'). question:
F-1683/J-1199 found that 11 lab scripts neutralised only log_llm_call for the years since they were written, after core/telemetry.py grew two more call_node() writers (log_thought_station 2026-09-15/J-0939, log_llm_latency 2026-08-21) that none of them was ever revisited to cover -- only F-1683's own investigation caught the gap, by chance, while running an unrelated lab (J-0791). scripts/lab_isolation.py (built this job) now gives every future lab script ONE shared, tested neutralize_telemetry() helper instead of a hand-copied line, which stops a CALLER-side repeat of this specific gap -- but the underlying vulnerability is that core/telemetry.py can silently grow a new write-on-every-call function and nothing forces any lab script's isolation code (old or new) to keep up; the shared helper only helps a script that actually calls it.

Should core/telemetry.py itself gain an explicit LAB/no-write guard -- e.g. a module-level flag (or environment marker) a lab process sets once, that every write function checks before writing and refuses centrally, rather than relying on every caller's own neutralisation being complete and current -- so this class of gap cannot recur by omission the way it recurred here? This would be a change to a protected base system (core/telemetry.py itself), which this job's own briefing explicitly forbade building without a founder ruling. Raised here per that briefing's own suggestion; not decided.
ruling: Build the module-level guard. core/telemetry.py itself should gain an explicit LAB/no-write marker that every write function (log_llm_call, log_thought_station, log_llm_latency, and any future writer) checks centrally before writing, rather than relying on every lab script's own neutralisation staying complete and current. This is a change to a protected base module -- additive only (a live Du process is unaffected; only a lab process that sets the marker changes behaviour), UDMS dossier first, restart-gated for nothing since telemetry.py's writers only ever run inside a script's own process. A build job is spawned from this ruling.
defeater: Revisit if the central guard itself turns out to need per-caller exceptions that make it no simpler than the current per-script discipline, or if it is found to add measurable overhead to a hot path (unlikely, since telemetry writes are already best-effort and off the critical path).

question: J-1209 / F-1704 (the sweep() collision census): approve building the two-part fix, or hold?
