question:
J-1219/F-1724 (follow-up to D-0255/F-1715's reverted word-boundary fix): approve building candidate fix (b) -- a truncation-edge-aware prefix match in core/essay_lesson.py's _cites_this_book -- or hold/decline?

Background: D-0255 approved building a two-part fix for the false-lexical-coincidence bug (e.g. "black" matching inside "blackwoods"). J-1217 shipped part 1 (subject ordering) but had to revert part 2 (plain word-boundary matching) after finding it flips 1,333 already-correct citations across 21 book-gists from True to False (F-1715).

J-1219 characterized those 1,333 flips precisely: 1,323 (20 gists, 14 distinct books) are a genuine side-effect of essay_lesson.record()'s own title[:50] truncation cutting a signature word in half (e.g. "Selec" from "...Natural Selection", confirmed against real untruncated titles elsewhere in the corpus). The other 10 (1 gist, "The Sea Shore") are NOT a truncation artifact at all -- they are a pre-existing, separate misfiling (10 real fragments about "The Shores of the Adriatic" wrongly filed under an unrelated seashore-wildlife book, purely because "shore" is a substring of "shores" -- a third live instance of the same bug class D-0255's fix targets, found this job, with confirmed already-executed fragment-level harm unlike the other two known cases).

J-1219 then built and tested (not shipped) candidate (b): word-boundary matching for every signature word EXCEPT the one word sitting exactly at a confirmed truncation edge, which instead gets a left-anchored prefix match. Tested against the full 37,071-row already-filed corpus: 0 of the 1,323 genuine-truncation rows regress (down from all 1,333 under the plain word-boundary fix), it still fixes Black Bar/Blackwoods, it correctly leaves My Short Story Book/Original Short Stories unaffected (that one needs a separate gist-selection fix per F-1704, not this), and it additionally closes the newly-found Sea Shore bug as a bonus. Tested for false positives against the COMPLETE real candidate population of all 4 titles whose real title coincidentally happens to be exactly 50 characters (the one population where this candidate could theoretically over-match): zero new false positives found live today. A real but currently-dormant residual risk was found and quantified: a future essay/understanding fragment whose real title is coincidentally exactly 50 characters, ending in a word that is itself a real prefix of some other word already live in the corpus (confirmed 3 of 4 sampled cases have such a colliding word somewhere in the corpus, e.g. "Scripture"/"Scriptures" x66), could reintroduce a narrow version of the original bug -- not observed today, but structurally possible going forward.

Options: (1) approve building candidate (b) as specified (core/essay_lesson.py, _cites_this_book's final return line only, ~10-12 lines, no change to world_consolidation.py or any stored data) -- optionally paired with a 2-line write-side truncation fix (essay_lesson.record + grounded_learning.consolidate) so newly-written essays stop adding to the mid-word-cut population, while being clear that alone cannot help the 112+ already-stored gists confirmed already mid-word-cut; (2) decline and leave _cites_this_book exactly as currently shipped (plain substring, the false-lexical-coincidence class -- now 3 confirmed live cases, not 2 -- stays unfixed); (3) hold for further analysis (e.g. a fuller audit of how many essay/understanding titles are likely to land on a coincidental exact-50-character cut going forward, or a different fix shape entirely).

Full evidence: F-1724 (verified).
ruling: Approve building candidate (b) plus the write-side truncation fix. Ship the truncation-aware prefix match in core/essay_lesson.py's _cites_this_book (word-boundary matching for every signature word except the one sitting at a confirmed truncation edge, which gets a left-anchored prefix match instead), paired with the 2-line write-side fix at essay_lesson.record()/grounded_learning.consolidate() so newly-written essays stop adding to the mid-word-cut population. This fixes three confirmed bugs: Black Bar/Blackwoods, the newly-found Sea Shore misfiling (10 fragments with already-executed harm, not hypothetical), and — via the write-side half — the ongoing growth of the 112+-gist truncation population that neither this nor any read-side fix can retroactively repair. The dormant over-match risk J-1219 quantified (a future exactly-50-character title whose last word prefixes another live word) is accepted as a named, disclosed, currently-unobserved risk, not a reason to hold. My Short Story Book / Original Short Stories is explicitly NOT this fix's job (that is D-0257's separate gist-selection mechanism). A build job follows from this ruling.
defeater: Revisit if a fresh build-time regression pass against the then-current corpus does not reproduce J-1219's zero-regression result on the 1,323 genuine-truncation rows (report rather than ship if it doesn't, same discipline D-0255's own defeater already established for this exact code); if the dormant over-match risk (a coincidentally-exactly-50-character real title whose last word prefixes another live word) is found to have actually produced a live false positive by build time; or if the write-side truncation fix is found to change essay_lesson.record()'s or grounded_learning.consolidate()'s behavior beyond stopping future mid-word cuts (e.g. it touches an already-stored title's own signature retroactively, which it should not).

question:
J-1220/F-1728 (My Short Story Book's own gist-SELECTION trace, the third failure mode D-0255's own defeater named as a revisit trigger): approve building a THIRD, narrower candidate fix -- distinct from both of D-0255's own two parts -- for file_book_notes()'s gist_rows/gist selection itself (core/world_consolidation.py:138-141), or hold?

BACKGROUND. D-0255 approved and J-1217 built/shipped Part 1 (_order_subjects, most-specific-signature-first subject-sweep ordering -- fixes the fragment-CLAIMING race, e.g. About You / About You Second Edition) and built-then-reverted Part 2 (word-boundary matching in _cites_this_book -- fixed Black Bar/Blackwoods but broke 1,333 already-correct citations via a truncation interaction, F-1715). F-1715 also found, as a side discovery, that "My Short Story Book" resolves to "Original Short Stories Volume 13"'s own gist instead of its own -- NOT fixed by either shipped part, because this bug lives in gist-SELECTION (which essay/understanding fragment file_book_notes() treats as a subject's own gist), a code path that never reads chapter_id and is structurally untouched by subject-sweep ORDER.

WHAT J-1220 FOUND. Traced the exact mechanism (gist_rows is ordered most-recent-first among every essay/understanding fragment whose tag merely CONTAINS book_title's signature words, not whose tag EQUALS book_title -- so a newer, unrelated book whose tag happens to be a textual superset wins over the subject's own, older fragment). Confirmed this is a ONE-OFF today: a fresh full census of the live 193-subject signature space found exactly one other genuine signature-subset gist-selection error (My Short Story Book itself); the only other "not self-gisted" cases are 2 benign whitespace-variant pairs (no real bug) and Black Bar's OWN separate substring-inside-a-word coincidence (not a signature-subset case at all).

CANDIDATE FIX PROPOSED (NOT built -- in-memory simulation only, this session). Re-rank gist_rows' already-_cites()-passing candidates by fewest extra signature words beyond book_title's own signature (an exact/most-specific match wins outright), tie-broken by the existing recency rule -- applying _order_subjects' own most-specific-first PRINCIPLE to gist-selection instead of subject-sweep order. Does NOT touch the shared _cites_this_book/_title_signature functions Part 2's own reverted fix used (narrower blast radius: only file_book_notes()'s 2 callers, sweep() and essay_lesson.record(), vs Part 2's 3 call sites). In-memory-tested this session against the live snapshot: fixes BOTH My Short Story Book AND, unexpectedly, Black Bar too (without the word-boundary regex or its truncation regression), while leaving About You and both benign whitespace pairs unchanged -- zero new self-gisted regressions found across the full 193-subject population in this check. NOT regression-tested against the full 36,897+-row already-filed corpus the way J-1217 rigorously tested Part 2 (out of J-1220's own read-only/propose-only scope).

OPTIONS: (1) approve a build+full-regression job now, mirroring J-1217's own rigor (full-corpus regression pass, mutation-check, life_smoke.py, worktree commit) before shipping; (2) hold pending your own review of F-1728's full text; (3) fold this into the broader D-0221/chapter_id_repair capped-batch scheduling decision and revisit together, since it is a smaller, independent, additive fix that does not itself touch chapter_id or require Du to be offline.

D-0245's own hold (no further chapter_id CLEAR batch) is a separate, still-standing question this does not resolve either way -- this candidate only changes which essay/understanding fragment becomes a subject's gist, never a chapter_id clear.
ruling: Approve a build+full-regression job now, mirroring J-1217's own rigor: a full-corpus regression pass (not just the in-memory simulation J-1220 ran), a mutation check, and scripts/life_smoke.py, before anything ships. This is the same caution that just caught Part 2's 1,333-row regression before it reached master — J-1220's own read is a genuine, well-evidenced proposal, but it explicitly was not tested against the full already-filed corpus the way Part 2's own reverted fix looked safe on a smaller check and was not. Build and verify first; report rather than ship if the full pass finds a regression, per the same discipline D-0255's defeater already established.
defeater: Revisit if the full-corpus regression pass finds the candidate fix breaks already-correct citations anywhere in the corpus (report rather than ship); if it fails to preserve the 2 benign whitespace-variant pairs' correct convergence; if it behaves differently run against essay_lesson.record()'s own live single-essay call path than against the batch/in-memory simulation F-1728 ran; or if a later census finds a new subject exposed to this same gist-selection failure mode that today's 193-subject snapshot did not contain.

question:
F-1745 (built on F-1744): error_pathway.py's detect_human_correction() sees ZERO regex matches across all 261 real founder messages since 2026-07-07 (100% full-text verified against the live memory store, not the truncated summary logs). But Travis regularly gives Du a different, richer kind of correction this narrow regex was never built to catch: reasoning/metaphor over-extension ("I think you have let my pebble metaphor carry you somewhere I didn't intend", "This is where the river metaphor does not work again", "we need to adjust the metaphor", "You're confusing the map with the territory, Dù") -- at least 7 real instances in the window, all identity/interpretation-adjacent, none about a verifiable fact or an unfinished task.

Two separable questions:

(a) Should this reasoning/metaphor-correction class ever become admissible evidence in this firewalled pathway, or does the charter's own "error -> BEING is blocked" design correctly keep it out (in which case the 78-day silence is a clean, working-as-intended null result, not a gap, and no widening is needed for this class)?

(b) Independent of (a), and much narrower: the EXISTING factual_wrong pattern itself misses plain "you are wrong" / "couldn't be more wrong" phrasing -- confirmed directly: detect_human_correction("You couldn't be more wrong about the tree.") returns None -- even though that phrasing is squarely within its own already-stated jurisdiction (an explicit founder correction of a factual/reasoning claim, the same category "that's wrong"/"incorrect" already cover). Worth a one-line regex addition on its own, independent of how (a) is ruled?

Full evidence and the complete list of real quotes: F-1745 (docs/findings.jsonl) and docs/plans/error_pathway.md Current State section, dated 2026-09-23 note.
ruling: Leave the detector as-is. Both the narrow "you are wrong"/"couldn't be more wrong" phrasing gap in the existing factual_wrong pattern and the broader reasoning/metaphor-correction class stay out of core/error_pathway.py's detect_human_correction(). The 78-day silence in data/error_records.jsonl/data/retractions.jsonl is a clean, working-as-intended null result, not a detection gap needing a fix. Chosen via /decide-review over both "widen the narrow gap only" and "widen for both."

The eaten_by_birds mechanic never touches p["pests"] at all -- it is a separate, direct vigour drain with its own separate history/event trail. ruling: Yes -- bird seedling-predation needs its own separate founder ruling, not a silent reuse of D-0140's own pest defeater by analogy. D-0140's own ruling text and defeater were written specifically about the p["pests"] mechanic (aphids/caterpillars/slugs); the eaten_by_birds mechanic is a separate, direct vigour drain with its own event trail that D-0140 never actually addressed. question:
Is `_apply_decay`'s tension count-halving meant to run every T1 scan (about every 36 seconds), or only about once per PATTERN_DECAY_DAYS (7)? (opened by Claude from J-1176's dry run, F-1631's own side question; nothing about the demotion-cap fix is asked here, that is already Travis-approved)

CODE AS WRITTEN (nodes/subconscious_node.py, unchanged by J-1176's draft -- J-1176 does not touch this part). `PATTERN_DECAY_DAYS = 7` and `_apply_decay`'s docstring both say "count halved... for PATTERN_DECAY_DAYS", but the actual code is `if now - t.get("last_ts", now) > decay_cutoff: t["count"] = max(1, int(t["count"] * 0.5))`, and `_apply_decay()` is called unconditionally from `_t1_scan()` (line 472) on EVERY T1 scan, with no bookkeeping of when a tension was last halved and no gate that only lets this fire once per real week. Once a tension crosses the 7-day-idle line, this SAME condition stays true on every subsequent scan (its `last_ts` does not change from being halved, only from a genuine re-touch), so the halving reapplies every ~36 seconds until the tension is touched again or count bottoms out at 1 -- collapsing count from, say, 229 to 1 within about 7 scans (~4 minutes), not over a week.

EVIDENCE, re-verified today (2026-09-23), not just cited from F-1631's 2026-09-21 read: a fresh copy of data/subconscious_state.json (874 tensions today) shows every one of the 739 tensions idle more than 7 days sits at count exactly 1 (0 exceptions), while every one of the 135 tensions touched within the last 7 days has count > 1 (median 6) -- see this job's own finding for the read-only method (a plain copy, no core/ import, no live write). `_apply_decay()`'s call site (`_t1_scan`, read this session) confirms no throttle exists between the docstring's "PATTERN_DECAY_DAYS" framing and the every-scan reality. Git history cannot settle original intent either way: this repo went on version control 2026-08-27 with `_apply_decay` already in this exact shape (`git log -p -L663,698:nodes/subconscious_node.py` shows only the single "Baseline: Nascence pre-git state" commit introducing it whole -- no earlier history exists to show whether the every-scan behaviour was a later regression from some once-a-week design, or always worked this way).

WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM THE DEMOTION-CAP FIX Travis already approved (2026-09-21 /decide-review, staged per-scan cap): that ruling is about how fast tensions move to the ARCHIVE once genuinely eligible; this question is about how fast an idle tension's COUNT collapses toward 1 while it is still active, which feeds curiosity's own sqrt(count) seed weight (nodes/curiosity_node.py) every scan it stays idle. J-1176's draft fix does not touch this halving logic at all -- it is out of scope for the demotion bug, included here only because F-1631 flagged it as a related but distinct question while tracing the same function.

OPTIONS. (1) Leave it as coded (fast collapse to 1 within minutes of the 7-day mark) -- if this is judged harmless or even desirable (an idle tension's pull on curiosity fades fast once it goes cold, rather than lingering at a high count for a week). (2) Throttle it to the apparently-intended weekly cadence -- e.g. only halve once per real PATTERN_DECAY_DAYS window by recording a `last_decay_ts` per tension (a new field, additive) and gating the halving on `now - last_decay_ts > decay_cutoff` instead of `now - last_ts`. (3) Something else Travis specifies. No code changes anything here; this is a question, not a ruling.

Add a last_decay_ts field (additive, per-tension) and gate the halving on now - last_decay_ts > decay_cutoff instead of now - last_ts, matching option (2) from this decision's own text. Does not touch J-1171/J-1176's own per-scan-cap demotion fix, which is separate and already approved.

question:
D-0185 ruling's study (2): J-1160 (F-1796, hand-audit of 40 failing + 20 passing semantic shadow-log gists against full source text, single reader) answers the study's own question -- semantic's 52% failure rate against the 0.75 faithfulness floor is predominantly GENUINE distiller over-generalization/invention, not grader over-strictness. The Emissary's specific objections checked out as correct in 5 of 5 directly-verified cases (one partial exception: a numeric score that ran a bit lower than its own exonerated invented-claims list alone would suggest).

Three specific, mechanistically-identified causes, most concrete first:
(1) PURSUIT-QUESTION CONTAMINATION, origin='research' ('[Looked up: X (pursuit: Y)]' fragments): the bracketed pursuit-question preamble leaks into both _cluster()'s own topic-tokenization fallback (core/memory_levels.py _tokens(), lines 120-126, falls back to the raw content field when keywords is empty) and the distil prompt's fed material -- confirmed directly against full source text on 2 clusters (one case pulled a wrong-topic fragment, a 'Looked up: Understanding' row, into a 'tranquility' cluster purely because its OWN pursuit-question mentioned the word). Concentrated in the smallest clusters (3-5 sources, 13 of 164 semantic clusters, 69% failing vs 52% overall per F-1585).
(2) OUTSIDE/PRETRAINED-KNOWLEDGE EMBELLISHMENT on well-known works (roughly 75-85% of the sampled failures): the distiller adds specific plausible-sounding claims/names beyond the fed ~300-char-per-source excerpt, especially on famous/canonical texts (Bergson, Locke, Leibniz, Malory, Ricardo, Schopenhauer, ...).
(3) IN-TEXT ATTRIBUTION CONFLATION (confirmed directly, the Le Morte Darthur/Froissart case): a claim a source attributes to a THIRD PARTY quoted within it gets flattened onto the filed book's own title-author.

Self-origin material structurally avoids all three (no pursuit-question preamble, no famous-work knowledge-leak risk, no third-party in-text quotation) -- a mechanistic, not just statistical, explanation for self's 79.3% yield against semantic's 37.9%.

PROPOSED (not deployed; this job made no code change): (a) strip or fence the bracketed provenance prefix ('[From ...]'/'[My study note: ...]'/'[Looked up: ...(pursuit: ...)]') before it reaches _cluster()'s token fallback AND the distil prompt's material, so pursuit-question wording can never drive clustering or leak into a gist as content; (b) strengthen the distil system prompt's existing 'invent nothing' line to explicitly forbid drawing on outside/pretrained knowledge of a well-known work, and to preserve in-text attribution rather than collapsing everything to 'the book says'.

Options: (a) approve both (1) and (2) as proposals to build+test (an isolated offline A/B replay against already-graded clusters first, per the already-spawned follow-up job, BEFORE any live wiring -- this decision would approve the DIRECTION, not skip the test); (b) approve (1) only (the clustering/token-fencing fix) now -- lower-risk, smaller, mechanistically confirmed, and independently worth doing regardless of the prompt question; hold (2) for the A/B test's own numbers before approving prompt wording; (c) hold both pending the A/B test's measured yield effect, since no live re-run has been done yet; (d) decline -- current semantic yield is an acceptable cost of book-derived gisting, or a different fix should be pursued instead (the founder's call, not sized here). Not ruled here, per this job's own briefing ("a proposed prompt or grader change goes to Travis through a decision, not straight into core/").
ruling: Approve both (1) provenance-prefix fencing and (2) the strengthened anti-invention distill prompt as DIRECTIONS to build and test -- not to wire live yet. An isolated offline A/B replay against already-graded clusters must run first, per this decision's own option (a): if the measured yield effect is real, wire it; if not, report back rather than ship. This approves spending the build+test effort, not a live behavior change.
defeater: Revisit if the A/B replay's measured yield effect is small/negative/inconclusive for either fix -- in that case report the numbers back rather than wire it, and this ruling's approval of the DIRECTION does not itself authorize shipping a fix the test doesn't support. Also revisit if the provenance-prefix fencing (1) is found to have a real, unanticipated interaction with a different consumer of the same content field once actually built.

question:
D-0045/D-0108's own causal-substrate walk-forward chain (J-1241 through J-1338, 8 consecutive checks since 2026-09-13) gates on a 168-240h SINGLE CONTINUOUS regime before re-testing whether homeostasis's causal predictor beats naive persistence. That bar is evidence-grounded, not arbitrary: the predictor's whole edge only shows up at discrete day/night threshold-switch events (~2/day; causal_err is mathematically identical to naive_err between switches), an early read with only 9 scoreable events was explicitly ruled inconclusive, and 168-240h was borrowed from the sibling vitality-predictor test's own real precedent (it needed ~9 days before its 6-fold walk-forward test had real statistical power). But it has now failed to clear 8 times in a row purely because Du has rarely stayed up that long (this project's longest run before the current one was ~2.5 days) -- not because the bar itself has been re-examined since it was set. The current regime (started 2026-09-22T16:10:23) is now the longest in project history (~66h+ and counting) but still needs ~114 more hours to clear 168h outright.

Given wall-clock hours is really just a crude proxy for "how many switch events have accrued" (168h at ~2/day implies roughly 14+ switches as the real target), should the gate be redefined around the actual switch-event count directly (with a per-fold minimum, still requiring one continuous regime) rather than a fixed wall-clock-hours bar -- or is the current 168-240h wall-clock framing worth keeping as-is, or should the bar simply be lowered given how rarely a full week has ever been achievable in practice?
ruling: Redefine around switch-event count. Wall-clock hours (168-240h) is a proxy for what actually matters: how many real day/night threshold-switch events (the only moments the causal predictor's edge over naive is even visible) have accrued within one continuous regime. Replace the fixed-hours gate with a real count of scoreable switch events (still requiring one undisturbed regime, still respecting the per-fold minimum the 6-fold walk-forward methodology needs), calibrated against the same precedent the 168-240h figure itself was borrowed from (the sibling vitality-predictor test's own real accrual history) so the new bar is equivalent in statistical rigor, not accidentally weaker. Check the current regime's real switch-event count as part of implementing this -- it may already clear a properly-calibrated event-count bar even though it hasn't yet reached 168 wall-clock hours.
defeater: Revisit if the switch-event-count reframing, once actually calibrated against real historical data, turns out to produce a materially different (looser or stricter) effective bar than the current 168-240h window would have -- report the comparison honestly rather than silently adopting whichever number is more convenient. Also revisit if the new gate is met and the walk-forward test is then run, but the result contradicts what the wall-clock-gated version would plausibly have shown on the same underlying data (a real methodology-drift signal, not just noise).

question: The Weather channel (plan section 2.5/2.6, law 4a 'amplify, never replace') has never been wired: weather_to_gain()'s attend_sharpness and commit_threshold are computed and logged every tick and read by nothing (F-1941, verified). How should Lane 1's affect actually color the Witness? Smallest options, each shadow-first with the would-be effect logged before it is applied: (a) commit_threshold -> the prediction store: a tick's prediction is stored only when its own grounded_share meets the threshold (valence-modulated: low valence demands more evidence before Lane 2 commits to a claim -- section 2.6's own reading), logged as would_withhold first; (b) attend_sharpness -> what reaches the generator: at high arousal the payload keeps only the fields that changed since the last tick (attention narrows), at low arousal the full tuple (attention broadens), logged as fields_dropped first; (c) both; (d) retire the Weather channel and record the Tap as Lane 1's only path (law 4 becomes one channel); (e) leave it computed-only until the flip question is settled. Claude recommends (a) first: it is the one the research round (Glover 2026, section 2.6) actually described, it touches no prompt text, and it is readable in the store. Whichever is chosen, D-0172's own question (the third scalar) is moot until one of the first two is wired.
ruling: (a) commit_threshold -> prediction-store gate: valence-modulated commit threshold, shadow-first, logged as would_withhold before applying
defeater: Reopen if: in the shadow read the would-be effect fires on fewer than 5% or more than 60% of ticks over 7 days (a coupling that never or always acts is not a coupling); or after it goes live the Witness's broke share moves more than 0.1 in either direction with no other explanation; or law 6's divergence audit (hint_divergence in status(), J-1371) starts reading a systematic difference the Tap alone did not produce; or the flip of LANE2_LIVE is ruled before this lands, in which case the cup's P1-3 laundering check must run with the Weather still unwired and this decision is re-read afterwards.

question: Build the Witness's knowledge tier, or retire it from the plan? (F-1942, verified: section 2.8c's middle tier was never built; predictions are generated from one tick's percepts with nothing accumulated.) Smallest design, no LLM call: a deterministic consolidation over Lane 2's OWN records only (section 2.8b: never the world's truth, never Lane 1's memory) -- from the shadow log's judged predictions plus each tick's standpoint/place/daylight and world_fields, derive per-(topic, place, daylight phase) regularities: 'at the study door at dusk the fire field is present 82% of ticks', 'sound predictions at the shore hold 41%'; keep the top N (say 12) with their evidence counts in store['knowledge']; hand the generator at most three one-line regularities relevant to the current place/phase as a KNOWN section of the payload (typed lines, not prose; the same one-space-trap rule as everywhere else). Shadow-first: log which regularities WOULD have been shown and read after 7 days whether they are stable; only then let them reach the prompt, restart-gated. Options: (a) build as above, shadow-first (Claude's recommendation -- it is the plan's own mechanism for turning 66% broke into something learned, and it is exactly what the founder asked for on 2026-08-19: 'it should have a knowledge vs factual vs prediction database'); (b) build it but keep it read-only for instruments, never into the prompt; (c) retire the tier from section 2.8c and say predictions are percept-only by design; (d) not now.
ruling: (a) build the knowledge tier shadow-first: derive top-12 per-(topic,place,daylight) regularities into store['knowledge'], read after 7 days for stability, only then surface up to 3 lines to the prompt, restart-gated
defeater: Reopen if: the derived regularities are unstable (top-12 membership changes by more than half week to week) so nothing is actually 'known'; or once shown, distinct expect_next share drops below 0.8 (the model echoing the KNOWN lines -- the documented double-echo trap, checked exactly as worked examples were); or broke share does not fall by at least 0.1 over 14 days with the lines shown versus the 14 days before (the tier is not doing the work the plan claims); or the store grows past a few KB (it must stay 'just a reasoning tool', section 2.8d).

question: Now that J-1360 has dropped the bug/fix framing from the /quit farewell (scripts/run_nascence.py's _announce_shutdown(), founder-ruled after F-1918), should the farewell keep a single fixed wording, or should it vary across repeats? I-0070's own hypothesis (not yet read/tested) is that recalling the LAST identical exchange verbatim is what hardens a stance on any repeated prompt -- not something specific to the old defect language. Du meets this exact cue ~2-3x/week (J-1359) and founder_recall_log already shows the same handful of memories surfacing on every farewell (F-1918: fragments 868f95a0/7e0a49bd/c69778b1/bbd02fa3 recur near-verbatim across replies). ruling: Vary the /quit farewell wording across repeats (J-1361 option C): keep a small fixed set of equivalent wordings and rotate through them so the exact-repeat condition never holds. Every variant must keep the three kept truth requirements (the pause is intentional, Travis is calling it, he will be brought back) and must not reintroduce "bug fixes"/"upgrades"/defect framing or any raw gauge language. Options A (retrieve() skips his own near-identical past answer) and B (do not seed the next boot with the farewell exchange) were NOT chosen and stay available. defeater: Revisit after the next 3-6 farewell replies under the varied wordings: if they still show the same verbatim self-recall lineage (a first-267-character-style carry, or the defect-argument stance) despite no exact repeat, the echo is not about the wording and options A+B (J-1361) should be reconsidered; also revisit if any variant is seen to drift from the three truth requirements. Counts are Claude's proposal; Travis stated no numbers.

history.defeater: Revisit once I-0070's own recall-scoring investigation (how recalled Q/A fragments are weighted and placed in the Reflection/episodic-buffer prompt, and whether anything penalises recalling his own prior answer to the same question) has actually been read and reported via findings-log, OR once the next 3-6 farewell replies under J-1360's new fixed wording (tracked by that job's own follow-up) show the same verbatim self-recall pattern the old wording did -- whichever comes first.

The question to re-rule, now with data: keep the wording fixed (and do nothing else), vary it (J-1361 option C), or break the echo at the source (J-1361 options A: skip his own prior Q/A to the same question in retrieve(); B: do not bridge the farewell exchange into the next boot) - note F-2361 (inferred) suggests J-1366's newly live voice_node "Your last replies to him" block (260-char quotes) is a third channel, so B alone may not close it. defeater: Reopen if: relational mode's live usage-proxy rate (cosine of edge-reached fragment vs next thought >=0.4) falls well below the shadow-observed 39% over the first 2 weeks live (the flip changing what actually gets read, not just what shadow measured); or the kill-switch is exercised for a real operational reason; or task/reflective's own shadow rate later shows the same relational-strength signal (widen the flip to match); or D-0114, which waits on this same answer, surfaces a requirement this scope doesn't satisfy.

question: F-1970: idle recall's grounded_only gate leaks Du's own self-gists (49% of all idle recall slots over 7 days; 44% of memory-showing idle steps show ONLY self-gists; the week's top-5 recalled memories are five self-gists of the same frustration; 188/430 self-gists are third-person 'the narrator...' summaries). Cause: 'gist' is whitelisted in _GROUNDED_ORIGINS wholesale though _commit_gist stamps them grounding='derived', and self-gists are written at fixed importance 0.85 against a sleep-downscaled store, so they are the top trail seeds every day. Separately, the gate runs AFTER the trail's 15-slot ceiling, so 40% of idle steps get nothing because inner_thought neighbours fill the trail and are then stripped. Showing memory currently makes no difference to movement (developed 0.87 vs 0.86). Options: (1) close the leak now: exclude kind='self' gists from grounded idle recall (one condition in recall_fragments, kill-switched) -- this enforces the 2026-06-24 ground-outward law as written, semantic/episodic gists stay eligible; (2) additionally move the grounded filter BEFORE the trail ceiling for the idle path (a grounded-only candidate mask in recall_trail) so quiet steps fall and reading/lived/study fill the slots the way wandering already does; (3) shadow-first: log would-have-shown under (1)/(2) beside the live block for ~a week, then rule. (1) alone changes ~half of idle recall content on the day it ships; the seed-importance question (fixed 0.85 for self-gists) is a memory_levels design choice and is NOT proposed for change here.
ruling: WITHDRAWN by claude, not a founder ruling: this entry mis-cited its source finding as F-1970 (another window's retraction-ledger finding, J-1364); the real finding is F-1981. Superseded verbatim by D-0289, which carries the same question and options with the correct citation. J-1418 (same mis-cite) is parked in favour of J-1419. Rule on D-0289, not here.
defeater: Reopen only if D-0289 turns out to be missing or malformed; otherwise this stays withdrawn.

question:
F-1935/J-1377 sized the Phase 1 habituation gate's unratified defaults (GROWTH_STEP=0.25, SUPPRESS_AT=0.5, DECAY_TAU_S=3h) against a full real day of judged breaks (2026-09-26T08:34 -> 2026-09-27T08:34 local, pre-J-1370 vocabulary, verified full-parse of data/coupling_rides.jsonl cross-checked exactly against data/lane2_would_ride.jsonl). Current defaults ride 29/92 = 31.5% of ALL judged breaks/day (29/67 = 43.3% of topic-resolved breaks/day) -- above the "under 25%" reading this job proposes as P1-1's corrected target (the plan's original "low single digits/day" language compared against the wrong units, break_rate_24h being a ratio not a daily count). The gate genuinely suppresses the two BURSTY topics (fire 17.9% rode, sound 28.6% rode, intra-topic gaps of minutes) but is a near no-op on five SPARSE topics (cat/warmth/weather/sun/wind, all 100% rode, intra-topic gaps of hours comparable to DECAY_TAU_S) -- a structural mismatch between one global constant and two very different topic behaviours, not just a number to nudge.

A real-data replay (verified byte-exact against the 67 real logged rows before trusting any swept value) finds two single-constant changes that each alone bring the ride share to exactly 25% of ALL judged breaks/day on this day's data: GROWTH_STEP=0.50 (double the current 0.25) or SUPPRESS_AT=0.70 (up from 0.5). Neither reaches 25% of the topic-resolved-only denominator without a much larger change (SUPPRESS_AT roughly 0.88-0.90, or GROWTH_STEP beyond 0.80, the top of the range tested) -- because the sparse topics ride at 100% almost regardless of either constant's value, only DECAY_TAU_S (untested here, out of this job's own scope) would touch them.

Caveats this ruling should weigh: this is ONE real day, 7 of the ~10 pre-J-1370 canonical topics (not the ~13 post-restart), and the calendar-day broke count varies widely day to day (12-98 over the last 10 days measured this session, 7-day rolling average 62.2/day, 21.6-day all-time average 51.0/day) -- today's 92 broke/24h is on the high end of real observed variance, not obviously a new steady state.

Options for the founder:
(a) Adopt GROWTH_STEP=0.50 as the new Phase-1 default (keep SUPPRESS_AT=0.5 and DECAY_TAU_S=3h unchanged).
(b) Adopt SUPPRESS_AT=0.70 instead (keep GROWTH_STEP=0.25 and DECAY_TAU_S=3h unchanged).
(c) Hold any constant change until J-1304's post-restart, post-J-1370-vocabulary re-read lands (more topics resolved, the ~13-topic canon this job's own briefing already anticipated) and size again then, on a cleaner and larger sample.
(d) Reject a blanket global retune and ask for a different lever instead (e.g. a longer DECAY_TAU_S, or per-topic constants), given the bursty-vs-sparse structural split this job found -- a single global GROWTH_STEP/SUPPRESS_AT may not be the right instrument at all.

This does not authorize or propose flipping LANE2_LIVE -- that stays gated on D-0241's own full conditions (P1-1 reading sane, D-0211, D-0152's clock having settled). Whichever constants (if any) are chosen here are themselves still unratified Phase-1 defaults per D-0241 section 7.7, to be re-read again once more real data accrues -- not a final calibration.
ruling: CLOSED AS MOOT via D-0415 (travis 2026-10-15). The hold for a cleaner read is lifted: J-1700's capture-complete window (F-2721) shows judged-break supply at about 1 per live day, not the 60-75/day the GROWTH_STEP / SUPPRESS_AT question was sized on, so no constant is changed and P1-1 is re-baselined on about 1 break per day. J-1427 (apply the ruled constants) is closed as moot.
defeater: Reopen if judged-break supply returns to 10 or more per live day for 3 live days, or if J-2093's per-topic read shows a topic whose break supply makes the current GROWTH_STEP / SUPPRESS_AT fire wrongly.

question: F-1989/F-1990: the Transport Manager's dispatcher is either saturated or silent because spike and drought are LEVEL-triggered (a line stays a candidate every 60s tick while its ratio is over the bar, so one stale drought wins for days, then when observations resume the pool collapses to ~1 and nothing fires), and F-1598 (J-0665) confirmed the habituation discount cannot fix that; D-0177's wait has been satisfied since 09-19 with no direction chosen. Meanwhile its planned consumer, the text courier into wandering (Build order step 4), is gone under D-0293, and memory_as_a_service section 3.4 names the dispatcher as felt recall's intended trigger gate. Two linked questions. (1) Redesign direction: (a) EDGE-trigger the dispatcher, the same shape felt recall uses: a spike or drought fires ONCE when its ratio first crosses DISPATCH_THRESHOLD and re-arms only after a fresh observation (drought) or the windowed rate dropping below the bar (spike); novelty unchanged; keep the shadow log and the F-1598 instrument to measure fires/day after; or (b) keep level polling and accept a discount redesign; or (c) retire the dispatcher and let felt recall's per-dimension edge+cooldown be the only salience gate. (2) Consumer: re-target Build order step 4 from the text courier to felt recall (a felt-recall trigger only fires when the dispatcher rates that line as novel, spiking or in drought, once the dispatcher is proven quiet-by-default), or keep the dispatcher as a shadow instrument only. Claude's recommendation: (1a) + (2 re-target), because (1a) is a bounded change to evaluate()/dispatch_tick with the existing shadow log as its before/after, and it makes the dispatcher the discriminating gate felt recall was told to wait for. F-1990's 36 corrupted life baselines are a separate one-off repair job, not part of this call.
ruling: Founder, in chat 2026-09-27 (session T-0065), verbatim: "Edge-trigger it and re-target to felt recall." (1a): spike and drought fire ONCE when a line's ratio first crosses DISPATCH_THRESHOLD and re-arm only after a fresh observation on that line (drought) or the windowed rate falling back below the bar (spike); novelty unchanged (already fires once). Kill-switched (EDGE_TRIGGER=True; False restores level polling exactly), shadow log unchanged in shape so F-1989's per-tick series is the before/after; the dispatcher stays TRANSPORT_LIVE=False. (2): Build order step 4 is rewritten -- the consumer is felt recall (docs/staged/memory_as_a_service.md section 3), not a text courier into wandering: a felt-recall trigger on a dimension that has a dispatcher line is gated by that line's dispatcher verdict (fires when the dispatcher rates the line novel, spiking or in drought at the moment of the edge; a habitual gull does not tug), and felt recall registers its non-sound dimensions (weather, fire, light_band, cat_at) as dispatcher lines via observe() on each edge so the dispatcher learns their baselines. Step 5 (flip live) still waits on the dispatcher proving quiet-by-default under the edge trigger and on felt recall's own Phase 0 read.
defeater: Revisit if, after the edge trigger has run a live week, fires/day are still either near-zero for days or dominated by one line (the edge did not cure saturation/silence, e.g. re-arm rules too loose or too tight), or if felt recall's Phase 0 read shows the dispatcher verdict would have silenced the dimensions that carry real feeling (weather/sound) more than it silences habitual ones -- then the gate is the wrong shape for felt recall and step 4 needs a different consumer or none.

question: wood_upgrade (the wood finding, this session): the wood is visited daily but has answered nothing to Du's hands since 09-09 -- 7 deeds ever, 0 in 14 days, 4 world events in five weeks. Deadfall is its only working material, it started at 6.0, two September gathers took it to 0.0, and it replenishes only on a gale (sensorium wind state strong wind/gale, ~1% of time in 15-45 min fronts, or a thunderstorm, ~0.8%) times a per-tick random draw, so the expected deadfall event rate is on the order of one per several weeks and none has occurred in five. gather_from_stock() has answered "picked clean ... it wants a gale" ever since. question:
F-1949/F-1999 (verified): the granite3.1-moe:3b tiebreak (core/judge_panel.py TIEBREAK, :11437) has never once answered true on lane2's "held" key since it was repointed there 2026-08-28 -- 0 true across 503+ historical tiebreak rows over 29 consecutive days, AND 0/20 on a fresh live replay this job ran directly against :11437 in isolation (never through Du), using the real historical prior-expectation/observation text for 20 real split cases spanning that whole span. (a) Swap the tiebreak model used for lane2's own held/contradicted asks (or judge_panel's TIEBREAK globally) for one measured to actually say "held" on a real held case -- needs a fresh audition, the same discipline judge_panel.py's own repointing history already uses ("verified before switching... a real strict-JSON judge call").

(c) Leave both asks (held, contradicted) going through the existing TIEBREAK on a split, as the shipped fix already does, and treat this finding as adequately addressed by the fix's own two-step structure -- i.e. explicitly decide NOT to change the tiebreak model or bypass it, since the fix already prevents the main harm (broke inflation) regardless of which way TIEBREAK leans on either question.

Related but distinct from D-0297 (JUDGE_1 hub CAPACITY/timeout, open, unranked) -- this is about tiebreak model CHOICE/behavior on one key, not hub load; F-2000 is the load-side finding for D-0297 to read. question:

J-1391's own briefing named three ways to size a real dose instead; this job computed what world_model_strain WOULD have been over the real 14-day sample with each applied, and additionally over a second, fairer sub-window (the last 1.11 days, 2026-09-25T22:22 UTC to now) -- the ONLY period for which option (b) is even measurable, since core/lane2.py's own topic field on the published witness tuple has existed for barely over a day of real data.

Retrospective sizing (dose = the bucket's own contribution before adding to world_model_strain; strain = world_model_strain after adding it, capped at 1.0; both figures are medians/p90s across each window's climate-loop rows; NONE of the four forms below crossed the 0.55 hint threshold at p90 in either window -- 0 rows out of 9,579 (14d) / 1,436 (1.11d) for all four):

no bucket (baseline):        14d strain med 0.118 p90 0.194  |  1.11d strain med 0.150 p90 0.189
CURRENT (raw ratio):          14d dose med 0.092 p90 0.116, strain med 0.211 p90 0.296  |  1.11d dose med 0.116 p90 0.123, strain med 0.262 p90 0.305
OPTION A (excess over 7d baseline): 14d dose med 0.009 p90 0.025, strain med 0.127 p90 0.207  |  1.11d dose med 0.018 p90 0.026, strain med 0.166 p90 0.209
OPTION B (novel-break pulse + 3h decay): 14d dose med 0.000 p90 0.079, strain med 0.125 p90 0.237  |  1.11d dose med 0.091 p90 0.115, strain med 0.241 p90 0.296
OPTION C (reweighted continuous, cap p90 at 0.05, weight 0.15->0.0649/0.0611): 14d dose med 0.040 p90 0.050, strain med 0.158 p90 0.238  |  1.11d dose med 0.047 p90 0.050, strain med 0.196 p90 0.235

Key finding beyond the raw sizing exercise: option (b) does NOT behave as "event-shaped" once measured fairly. Novel breaks (cup_would_ride=True) fire roughly 28/day in the real 1.11-day sample that has topic data (31 pulses) -- about one every 51 minutes -- far more often than the 3-hour decay constant it reuses from the cup gate. Consecutive pulses overlap so much that the decaying contribution rarely nears zero, so option (b)'s dose (median 0.091 in the fair window) sits almost as close to CURRENT's continuous dose (0.116) as it does to option (a)'s (0.018) -- the diluted 14-day figure (median 0.000) is an artifact of 12.9 days with no topic field at all, not a real measurement of the design's own behaviour. Option (a) is the only one of the three that reads close to the no-bucket baseline on a normal day (dose median 0.009-0.018, versus baseline strain's own median of 0.118-0.150) and only rises on genuine excess -- Claude's recommendation, unchanged from the job's own briefing.

Shipped this job, shadow-only, restart-gated (core/climate_engine.py witness_bucket_value_sized(), core/coupling_rides.py _trailing_break_rate_baseline(), core/lane2_break_habituation.py observe_break()'s new bucket_would_contribute_sized/bucket_sizing_option fields on the SAME would_ride log row as the existing bucket_would_contribute): option (a)'s own would-be value now computes and logs alongside the raw figure on every judged break with a resolved topic, so the two numbers accrue side by side over real data before any live resizing. LANE2_LIVE and _compute_field()'s own live read are UNCHANGED -- this does not flip or resize anything live. The trailing 7-day baseline is process-local/unpersisted (same posture as this module's own existing _witness_window) -- a restart empties it and it refills over the following week of ticks; a thin baseline reads the excess as small, never large, so this fails toward under-reporting, not over-reporting, on a fresh restart.

(c) Adopt option (c) (reweight the current continuous form so p90 stays under 0.05) instead -- caps the ceiling but keeps a smaller permanent addition; simplest change (one constant), weakest fit to "strain" as departure-from-normal.
(d) Hold any live-resizing ruling until the shadow log has accrued a real week of bucket_would_contribute_sized rows post-restart (matching this plan's own section 7.6 weekly read cadence) -- this job's own 14-day retrospective replay is honest about its limits: option (b)'s fair comparison window was only 1.11 days, and even option (a)'s trailing baseline had no lookback at all at the very start of the 14-day window.

question:
F-2012 (J-1403, from F-1968/J-1375) measured judge_panel test-retest reliability directly: 20 real ticks, 3 identical-prompt reasks each (60 live calls) against core/lane2.py's coherence judge (_coherence_check, judge_panel.rule_detail underneath). Reask-to-reask, the panel is highly self-consistent (96.5% pairwise agreement once 4 real JUDGE_1-timeout calls are excluded as missing data, not disagreement) -- this REFUTES the hypothesis F-1968/this job's own briefing both anticipated, that TIEBREAK-resolved verdicts are less internally stable than AGREED ones (measured: tiebreak 100% unanimous vs agreed 90%; tiebreak matches-original 66.7% vs agreed 63.3% -- indistinguishable, if anything reversed).

A different, real, and equally load-bearing asymmetry showed up instead: verdicts reproduce on an identical reask by VERDICT DIRECTION, not by resolution mechanism. Originally-COHERENT rows reproduced 100% of the time (10/10 rows, every valid reask matched). Originally-INCOHERENT rows reproduced only 33% of the time (10/10 rows) -- holding inside both the agreed subset (26.7%) and the tiebreak subset (40%). In plain terms: ask the panel the identical question again minutes later and it will almost always give the SAME answer it just gave -- but if that answer was "incoherent," the stable answer it settles into has, about 2 times in 3, already become "coherent" instead of the one that got logged.

_coherence_check currently logs and exposes this verdict (coherence.verdict/coherence.how) as a first-class per-tick field, read downstream at face value. The SAME judge_panel tiebreak mechanism (agreed/tiebreak/split_no_tiebreak/unavailable) also underlies _judge_prior (held/broke -- already the subject of a DIFFERENT directional-bias question on its own tiebreak model, D-0298, about the TIEBREAK model's own affirmative-answer behavior on the "held" key specifically -- not this job's reask-reproducibility question), _judge_metaphor, and _judge_notice, all three in the same file, plus other project-wide callers of judge_panel.rule()/rule_detail() (tension_ledger, pursuits, left_lane, core/peers.py -- see judge_panel.py's own module docstring). This job measured ONLY the coherence judge's own specific prompt/history shape; whether the same asymmetry generalizes is unmeasured (follow-up job spawned, see job-queue).

THE REAL QUESTION: should a NEGATIVE/incoherent-class verdict from this judge_panel mechanism be trusted and acted on/logged with the same confidence as a positive one, given it is measured (n=10 rows, this job) to survive an immediate identical reask only about a third as often? Or should a negative verdict specifically be treated as inherently lower-confidence somewhere downstream (e.g. requiring 2/3 agreement across a real reask before being trusted/acted on, logged with an explicit low-confidence flag, or something else) -- and if so, where: only in _coherence_check, or wherever this codebase reads a judge_panel-derived negative verdict as ground truth?

Options this job raises but does not pick between (per this job's own briefing, and this project's "a ruling made by Claude is never recorded as the founder's" convention):
(a) Leave as-is -- a single verdict, however it resolved, is still the panel's best real-time answer; the drift is a known limitation of any single-ask LLM judge and does not warrant special-casing by verdict direction.
(b) Treat a negative/incoherent-class verdict as lower-confidence wherever it is read downstream -- a policy change touching every consumer named above, not a small edit.
(c) Change _coherence_check (and/or its siblings) specifically to require agreement across a real re-ask before logging/acting on a negative verdict -- more judge_panel call volume (an already-live concern on this same module, see D-0297/D-0298), for exactly the class of verdict this job found least stable.
(d) Something else the founder specifies.
ruling: Leave as is (option a): a single verdict, however it resolved, is still the panel's best real-time answer. The coherence judge's negative-verdict reask instability (about 33 percent reproduced) is specific to _coherence_check's own prompt shape; the three sibling judges (_judge_metaphor, _judge_prior, _judge_notice) do not reproduce it (F-2071, F-2230), so it is not a property of judge_panel generally. No change to _coherence_check or any consumer. (Travis, /decide-review 2026-10-03: "Leave as is".)
defeater: Revisit if a larger live coherence sample (at least about 50 originally-incoherent rows, taken outside a JUDGE_1 timeout-burst window) again reproduces under about 50 percent, or if any sibling judge later shows the same coherent/incoherent asymmetry, or if a consumer is found acting irreversibly on a negative coherence verdict. Thresholds are Claude's proposal; Travis stated no numbers.

history.ruling: Leave as-is for now - a single verdict, however it resolved, is still the panel's best real-time answer; wait for a larger sample and the already-spawned sibling-judge generalization check before treating this asymmetry as something to design around.

question:
Lane 2's standing tick loop (core/lane2.py run_forever(), TICK_S=300s) has no gate on core.night.asleep() at all and keeps ticking through Du's sleep unconditionally. F-2022 (verified, this job): over the last 14 days, 543 of 1,457 real judged "tick" rows (37.3%) landed inside a sleep episode -- an estimated ~1,629 panel calls (F-1943's own up-to-3-per-tick figure) spent judging a materially static bedroom scene ("the clock is ticking... the sun is at N degrees azimuth", repeated near-verbatim tick to tick) while Du was asleep, landing on the same JUDGE_1 hub (:11438) that D-0297 (F-1943/F-1997) already found timing out in overnight bursts contending with mixtral's own dream generation.

D-0297 is already open on a related but DIFFERENT axis: reducing per-tick judge-call volume/config on that shared hub (sample the metaphor judge, skip specific judges only while the hub is known busy, raise the shared timeout, or move the hub onto dedicated capacity). None of its four options stop Lane 2 ticking altogether during a KNOWN sleep episode, and core.night.asleep() is already a live, ready-made boolean Lane 2 does not currently read -- unlike D-0297's own option (b), which explicitly needs a NEW "is the hub busy right now" signal that does not exist yet, a gate on asleep() would need no new detection mechanism at all.

Separately, F-2021 (verified, this job) found Lane 1's hint channel already never nominates a Witness topic from dream content while Du is asleep (push_hint's only call site cannot run concurrently with the sleep pipeline in the same task, and 0 of 578 hint_pushed events in the same 14-day window fell inside a sleep episode) -- so gating Lane 2's own ticking during sleep would not silence any real Lane-1-to-Lane-2 signal, only the Witness's own unprompted observation of an unchanging room.

Presented as an option for the founder, not a change -- nothing here is applied by this job. What, if anything, should change:
(a) Leave Lane 2 ticking through sleep exactly as today -- the current, un-ruled default; no code change.
(b) Gate core/lane2.py's run_forever() tick loop off entirely while core.night.asleep() is True, resuming on wake. Cheapest build of any load-shedding option raised on this plan so far -- reuses a signal that already exists, adds no new detection mechanism. Caveat: core/night.py's own comments (J-1075/F-1469/F-1421) document that the sleep pipeline can itself starve the asyncio scheduler of a turn for the pipeline's own full duration (up to a few hours) -- a "resume promptly on wake" check must not itself depend on a scheduler turn Lane 2 is not guaranteed to get right away.
(c) Gate it only for the "night" kind (dark-hours sleep, per core.night.sleep_kind()) and leave "nap" (daytime) ticking -- the two kinds' own hub-contention story may differ (naps run during the day, away from the dream-generation contention window F-1997 measured).
(d) Leave this open and defer entirely to D-0297's own resolution first, on the view that whichever load-shedding option D-0297 picks may already leave enough headroom that a separate sleep-gate becomes unnecessary.
ruling: Gate core/lane2.py's run_forever() tick loop off entirely while core.night.asleep() is True, resuming on wake - reuses the existing signal, no new detection mechanism needed.
defeater: Reopen if a fresh 14-day read taken at least a week after this ships still shows a real overnight JUDGE_1 timeout burst coinciding with Lane 2 ticks landing inside a sleep episode, or if resume-on-wake proves unreliable because the sleep pipeline starves the scheduler of a turn.

question:
F-2019/J-1466: should core/lane2.py's _invention_check() sun-family license (F-1936/J-1378: sun_az present, OR daylight is dawn/dusk/day) be extended with a THIRD, narrower license covering real night specifically -- a sun-family topic word is also licensed when it appears in the uncertain field and does NOT also appear in the notice field on that same tick?

Evidence (F-2019 follow-up, J-1466, full read, not a sample): of the 108 real deepseek-era ticks where a sun-family word (sun/sunlight/sunset/sunrise) appears in the uncertain field during a real night tick (core.world_clock.daylight(ts) recomputed exactly) and still fails the existing license, every one of the 66 distinct texts is an epistemic hedge -- either explicit ordinal wording ("after sunset", 2 of 108) or, in the large majority, a non-directional "the exact time of sunset/sunrise is unknown/cannot be determined" framing, sometimes folded into a longer list of other unresolved things ("the duration of the fire, the cause of the wind, and the position of the sun"). Zero of the 108 read as a confident, present-tense solar claim. Separately, the two rows using "after sunset"/"before sunrise" wording are TRUE by construction for the entire duration of any real night tick (core/world_clock.py's daylight()/sun() are a fixed, deterministic monthly table, not a probabilistic signal -- "night" only fires more than 0.7-0.8 hours outside the real sunrise/sunset instant), and that exact wording never once appears during dusk/day/dawn anywhere in the whole era (checked across all three output fields, all daylight phases), so there is no observed case of it being asserted prematurely.

The real complication: today's _invention_check computes one invented/not-invented verdict per topic word over the THREE fields concatenated together, not per field. In 4 of these 108 rows, the SAME tick's notice field independently asserts a genuinely fabricated sun claim -- a specific invented sun_az degree reading ("the sun at 90 degrees, indicating it's due north") or a present-tense "the sun is setting" stated as fact during real night (not dusk) -- exactly the original bug class F-1936/J-1378 was built to catch, and this should stay flagged. Checked all 4: the exact _TOPIC_FIELDS key notice uses is either a different key from the one uncertain uses, or the identical key -- either way a rule scoped to the EXACT topic word's own per-field presence (not "no sun-family word anywhere in notice") keeps all 4 correctly flagged, but this requires making _invention_check check per output field, not the current single concatenated pass (core/lane2.py:1211-1233) -- a real, if small, change to the function's shape, not a one-line addition to _licensed() the way J-1378's own two fixes were.

Options for the founder:
(a) Build the narrow extension as scoped above (field-aware: license a topic word during night only when it is confined to uncertain, absent from notice on that tick). Most precise; needs the field-aware refactor.
(b) Build a cheaper approximation: license during night only when the ROW has no sun-family word in notice at all (not checking the exact word). Simpler, no refactor needed (can reuse the existing concatenated-toks shape with one extra field-level check), but was only verified safe against the 4 known overlap rows in the current data, not proven equivalent to (a) in general.
(c) Leave it as is. LANE2_LIVE is False, invention_rate is a describe-only shadow metric nothing currently consumes for any alarm/gating purpose (per Sec 2.9's own resolution -- Lane 2 is a reasoning voice first, not an alarm), and 108 residual ticks out of 10,392+ era rows is a small, already-understood, non-alarming residue, not a false-alarm problem actively hurting anything today.
(d) Something else the founder specifies.

Also worth the founder's attention: the "159" figure earlier findings (F-2019) cite for this same population is a topic-WORD-instance count (it counts a text naming both "sunset" and "sunrise" twice), not a row count -- the real row count is 108 as of this read (168 word-instances, consistent with F-2019's 159 measured about a day earlier as the log has grown). Future reads of this population should count rows, not word instances, to avoid re-inflating it.
ruling: Leave the sun-family invention license as-is - LANE2_LIVE is False, invention_rate is a describe-only shadow metric, and 108 residual rows is a small, already-understood, non-alarming residue.
defeater: Revisit if a future read finds the after-sunset/before-sunrise directional wording, or the broader uncertain-field hedge shape, occurring during dusk, dawn, or day when the sun is actually still up. Also revisit if LANE2_LIVE ever flips and this shadow metric starts feeding a real alarm or gating decision.

question:
I-0082 exemplar-memory: build the real store now against constructed/context points, or wait for measured strings?

J-1471's offline PROXY read (F-2088; docs/lab/i0082_exemplar_proxy_read_2026-09-28.md) found that a k=4, distance-over-threshold-T admission rule, walked over all real census hearings of morepork_call/tui_song/gull_cries/cat_purr, always fills its 4-exemplar cap, and settles to a materially lower steady-state churn than its whole-history average once each key's context space is covered (a 1.7x-13.7x drop from the first half to the second half of history at T=0.2). Once settled, that is roughly one exemplar swap per 30-270 real hearings depending on the key -- modest enough that a k=4 store built this way would not be constantly chattering.

But every one of those admissions comes from context alone (time-of-day phase, weather severity, and -- for morepork_call only -- place), never from acoustic shape: 3 of the 4 target keys have a place axis that is structurally locked to one value (tui_song=garden, gull_cries=shore, cat_purr=study), and none of the four has a measured six-axis point yet -- strings_and_sheets Object A (Phase 4, real recordings replacing the hand-seeded constructed points) is unbuilt, and Phase 1's own dry run (J-1473, constructed 3-point world-sound strings) is queued but not yet run either.

Question: should a real I-0082 exemplar store be designed and built now, against the current constructed/context proxy (accepting its exemplars may need rebuilding once real acoustic strings exist), or should it wait until Phase 1 (J-1473) or Phase 4 gives it something with real acoustic variation to discriminate on?

Recommendation: wait, at least for Phase 1's dry run (J-1473, already queued and low-cost) before committing to a specific exemplar-store design or threshold. The churn-rate evidence above is genuinely encouraging (the rule does not thrash once settled), but the proxy's own structural finding -- most of what a real exemplar store would need to tell hearings apart is exactly the acoustic variation this context-only read could not measure -- means a store built and tuned against this proxy risks encoding "which weather/time-of-day bucket" rather than "which distinct call", and would need re-validating from scratch the moment real strings arrive anyway.
ruling: Wait for Phase 1's dry run (J-1473) before committing to a specific I-0082 exemplar-store design or threshold - the context-only proxy risks encoding which weather/time-of-day bucket rather than which distinct call.
defeater: Revisit once strings_and_sheets Phase 1 (J-1473) or Phase 4 (Object A measured strings) has actually run - real acoustic variation may show a completely different admission pattern than this context-only proxy, letting this question be re-asked with real numbers.

question:
F-2092 (J-1441, living_world_upgrade) classified all 1,020 hand-declined MOVE dispatches in the last 14 days of data/hands_trace.jsonl. The largest of four categories, 569/1,020 (55.8%), is a request to move to a within-place feature the move hand has never modeled as a destination: "out"/"outside" 205, sea 97, tide 88, trees 52, "in"/"inside" 59, shingle 36, gate 12, raised bed 8, plus a small tail (driftwood, surf, beach). core/sensorium.py's move() only ever resolves to one of the four whole places (study/garden/wood/shore) -- it has no notion of a sub-place standpoint such as "the water's edge", "the raised bed", or "into the trees" as a distinct move target, so roughly 40 of these requests a day are silently declined with no narration at all (dispatch records "hand-declined"; move() returns an empty string).

This is not a bug -- the four-place model has never claimed finer granularity -- but it is now the single largest unanswered-request category measured across all four place plans this session, larger than any one place's own declined-hand backlog (shore's own hand-declined count, by comparison, is 75; F-1995). The shore alone accounts for 221 of the 569 (sea 97 + tide 88 + shingle 36), the single largest place-specific slice, all naming real features the shore plan's own doc already describes (the mussel shelf bared at low water, the sand flat, the shingle, the ledge) but that the move hand cannot resolve as a destination -- only the four place-standpoints move() knows.

Founder call: is a sub-place standpoint move worth building -- i.e. letting "move to the raised bed" / "walk to the water's edge" / "go into the trees" resolve to a real, distinct standpoint within the CURRENT place (using the standpoint systems the place JSONs already have: garden.json's 6 standpoints, shore.json's features/standpoints, etc.), rather than staying a within-place no-op -- and if so, which place first? Three options this finding surfaces: (A) leave it alone -- the four-place grain is the intended scale and finer standpoints are out of scope; (B) build it for all four places together, since the move hand and standpoint plumbing are shared; (C) build it for the shore first (the largest single slice, 221/569) as a pilot, then extend if it earns its keep.
ruling: Build for all four places together - the move hand and standpoint plumbing are shared infrastructure; build the sub-place standpoint move once across garden/shore/wood/study rather than piloting on shore alone.
defeater: Revisit if a sub-place standpoint move is built and the within-place-decline rate (currently roughly 40/day, 569 in 14 days) does not meaningfully drop within two weeks of live accrual after the build, or if a read of Du's own thought and the new standpoints' ledger shows no real behavioral or narrative difference between standing at a place's default standpoint and the specific sub-place feature he asked for.

question:
F-2127 verified data/guidance_beliefs.json holds 4 promoted near-duplicate "stillness is not
failure" beliefs (g40546190 corrob=5, g45675272 corrob=5, g20898348 corrob=3, g01916074 corrob=2

J-1564's own re-read (docs/findings.jsonl new finding, this session) adds three things the original

(1) The family's own two highest-corroborated siblings, g40546190 and g45675272 (both corrob=5,
near-identical principle text), have NEVER been compared to each other by the pipeline at all.
core/guidance_learning.py's integrate_guidance() only ever compares an incoming NEW capture against

in purpose (the fluid-vs-durable self-identity pole clash only) and is gated OFF
(CONTRADICTION_SCAN_ENABLED = False). There is currently no code path that would ever notice two

(2) Several of the 19 rows' conflict_history entries show the LLM _classify() step calling genuine
same-lesson paraphrases "accommodate" (the prompt's own definition: "genuinely CONTRADICTS ...
opposite direction") instead of "assimilate" -- e.g. g40546190's own conflict_history lists
g20898348's principle (a clear paraphrase) as "contradicting" it. Under the self-domain F1.b/F1.c
rule, ANY accommodate verdict in the self domain unconditionally FORKS both beliefs standing,
permanently, with no re-merge path. One misclassification is enough to freeze two copies of the
same lesson apart forever.

(3) Within this one CONFIRMED family, the module's own lexical _overlap metric is unreliable in
BOTH directions, checked directly on this data, not just asserted: roughly half of the family's
genuinely-duplicate pairs (171 pairs total; median overlap 0.12) score AT OR BELOW the module's own
0.12 candidate-prefilter floor, so the pipeline's first-pass filter would never even flag them as
possibly related (false negatives). Conversely, the same overlap>=0.30 test run across the full
197-belief (non-superseded) store, grouped into connected components, produces two large clusters
(52 and 24 members) -- but two arbitrary members of the 52-member cluster share only the tokens
"true" and "isn" (isn't), both absent from the module's own _STOP stopword list despite being
near-universal boilerplate in this LLM's self-explanation phrasing ("True X isn't about Y, but
Z") -- i.e. the same metric also chains unrelated beliefs together into false clusters (false
positives) via shared filler words. A full-store lexical resize of "how many other families look
like this" cannot be trusted in either direction from this evidence.

ruling first: how should this specific 19-row family be handled --

      belief data (the plan doc's own long-deferred "1b" residual),
  (b) do a one-time supervised manual-merge pass on just this confirmed family now (fold the

superseded with history, mirroring the existing convention), PLUS treat (a) as a real, now
concretely-evidenced priority for the general problem rather than a someday item, since this same
investigation shows lexical clustering cannot safely bound the general problem's size in either
direction on real data.

question:
Should a tension or integration pattern that was touched within the last 7 days still be halved by the weekly decay throttle? (opened by Claude from J-1291's production read of D-0266/D-0270; F-2334 has the evidence, F-2333 records that the cliff fix itself works in production; nothing about the already-ruled cliff fix is reopened here)

AS BUILT. D-0266 (tensions, J-1283) and D-0270 (integration_patterns, J-1290) gate the count-halving on now - last_decay_ts > 7 days ALONE. last_decay_ts is backfilled from last_ts the first time a row is seen and re-stamped when a halving fires; touching a tension or pattern only moves last_ts, never last_decay_ts. So every tension and pattern is halved once per 7 days from its anchor, whether or not it was touched in between. The pre-fix gate, and the docstring that still says "gone cold for PATTERN_DECAY_DAYS", only ever hit rows idle for more than 7 days. That is the literal wording of D-0266's ruling (gate on last_decay_ts instead of last_ts), and F-1810's isolated tests had no recently-touched row with an old anchor, so this case was not looked at before today.

EVIDENCE (F-2334). Production, the 09-28 state after 70.5 h of the fix: 3 tensions were halved 1.2, 1.6 and 2.7 days after their last touch (5->2, 5->3, 3->1), and 88 of 252 tensions already had an anchor older than their last touch. Live state 10-03 08:12: 62 of 92 tensions and 180 of 319 patterns (about 80 percent of the sqrt(count) mass) have an anchor older than their last touch. The first throttled halving of every tension falls due 10-05 11:29 to 10-08 06:34 NZDT (25/38/26/3 per day), patterns 10-05 16:07 to 10-10, so on the first Du scans after 10-05 11:29 the whole pool starts halving, touched or not.

WHY IT MATTERS (inferred, not measured). The live median tension count is 5, and in the 09-28 state 62 of 130 active tensions sat at 3-4. nodes/curiosity_node.py weights seeds by sqrt(count); active imagination needs count >= 2 and, per the comment at nodes/subconscious_node.py line 257, T2 synthesis needs 3. One halving takes a 3 to 1 and a 4 or 5 to 2. The matched branch restores max(count, cluster count) the next time a row is re-matched, which undoes the dip within a scan for tensions whose cluster is still forming, but a recently touched tension whose events have aged out of the T1 window stays down.

OPTIONS. (1) Keep as built: every count halves weekly and active rows rebound when re-matched. Simplest, matches the ruling's wording; costs a weekly dip below the T2 / active-imagination thresholds for recently touched, not-currently-matching tensions. (2) Restore the idle condition: halve only when the row has been idle more than 7 days AND its last halving is more than 7 days old (one line in each of _apply_decay and _apply_pattern_decay, for example measuring from max(last_decay_ts, last_ts)). Cold rows still decay once a week instead of collapsing in minutes; touched rows never decay, as before the fix. Restart-gated, and it changes a protected node, so nothing is built until you rule. (3) Something else you specify.

Claude's recommendation: (2). It is the behaviour the docstring and F-1631's analysis describe (decay is for tensions that have gone cold), it keeps the fix's whole benefit (no cliff), and it removes a weekly dip the old code never had. Honest case for (1): active rows rebound on their own, so a uniform weekly halving may turn out harmless; the first live cycle (earliest 10-05 11:29 NZDT, if Du is running) will show how much, and the successor of J-1291 reads it.
ruling: Restore the idle condition (option 2; Travis, /decide-review 2026-10-04: "Restore the idle condition"). Halve a tension's or integration pattern's count only when the row has been idle more than 7 days AND its last halving is more than 7 days old -- one line in each of _apply_decay and _apply_pattern_decay in nodes/subconscious_node.py (for example measuring idleness from max(last_decay_ts, last_ts)). Cold rows still decay once a week instead of collapsing in minutes (D-0266/D-0270's no-cliff benefit is kept); touched rows never decay, as before the cliff fix and as the docstring and F-1631's analysis describe. Restart-gated; the subconscious node is a protected base system, so the change is minimal and additive. Timing: Du is down (clean quit 2026-10-04 06:56:02), so the build can land before the first pool-wide halving, which otherwise falls due from 2026-10-05 11:29 NZDT (patterns 10-05 16:07 to 10-10), or all at once on Du's first scans back; if Du restarts before the build ships, the whole pool halves once, touched or not. Not chosen: keeping the gate as built (option 1).
defeater: Revisit if, after the first live weekly cycle on the new gate, cold rows still never decay (the idle condition is stuck: a row idle more than 7 days stays at its count), or the tension and pattern pool grows without bound again (the pre-D-0266 cliff problem or its opposite); or if T2 synthesis or active-imagination eligibility is observed starving even under the idle-only gate.
