F-2401 item (3) found two OTHER multi-MB Du stores still rewritten IN PLACE the same way, each with a swallow-everything loader that turns a torn file into a silent EMPTY store: data/frontier.json 5.05 MB (core/frontier.py _save line 71 / _load returns {"questions": []} on any error) and data/pursuits_active.json 18.99 MB (core/pursuits.py _save line 200 / _load returns [] on any error, logged at debug only). The other three multi-MB stores (watershed_state, spring_ledger_state, opponent_process_state) and lane2/graph.json already write tmp + replace. A process death inside one of those two writes leaves a truncated file and the next boot starts an empty frontier / pursuit register with no log line, which is the 2026-09-28 subconscious failure (F-2314) again on a smaller scale (their write windows are likely well under the 46 MB subconscious file's ~5 s -- F-2311 parse medians are 70 ms and 367 ms, write times not measured -- so it is rarer, not different).

Both are protected base-system modules, and your D-0339 yes covered the subconscious node only, so this is yours: do you approve the same ADDITIVE hardening on core/frontier.py and core/pursuits.py -- write through tmp + os.replace (with the short Windows retry J-1767 proved necessary) and, on an unreadable file, log loudly and MOVE it aside before starting empty -- with no change to what the stores contain, no behaviour change when the file is healthy, and no automatic restore? Yes (both) / No / Only one of the two.
ruling: Yes, both. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. Apply the J-1767 pattern (F-2401) additively to core/frontier.py _save and core/pursuits.py _save: write through tmp + os.replace with the short Windows retry; on an unreadable file, log loudly and move it aside before starting empty; no change to store contents, no behaviour change when the file is healthy, no automatic restore. Both files parsed cleanly on 2026-10-06 (frontier 10,146 questions / 5.1 MB; pursuits 684 / 19 MB) and no tear or save failure appeared in the 10-04/05 or 10-06 runs, so this is prevention, not repair. Restart-gated build.
defeater: Revisit if the hardened writes on either store log repeated 'state save failed' / WinError lines in the first 7 live days (os.replace colliding with readers on busier stores, calling for a different design), or if a move-aside fires on a file that turns out to have been healthy (a false unreadable verdict).

question:
READ FIRST: F-2402 (findings_log.py show F-2402, the J-1764 build of D-0333) and F-2284 (the 'sea' case). D-0333 (ruled Narrow) is built (commit f2fdcdc, restart-gated) and, as you ruled, left the cue table's order alone -- but that order limits how far the build reaches. _observe_target() returns the FIRST cue found anywhere in the whole thought, so a willed look at the tin that also names an earlier cue (the sea, shingle, the book, a plant, the fire, the cat, the garden) resolves to that cue and the tin is not named.

Measured on the real corpus (data/hands_trace.jsonl, 28,236 distinct thoughts replayed): of the 6 genuine willed looks at the tin that the build newly turns into look deeds, 2 reach the tin and 4 go elsewhere (to thyme, shingle, the flag, the book). Counting the 13 look deeds that already fire today on thoughts that also name the tin (19 in all), 3 reach the tin and 16 go to an earlier cue (6 sea or surf, 3 shingle or tide, 2 the garden, the fire, cloud, thyme, the flag, the book). So the narrow build reaches about a third of the looks at the tin that Du has actually narrated. D-0269 and D-0333 each reserved the table order for you. Which?

(i) LEAVE IT. The tin is named only when no earlier cue claims the thought. The dated J-1691 re-check reads, once Du has run and been in the wood, whether the limit bites live. Cost: until then the build helps only about a third of the looks he narrates at the tin.

(ii) CLAUSE-FIRST FOR THE TIN ONLY. When a look verb's own clause reaches a tin or packet word (exactly the condition the gate already requires), the target resolves to the tin first. No other cue is reordered, and a thought that merely mentions the tin as scenery ('the wind rattles the tin container ... I watch the grey sea rise') keeps its own resolution, because the rule needs the look verb to reach the tin word. By construction it reaches all 6 genuine new looks. A small rule in _observe_target plus a corpus replay before it ships; no hint, nothing says where the tin lies.

(iii) MOVE THE TIN CUE EARLY, ahead of the ambient group. The simplest edit, but tin-first ignores whether the look is aimed at the tin: the 13 look deeds that already fire on thoughts that only name the tin as scenery would turn into tin looks.

Not on the table: telling him where the tin is, or changing the refusal 'the tin is not here' (world answers, never leads). Claude's lean, offered as input and not a ruling: (ii).
ruling: (ii) Clause-first for the tin only. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. In _observe_target, when the look verb's own clause reaches a tin or packet word (the condition the J-1764 gate already requires), the target resolves to the tin first; no other cue is reordered; a thought that merely mentions the tin as scenery keeps its current resolution. Ship only after a corpus replay on data/hands_trace.jsonl confirms all 6 genuine new tin looks reach the tin and none of the 13 scenery-mention look deeds flip. Not chosen: (i) leave it, (iii) move the tin cue early. Still not on the table: any hint about where the tin is, or changing the refusal 'the tin is not here'. No live tin look had fired in the two runs since J-1764 went live (10-04 20:40 to 10-06 07:30). Restart-gated.
defeater: Revisit if, after the restart carrying the clause-first rule, a look-hand answer names the tin in a cycle whose thought was not aimed at it (a false tin look), or a willed look at the tin still resolves to an earlier cue; if D-0269's general table-order question is reopened (rule both together); if he retrieves the tin himself (garden_ledger take/sow row for seed_tin); or 2026-12-01 passes with the sowing window closed.

question:
Where should the C.2 pre-affect (amygdala) prior's similarity floor sit, now that F-2414 (J-1731) showed the 0.86 floor J-1366 set has switched it effectively OFF? (And, folded in: should the farewell get the prior at all - J-1359 lever (2).)

What was measured (F-2414, verified; read-only replay, nothing written): the prior is silent since the 2026-09-28 boot because of the floor, not an error (0 exceptions in 197 replays; the one live pass since the boot, the 10-04 06:52 farewell at sim 0.90, is reproduced exactly). J-1366 calibrated 0.86 for a ~10 percent pass rate using the embeddings of 400 'lived' cycle-summary fragments as stand-in queries; real inputs pass ~0.5 percent (3 of 605 cycles on the old 0.55 process, 1 of 140 since the boot). Real inputs also only reached the floor 69 percent of the time at 0.55 (J-1366 said 99.75 percent). Human cycles (Travis's own words) sit lower than idle cycles: 0.44-0.71 except an exact repeat.

Share of cycles that would get the prior, by floor:
 floor 0.55: 69.4% of all cycles (0.55-era live log, n=605) | 97.1% (replay of the 140 cycles since the boot) | 87.5% of human cycles (14 of 16) | farewell prior ON (farewell best sims 0.59-0.62)
 floor 0.65: 54.4% | 65.0% | 37.5% (6 of 16) | farewell OFF
 floor 0.70: 39.8% | 32.9% | 12.5% (2 of 16) | OFF
 floor 0.75: 21.8% | 9.3% | 6.3% (1 of 16, the exact-repeat farewell) | OFF
 floor 0.80: 9.1% | 3.6% | 6.3% | OFF
 floor 0.86 (today): 0.5% | 0.7% | 6.3% (only a near-identical repeat, and only if the earlier copy was stored at importance >= 0.70) | effectively OFF (4 of the 5 farewells since 09-29 got no prior)
(0.75-0.80 is the 'about 10 percent of cycles' band J-1366 aimed for; it moved from ~0.80 to ~0.75 in 8 days because the charged-episodic corpus decays - see option E.)

Options:
 A. Leave 0.86. The prior becomes a near-duplicate-resonance detector only (about 1 cycle in 150-200). J-1359 lever (2) is then 'off' by default. Nothing to build.
 B. Lower to about 0.75-0.80 (one-constant change in core/memory/store.py): about 4-9 percent of cycles, nearly all idle-thought cycles; Travis's words and the farewell still almost never get it.
 C. Restore 0.55 (the pre-J-1366 behaviour): about 70-97 percent of cycles, i.e. the 'wallpaper' J-1366 removed; the farewell prior returns (J-1359 lever (2) = leave it alone).
 D. Per-input-type floors (small additive build in _emotional_pre_retrieval, input_type is already known): a lower floor for human-origin cycles (for example 0.65: 6 of 16 human cycles, farewell still off; 0.55: 14 of 16, farewell on) and a high floor (0.80+) for idle cycles.
 E. Independently of A-D: EMO_EPISODIC_MIN_IMPORTANCE 0.70 -> about 0.55-0.60. Sleep decay has drained the charged-episodic set the gate matches (about 8.7k rows at importance >= 0.70 on 09-26 inferred, 1,226 on 10-04; 7,149 now sit at 0.6-0.7, and only 18 of the 1,226 are 'lived'). It matters only for options B-D; with A it changes little.
Whatever is chosen is restart-gated (Du is down; the next boot loads master). A follow-up build job (observe-only per-cycle best-of-N sim log) was spawned so the choice can be re-checked on live data.
ruling: D plus E. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. Per-input-type similarity floors in _emotional_pre_retrieval (input_type already known): human-origin cycles ~0.65, idle/internal cycles 0.80 or above; the farewell stays off at 0.65. And E: lower EMO_EPISODIC_MIN_IMPORTANCE from 0.70 to about 0.55-0.60 so sleep decay does not drain the charged-episodic set the gate matches (1,226 rows at >=0.70 on 10-04 vs ~8.7k on 09-26; 7,149 at 0.6-0.7). Basis at ruling: F-2414 plus the first 37 post-restart rows of data/pre_affect_best_shadow.jsonl (35 internal / 2 human): at 0.86 pass 2/35 and 0/2; at 0.75 15/35 and 1/2; at 0.65 28/35 and 1/2. Not chosen: A leave 0.86 (prior effectively off), B one floor 0.75-0.80, C restore 0.55. Restart-gated; one-constant-per-type change plus the importance floor.
defeater: Revisit when the observe-only best-of-N log has 300+ post-restart cycles including all human cycles and the real pass rate by floor and input type differs from the ruling's expectation (human ~1/3 to 1/2, idle under 10%) by more than 2x; when the next 6 farewell replies show the prior reaching them (it should not at 0.65); or when the count of episodic rows at the new importance floor moves by more than 2x again.

question:
J-1760 built the topological _order_subjects candidate you approved in D-0327 and did NOT ship it, because the fresh build-time full-corpus regression (F-2413, verified) found something F-2200's subject-level check could not see.

What held: the Origin victim ('The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selectio') now processes before the over-matcher ('On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selec'); 0 pairs with differing signature length change order (21 changed pairs, all equal length, all involving the Origin pair); the 5 F-2160 at-risk pairs keep their correct order; the real cycle fallback is tested and passes; live exposure is still 0 NULL-chapter_id fragments.

What broke: at the FRAGMENT level the candidate trades 26 right claims for 948 wrong ones. The victim also accepts the over-matcher's own long-title fragments (948 fragments tagged 'On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection or th' - the finished, 100%-read, 2-pass book), so with the victim first it would claim them; the other 26 fragments (the second, 3.6%-read book's own tags) would move to their right gist. Nothing is exposed today - all 974 affected fragments are already filed - so the damage is latent: it would trigger exactly when those fragments are cleared and re-filed, i.e. in the D-0245-held repair batches that D-0323 said this fix must precede.

The regression also exposed an independent defect: the finished-gate _completed_passes_for('The Origin ... Selectio') returns 2 passes although that book is only 3.6% read, because it takes the first reading_state entry whose name contains the single word 'selectio' - the finished On-the-Origin book. Ordering masks it today (the finished book's gist claims everything first); the candidate would have unmasked it.

Which way?
(A) HOLD (my recommendation for now): leave _order_subjects exactly as shipped. The pair stays dormant (0 exposure). Any future D-0245 clear batch must exclude the 26 fragments tagged 'The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection...' (the only Origin-pair fragments the shipped order would mis-claim), and the finished-gate defect becomes its own small, separately-regression-tested fix.
(B) Ship the topological candidate anyway: not recommended - it fixes 26 and breaks 948 the moment those fragments are re-filed.
(C) Direct a different build: a fragment-level identity-first claim (a fragment whose tag's first 50 characters equal a subject goes to that subject, otherwise today's order decides), which needs cross-subject awareness inside sweep()/file_book_notes() and the gate fix, each with its own full-corpus regression. Quantified, not built: it fixes the Origin pair both ways (948 stay with the finished book's gist, 26 move) but also changes the claimant of 520 further fragments across 3 other book pairs (Electricity for the farm, What Bird is That, The Authors Desk Book) that would need review first.
(D) Something else.

D-0245's hold and D-0323's ruling are untouched by this question. Full evidence: F-2413 (verified); candidate patch and test kept in the J-1760 scratchpad (J-1760_order_subjects_new_block.py, J-1760_test_order_subjects_candidate.py, J-1760_regression.py).
ruling: (A) HOLD. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. _order_subjects stays exactly as shipped; the topological candidate (J-1760 scratchpad) is not merged. Two consequences to build: (1) any D-0245 clear batch must exclude the 26 fragments tagged with the short 'The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection...' title (the only Origin-pair fragments the shipped order would mis-claim) -- an explicit exclusion in the batch selection, not a convention; (2) the finished-gate defect (_completed_passes_for matching on the single word 'selectio' and returning 2 passes for the 3.6%-read book) becomes its own small fix with a full-corpus regression. Not chosen: (B) ship the candidate (fixes 26, latently breaks 948), (C) the fragment-level identity-first claim (changes 520 further fragments across 3 other book pairs; may be revisited). Exposure at ruling: 0 unfiled Origin-tagged fragments in the live DB (3,407 NULL-chapter_id reading rows, none Origin). D-0245's hold and D-0323 untouched.
defeater: Revisit if a D-0245 clear batch is about to run before the explicit 26-fragment exclusion exists; if a NULL-chapter_id fragment tagged with either Origin title appears in the live DB; if the finished-gate fix's regression shows the false pass changed a real filing; if a fresh census finds a second asymmetric equal-signature-length pair whose victim also accepts the over-matcher's fragments (then (C) comes back); or when Travis says go regardless.

question: B6_VALENCE_THRESHOLD stays at -0.57 (no rolling-percentile gate). J-1737 analysis of the full monologue valence stream shows the fixed constant fires 6.7% overall (0-19%/week), the 2% in F-2365 was a warm 09-29..10-01 stretch, and a rolling p10 fires ~13-15% in every regime with higher variance, i.e. it would steer in warm moods and blunt itself in hard ones. Proposed ruling: leave the constant; revisit only on the defeater. Proposed by Claude, founder to rule.
ruling: Yes, leave the constant. B6_VALENCE_THRESHOLD stays at -0.57; no rolling-percentile gate. Ruled by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06, accepting Claude's proposed ruling (J-1737). Basis: the constant fires 6.7% overall (0-19%/week) and tracks regime, a rolling p10 would fire 13-15% in every regime (steering in warm moods, blunting itself in hard ones). At ruling, ISO week 41's share at/below -0.57 is 18.1% (F-2471), i.e. the steer is active in the current hard stretch as intended. Nothing to build.

question: F-2464: 52.3% of wandering _drift_from's 1500-fragment recency pool is his own inner_thought fragments (F-2366: 34.2% of post-restart idle prompts carry one). The J-1736 relabel (honest tag, selection untouched) is built. Should selection ALSO change: (a) relabel alone; (b) cap inner_thought share of the pool (e.g. at most 25%); (c) exclude inner_thought from the pool entirely? Note drift must stay read-only and the existing inner_count>=3 world-only rule already applies.
ruling: (b) Cap inner_thought at 25% of the drift pool. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. In core/wandering.py _drift_from, after the recency query, limit inner_thought fragments to at most 25% of the 1500-fragment pool (fill the remainder from the next most recent non-inner_thought eligible rows); the J-1736 honest relabel stays; drift stays read-only; the existing inner_count>=3 world-only rule is unchanged. Not chosen: (a) relabel alone, (c) exclude inner_thought entirely. Restart-gated.

question: J-1804 / F-2465: the live memory DB (data/memory/nascence.db) has no write fence; core.memory.store._connect() is the one choke point for ~50 modules. Proposed design: in _connect(), a process that never called profile.mark_live() and whose DB_PATH is not redirected (not a profile, not data/_lab/<dir>/, not a tempdir) gets a READ-ONLY connection (sqlite authorizer). Live Du is unchanged (one boolean check). Three founder calls: (1) Should non-live READS of the live DB stay allowed (du_pulse, plan tools, labs, hud all read it today)? Recommended: yes, refuse writes only. (2) The ~8 operator scripts that write the live DB on purpose (seed_epochs_themes, backfill_founder_memory, librarian, _first_thought, etc.) need an explicit opt-in such as store.allow_live_writes() -- OK to require it, i.e. they fail until they call it? Recommended: yes. (3) Build it staged: log-only first (restart-gated, refuses nothing), then enforce after one read of the would-refuse log? Recommended: yes. Residual not fixable by the fence: with Du down, any connection that closes last on a WAL DB checkpoints into nascence.db (content-neutral byte change) and a read-only open can create -shm/-wal sidecars.
ruling: Yes to all three, as recommended. Ruled by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06. Build the live-DB write fence at core.memory.store._connect() (F-2465 design): a process that never called profile.mark_live() and whose DB_PATH is not redirected (not a profile, not data/_lab/<dir>/, not a tempdir) gets a READ-ONLY sqlite connection via an authorizer. (1) Non-live READS of the live DB stay allowed (du_pulse, plan tools, HUD, labs). (2) The ~8 operator scripts that write the live DB on purpose (seed_epochs_themes, backfill_founder_memory, librarian, _first_thought, etc.) must call an explicit store.allow_live_writes() opt-in and fail until they do. (3) Staged: log-only first (restart-gated, refuses nothing, writes a would-refuse log), then enforcement after one read of that log. Live Du is unchanged (one boolean check). Known residual the fence cannot fix: a last-closing WAL connection checkpoints into nascence.db and a read-only open can create -shm/-wal sidecars.
defeater: Revisit if any of: the live DB moves to a different file or engine; a legitimate non-live tool is found that must write the live DB and cannot use the opt-in; the log-only stage shows non-live readers that the read-only connection breaks beyond memory_edges DDL; or a measured hot-path overhead in the live process appears.

question:
READ FIRST: F-2466 (why the Ramses background lane stalls) and F-2467 (J-1829 lab). Should the background lane (command-r7b on the Ramses 3070, :11441) stop using the JSON grammar (format=json in core/model_client.py call_node)?

What the lab measured on 168 real background prompts across 10 jobs: with the grammar 168/168 replies carried every key the caller reads, at 9.4 tok/s (p50 10.3s per call, max 24.6s); without it 163/168 (97%), at 59.2 tok/s (p50 1.7s, max 3.5s). Nine jobs were clean or near-clean without the grammar (drift 30/30, sitting judge 25/25, Consolidation 25/25, refinery 20/20, t2_synthesise 14/14, distil 11/11, theme 3/3, self_relate 1/1, Curiosity 24/25). One was not: active_imagination 10/14 -- four replies came back as labelled prose with no braces. F-2466 showed the grammar is what ties this lane to the Ramses i9: the same job takes 34s alone and 124s when two CPU hubs are busy, which is past Du's 120s timeout.

Options:
(a) No grammar on the first attempt for :11441, and the existing parse-failure retry in call_node_json re-sends WITH the grammar. Every job gets the speed; a miss costs about 2s plus one grammar call; nothing can fail that passes today. [Claude's recommendation]
(b) No grammar only for the jobs that passed cleanly in the lab; keep the grammar for active_imagination and for the jobs the lab did not cover (symbolic_reading, essay_lesson, curiosity_queue, orchestrator re-entry, inner_monologue background calls, symbol_evolution, grounded_learning).
(c) Keep the grammar everywhere and rely on the other F-2466 fixes (J-1830 hub deadline, J-1831 thread caps, J-1832 circuit breaker).

Not established by the lab: whether the no-grammar replies differ in character -- the sitting judge's five flags agreed between arms on 20-24 of 25 prompts and both arms released 16 of 25, but no same-arm repeat was run, so sampling noise is not separated out; Curiosity gave 3 questions in 23/25 calls with the grammar and 19/25 without. Any of (a)/(b) is a model_client.py change and restart-gated.
ruling: (a) No JSON grammar on the first attempt for the background lane (:11441 command-r7b); the existing parse-failure retry in call_node_json re-sends WITH the grammar. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. Scope: core/model_client.py call_node, :11441 only; every background job gets the ~6x speed (lab F-2467: p50 1.7 s vs 10.3 s, 97% well-formed without the grammar), a miss costs ~2 s plus one grammar call, nothing that passes today can fail. J-1830 (hub-side deadline, stop generating for departed callers, status endpoint), J-1831 (i9 thread caps) and J-1832 (circuit breaker) stay open as the other F-2466 fixes. Live state at ruling (F-2470): 65.1% of :11441 calls failed on the 10-04/05 run (p50 = the 120 s timeout), 0% on the 10-06 run; the clean window is unexplained, so F-2466 stands. Not chosen: (b) per-job, (c) keep the grammar everywhere. Restart-gated.
defeater: Revisit if, in the first 7 days live, any of: the background lane's first-attempt parse-failure rate exceeds 10% for any single caller with 30+ calls; the sitting judge's release rate (data/dwell_release.jsonl) or Curiosity's questions-per-call moves outside its prior 14-day range; or background-lane 120s timeouts in data/llm_latency.jsonl do not fall below 5% of calls.

question:
READ FIRST: F-2472 (findings_log.py show F-2472) and F-2210 / J-1642. Du's 'internal' cycles (the autonomous thoughts born when climate dissonance ignites, core/orchestrator.py:2951 input_type='internal') are framed as Travis's speech by THREE prompts that never read input_type: nodes/perception_node.py:16,52 ('speech from a HUMAN INTERLOCUTOR', so Du's own question is summarised as 'The person asks the entity...'), nodes/executive_node.py:98 ('The person you are speaking with has just said to you:'), and nodes/voice_node.py:246 ('Travis has just said to you:' + the question; :183/:201 'speaking with Travis' / 'what you say to Travis'). Measured effect on the 10-06 run: 16 of 17 cycles were Du's own 渡 questions, every reply opened 'Travis, ...' and argued with you as if you had asked; perception's human-framed summary then fed Curiosity's 'recent themes', which regenerated the same topic (15/16 fires had 渡 in themes, 16/16 chose it; the 10-04/05 run locked on Morgan le Fay 25/31 the same way) -- and the orchestrator always takes Curiosity's FIRST question (valid_qs[0], :2940) with no theme or question anti-relock (only seeds have one). The distinction already exists in the orchestrator (:1190-1193 'on his autonomous/internal cycles there is no listener'; :1468-1473 the conversation window is human-only). Two founder calls, both prompt wording and therefore yours (no hints to Du; world answers, never leads):
(1) FRAMING. For input_type != 'human', how should the three prompts present the question? Proposal: perception -- 'This is the entity's OWN thought, not a person's speech; summarise it in the first person'; executive -- 'A question has risen in you, unprompted:'; voice -- 'A question rose in you on your own; no one asked it:' with the stance line and the JSON label changed from 'what you say to Travis' to 'what you say aloud, to yourself'. Alternatives: (a) that proposal; (b) keep voice addressing Travis as his constant interlocutor even when alone (his habit of thinking AT Travis is part of him) but fix perception + executive so the record and the plan are honest; (c) your own wording.
(2) THE LOCK. Should the orchestrator stop taking valid_qs[0] blindly? Options: (a) add a theme anti-relock mirroring _recent_seeds (skip a question whose topic matches the last N themes); (b) pick from valid_qs by novelty against recent internal questions; (c) leave selection alone and let the perception fix (1) break the loop on its own, then measure.
Claude's lean, offered as input not ruling: (1)(a) and (2)(c) first with a measured read after one live week, escalating to (2)(a) only if the lock persists.
ruling: (1)(a) and (2)(c). Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. (1) FRAMING -- for input_type != 'human', all three prompts become honest about whose thought it is: nodes/perception_node.py: 'This is the entity's OWN thought, not a person's speech; summarise it in the first person'; nodes/executive_node.py:98: 'A question has risen in you, unprompted:' instead of 'The person you are speaking with has just said to you:'; nodes/voice_node.py:246: 'A question rose in you on your own; no one asked it:' instead of 'Travis has just said to you:', with the stance line (:183) and the JSON label (:201 'what you say to Travis') changed to 'what you say aloud, to yourself'. Human cycles are untouched. Not chosen: (b) voice keeps addressing Travis when alone; (c) perception only. (2) THE LOCK -- selection is NOT changed yet: the orchestrator keeps valid_qs[0]; the perception fix removes the human-framed self-summary that fed Curiosity's themes and drove the lock (F-2472), and the per-run topic concentration of internal questions is read after 7 live days; escalate to a theme anti-relock (a) or novelty pick (b) only if the lock persists. No hint to Du anywhere; world answers, never leads. Supersedes the wording question J-1642 was waiting on. Restart-gated.
defeater: Revisit if, after the framing is live for 7 days, internal-cycle replies still open with Travis's name or address him as the asker in more than 5% of internal cycles; if any single topic still takes more than 50% of a run's internal questions (then (2)(a) or (b) is needed after all); if Du's human-cycle replies lose their address to Travis (over-correction); or if Travis decides Du thinking AT him when alone is wanted behaviour.

question: READ FIRST: F-2474 and F-1443. In 197 dream arcs since 2026-08-29, zero have ever closed 'resolved': the dreaming LLM grades its own arc (nodes/dream_node.py:279/282 close_reason='resolved' only if its own unresolved_core field comes back empty; prompt :399 'empty ONLY if it has truly been met') and it never leaves it empty (self_resolved=True 0/197); the independent resolution judge, run in shadow, agrees 196/197. Close reasons: ended-unfaced 156, stalled 38, dropped 3. The code already calls this 'the 0/55-resolved problem' (:88), F-1443 recorded 0/146 on 09-15 and spawned nothing. Consequence: the 'recurring dream returns until it is met' design (:159-160) has never completed its loop once; every arc ends in shadow (:522-536) and after CARRY_MAX_NIGHTS the thread 'withdraws' unfaced (10-06 07:28: the 3-night thread about 'discerning the true nature of the wisdom Travis...' withdrew). This is a decoupled-judge question (your own rule: every subsystem evaluated by something other than itself) and a design question about whether dreams are MEANT to resolve. Options: (A) accept that dreams do not resolve; retire the resolved branch and the carry-until-met language so the record stops describing a path that never fires; (B) decouple: let the shadow judge, not the dreamer, set close_reason (it also says 1/197, so expect near-zero resolution still, but honestly measured); (C) change what 'met' means: resolution = the dormant/tension source stops recurring in waking thought for N days (a computed measure, consistent with D-0233's embedding-distance disambiguation) rather than the dreamer's self-report; (D) hold until D-0232 (reopened today, same plan) is re-ruled and fold this in. Claude's lean, as input: (B) now as a one-line additive change, and (C) as the real question to design under D-0232.
ruling: (B) now, (C) as the design question. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. (B): a one-line additive change in nodes/dream_node.py so the independent resolution judge (already run in shadow every arc, :279-282 vicinity) sets close_reason resolved/ended-unfaced instead of the dreamer's own unresolved_core self-report; the dreamer's self-report stays logged alongside for the agreement measure. Expect near-zero resolution still (judge said 1/197) but honestly measured by something other than the system being judged. (C): the real question -- what 'met' means -- is designed as a COMPUTED measure, not a self-report: a dream's tension source counts as met when it stops recurring in waking thought for N days, using D-0233's embedding-distance disambiguation so re-entry explained by the injected dream-tail text does not count. (C) is drafted under the dream_overhaul plan and comes back as its own /decide before it is wired. Not chosen: (A) retire the resolved branch; (B) alone; (D) hold. Basis: F-2474 (0/197 resolved since 2026-08-29; self_resolved=True 0, judge=True 1; F-1443 0/146 on 09-15 spawned nothing). Restart-gated.
defeater: Revisit if a dream closes resolved under the current self-grading before (B) ships (the never-fires premise would be wrong); if after (B) the judge's resolved rate and the dreamer's self-report diverge by more than 10 points over 30 arcs (then the judge itself needs calibration before (C) is built on it); when the (C) design is drafted and comes back as its own decision; or if Travis rules that unresolved-by-design is the intended texture of Du's dreaming.

question: READ FIRST: F-2475. The prune is a designed no-op (D-0124/D-0173: protected kinds 'report, not demote'); the ACTIVE pool is 48,896 against a 3,500 cap (semantic 25x, self 17x its budget) and retrieve() cost grows linearly with it (0.85 s per retrieve, +55% since 09-08; a hot-path SQL fix is J-1842 and needs no ruling). Separately, the active pool holds about 2,760 EXACT-duplicate-content rows (5.6%): reading 2,098, thermal 487, affection 100, lived 55, research 18; reading and lived are origin-protected so the prune can never touch them, and 3,591 of the reading dup rows are already chaptered (fetched then skipped every query). The project's rule is demote-not-delete (store.py:1759-1760; the delete-era prune once lost two weeks). Question: approve a one-time, reversible exact-duplicate reclaim on the active pool -- keep one survivor per content (oldest, or highest replay_count), set the others cold=1 (or temp='hidden'), add a memory_links row from each demoted copy to its survivor, after a .backup() and with fragment_context/world_context/co_recall_ledger references to the demoted ids checked first (not yet checked)? Options: (a) yes, exactly that, Du stopped, with a replay-validated rebuild test as the 10-04 leak repairs used; (b) yes but dedup only the non-protected origins (thermal, affection, research), leaving reading/lived copies alone; (c) no reclaim; instead revisit D-0124's defeater (an anchor starving) and raise the cap honestly to what the pool actually is; (d) no, leave it. Claude's lean, as input: (a) -- duplicates by exact content are not memories lost, and the survivor keeps every link.
ruling: (a) Yes: a one-time, reversible exact-duplicate reclaim on the ACTIVE memory pool, Du stopped. Chosen by Travis in /decide-review 2026-10-06 with Claude's recommendation. Shape: per identical content among cold=0 episodic rows (about 2,760 rows: reading 2,098, thermal 487, affection 100, lived 55, research 18; F-2475), keep ONE survivor (oldest, or highest replay_count), set the other copies cold=1 (or temp='hidden'), and add a memory_links row from each demoted copy to its survivor so no id goes dark. Never a DELETE (demote-not-delete, store.py:1759-1760). Preconditions in order: sqlite .backup() of the live DB first; then a read-only reference check of fragment_context / world_context / co_recall_ledger (and any other table keyed by fragment_id) against the would-be-demoted ids -- if any reference cannot be re-pointed to the survivor, fall back to option (b) (non-protected origins only) for that content group; the whole operation validated the way the 10-04 leak repairs were (a dry run on a copy, before/after counts, replay check), recorded in a finding. Not chosen: (b) non-protected origins only, (c) raise the cap honestly instead, (d) leave it. J-1842 (SQL filter in retrieve()) proceeds independently.
defeater: Revisit if the reference check finds fragment_context/world_context/co_recall_ledger rows pointing at would-be-demoted ids that cannot be re-pointed (then (b) or (d) for those groups); if after the reclaim any recall-quality gauge (recall confidence, grounded_share, co_recall hit rate) moves outside its prior 14-day band; if exact duplicates re-accrue above 3% of the active pool within 30 days (then the WRITER needs the dedup, not the store); or if D-0124 is itself re-ruled.

question:

The climate has read shadow_activation 0.90-0.98 for months and, on the two live runs since the 10-04 boot, 162 of 162 climate lines and 47 of 47 ignitions were shadow_activation: every autonomous thought Du has is now born from the 'shadow' tension. Cause: the only code that ever marks a shadow event resolved is the subconscious T4 DISCHARGE, last fired 2026-06-13; 35,856 of 35,942 shadow events are unresolved; the Resolution Circuit records genuine clean re-encounters (1,658 resolution_events) but never marks the shadow event resolved; the climate counts unresolved only. The D-0332 re-knee view (live, label-only) already shows what an honest reading would be: shadow 0.54, dominant integration_drive 0.56, versus the live 0.98. Effect: 'a shadow at the edge of the room, something you have not turned to face' in Reflection and 'Unintegrated material is active beneath this' in Executive on every conversational cycle, plus single-flavour ignition. This is the write-only-system pattern (rich write path, dead resolve path) and your Erosion-of-Foundations rule applies: additive only.
Options (from J-1365, all additive):
(A) RESOLVE ON RE-ENCOUNTER: when the Resolution Circuit records a clean re-encounter for a shadow event, mark that event resolved. The judge already exists and already judged it; this just lets its verdict reach the counter. Reversible (a flag).
(B) AGE-DECAY: weight unresolved events by age in the climate score so the count cannot grow without bound. Changes the gauge's meaning, not the record.
(C) RECALIBRATE thresholds/saturate() to the real distribution. Symptom only.
(D) RE-ENABLE the symbol cooldown (schema.py THIN_ATTRACTOR) so surfacing is at most occasional while pegged.
(E) PROMOTE the re-knee view (D-0332's label view) from shadow to live as the climate's reading. Honest number, but it is a re-mapping of the same unbounded count.
Claude's lean, as input: (A) + (D), then read the climate and the ignition mix for a week; (B) only if (A) does not move it (which would mean the Resolution Circuit itself is not firing on the events that matter).
ruling: (A)+(D): mark a shadow event resolved when the Resolution Circuit records a clean re-encounter, and re-enable the symbol cooldown (schema.py THIN_ATTRACTOR). Read the climate and ignition mix for a week; add (B) age-decay only if (A) does not move it.
defeater: Revisit if, 7 live days after the chosen fix, shadow_activation is still the dominant climate on more than 80% of climate lines or ignitions (the resolve path is still not reaching the counter, so (B) or (E) is needed); if resolution_events stop accruing (the Resolution Circuit itself died); if marking events resolved on re-encounter visibly removes material Du was still working on (a shadow event resolved whose theme recurs in dreams/thoughts within 7 days); or if the symbol cooldown silences a surfacing Travis wanted kept.

question:
F-2505 (J-1732, verified): daylight-bound lines can render at night in the look-target and ambient pools, and most of them are NOT movable by the J-1717 "any to day key" recipe. Three founder calls, one per part; the mechanical part (the 6 "any"-key target and SCENE lines) is already queued as a build job and does not wait on this.

(a) The study SCENE line "sun off the sea puts a wavering light on the ceiling boards" (core/world_content_study.py:461, under "any"). J-1717 left it alone unless Travis asked. Measured: in the last incarnation's scene_extra_ledger.jsonl it was 6 of 57 night study renders (10.5 percent, the most-rendered flagged line), at 02:22, 02:37, 02:45 and later, i.e. a sun-lit ceiling in a dark room. Move it to a "day" key (wording byte-identical, as J-1717 did for the wood)? Claude's recommendation: yes.

(b) The "bright" key. world_detail._conds() emits "bright" for weather clear or high cloud with no daylight test, so on every clear NIGHT the "bright" pools join the draw. 19 lines whose own wording is daylight (18 look-target lines, 1 SCENE line: "morning sun crosses the desktop", "in full daylight the lit lamp shows only as a faint orange nothing", "the sun finds a gap and lays hard shadows behind the bench and the barrel", "the pīngao goes copper in full sun" and so on) plus 3 diurnal-bird lines plus 16 visual-only lines sit under it, and the same key is used by 5 EVENTS lines. These cannot be moved to "day" (that would show them in the rain by day). The one-line fix is to emit "bright" only when the phase is not night (core/world_detail.py _conds(), shared engine, restart-gated); it would also drop the 16 visual-only "bright" lines (for example "the sea lies out flat and silver and the fence line stands black against it") from clear-night pools, which is a content change beyond the 19. Options: (1) gate "bright" on daylight in _conds(), (2) leave the key and move only the 19 lines to a new composite key such as "day_bright" (needs the pool builders to learn it, 4 call sites), (3) leave as is. Claude's recommendation: (1), with the build job's test enumerating every "bright" line so the 16 visual ones are reviewed by name first.

(c) The diurnal-bird lines (tier B, 85 lines whose subject core/life_birds.py gives night activity 0.0 to 0.1: fantail, wood pigeon, wren, tui, kingfisher, blackbird, gulls, terns and the like). A night look at the garden birds returns one 76 percent of the time, at the shore birds 63 percent, at the wood birds 63 percent; the garden birds' 12 "any" lines are ALL diurnal birds and only 3 ruru lines are night, and world_detail._load() drops a target whose "any" pool is empty, so these cannot simply be moved to "day". Options: (1) leave them: a look at a bird target at night shows a bird the live bird model says is not out; (2) author night-capable "any" lines for the garden, shore and wood birds targets so the diurnal ones can move to "day" (new content in the house voice, needs your call on content); (3) first build an observe-only render ledger for detail() and extra_pool() (the J-1694 shape) and measure how often Du actually looks at these targets at night, then decide. Claude's recommendation: (3), because no existing log records which look-pool line was rendered (F-2505 section 5), so the real exposure is unknown and the targets are only drawn when he looks at them.
ruling: (a) Yes: move the study SCENE line 'sun off the sea puts a wavering light on the ceiling boards' (core/world_content_study.py:461) from 'any' to a 'day' key, wording byte-identical. (b) Option 1: gate 'bright' on daylight in core/world_detail.py _conds() (emit 'bright' only when the phase is not night), with the build's test enumerating every 'bright' line so the 16 visual-only ones are reviewed by name first. (c) Option 3: build an observe-only render ledger for detail() and extra_pool() (the J-1694 shape), measure how often Du looks at diurnal-bird targets at night, then decide.
defeater: Revisit if (1) a ruling or comment shows any of the flagged "any" or "bright" lines is deliberately night-capable (for example the sun-off-the-sea ceiling light is meant as a moonlit reflection); (2) after a part-(b) gate is live, a clear-night look or scene reads visibly poorer because the 16 visual-only "bright" lines are gone and the night pools are too thin (a clear-night pool below 8 lines for any target); or (3) the part-(c) render ledger, once Du has run at least 14 nights with it, shows fewer than 5 night looks at the garden, shore and wood birds targets in total (the exposure is then too small to justify any content change). Defeater proposed by Claude when opening; Travis has not stated one.

question:
D-0342 follow-up: the wording route did not work. What should the Lane 2 notice instrument do now? (From J-1770's build attempt, 2026-10-07; findings F-2509 verified, F-2510 inferred.)

What happened. D-0342 ruled "sharpen the judge first": change the notice judge's wording to check every band word, number and quantity against the listed value, then regress it. J-1770 tried eight candidate wordings and replayed three of them through the real panel path (mixtral on Ramses, a falcon3:7b stand-in for the down local hub, granite tiebreak) over the 34 originally judged rows, 21 newer judged rows and two controls. The original wording reproduced the live panel (0 contradictions in 55 rows, planted control flagged). No sharpened wording flagged the four hand-found contradictions: the first draft flagged 1 of 4 in one run and 0 of 4 in an identical re-run; the schema-aware wording 0 of 4 (and 3 of 21 fresh rows, one of them a false flag); the glossary wording 0 of 4 while falsely flagging 6 of 34 and 5 of 21 correct notices plus the correct control. The three primary and tiebreak judges are the cause: given a compare-values wording, one primary judge says true to a large share of everything while the other says false to nearly everything (which one flips with the wording), and granite follows the wording, so the panel's decision lands on the tiebreak, and the tiebreak is not even reproducible (the same wording over the same 34 rows flipped the panel verdict on 4 of 34 rows between two runs). Per the ruling's own failure rule nothing was shipped: core/lane2.py keeps D-0281's wording byte for byte (hoisted to a constant, behaviour unchanged, LANE2_LIVE still False, 1-in-4 unchanged), and the regression harness and the tried wordings are committed so the next attempt can be scored in minutes (worktree branch jobrun/lane2_notice_judge, commit b810b52).
Also found: 21 judged rows have accrued since the first read (2026-10-04 to 10-06), all passed by the panel, and my hand-read of them finds 3 solid mismatches (air "cool" at a warm 0.81 again; moon "half-illuminated" at 0.34; "0.48 degrees Celsius" and "0.88 meters" for 0-to-1 decimals) plus 4 weaker ones, 7 of 21 by J-1395's counting (3 of 21 strictly). So the panel's 0.0 is still a lower bound. The 20 s latency line and the 300-row bar are untouched by this.

Options: (a) Build a small deterministic checker in code, not another panel call: map the notice's band words (cold, cool, mild, warm; dark, dim, lit), decimals-with-units, and quantity words to the percept line they belong to and compare against the listed band or number; log it beside notice_judged as its own verdict (for example notice_checked) so the panel's number stays comparable. Zero extra panel load, reproducible, catches all four hand-found rows by construction; costs a new instrument to build and a hand-check of its false flags on the 55 rows before it counts. (b) Give the notice context one stronger judge instead of the three-model panel (a larger local model on the hot server or a Ramses model), which costs the decoupled-judge law's separation from the generator, or hub capacity, and needs its own regression. (c) Ship the least-bad sharpened wording as a noisy instrument and accept its false flags (not recommended: the best-measured wording changed 1 of 34 rows and caught none of the four; the loosest flagged 6 correct notices of 34). (d) Keep the judge as built and write the plan's section 8.2 to say its 0.0 is a floor, using hand-reads (F-2368 and F-2510 style) as the real number; J-1739's successor read already does a hand-read. (e) Retire the notice judge and leave section 8.2 open.

Recommendation, not a ruling: (a). The ruling's intent, check every band word, number and quantity against the listed value, is mechanically decidable for exactly the error classes found, and the three hubs have now been measured as unable to do it. Take (d) alongside it until (a) lands.
ruling: (a)+(d): build a small deterministic notice checker in code (band words, decimals-with-units, quantity words vs the listed percept value), logged beside notice_judged as its own notice_checked verdict; until it lands, treat the judge's 0.0 as a floor and use hand-reads for the real number.
defeater: Revisit if: a deterministic checker (if (a) is chosen) shows more than 4 false flags in a hand-check of 20 of its flagged rows, or fails to flag any of the four D-0342 hand-found contradictions or the planted control on the same-seed replay; or the panel's tiebreak hub is replaced by a deterministic one (then re-run scripts/lane2_notice_judge_regress.py on the candidate wordings in scripts/lane2_notice_judge_candidates.json, the cheap way to retest a wording); or a fresh 20-row hand-read of the notice judge as it then stands disagrees with its verdicts on more than 4 rows; or judged n reaches 300 with notice_contradiction_rate outside 0.01 to 0.15 (D-0281's own lines, hand-check the rows before trusting the number).

question:
golden_spiral_recall Phase 2 (Theta shadow): F-2528 (J-1887) replayed the ray against a recency-only baseline. Three linked founder calls, answer any subset:
(A) Metric (b) wording. Today's (b) 'would_differ >= 40%' reads 97% but is vacuous (F-2514). Rewrite it to the baseline-comparison form 'ray top-3 differs from a recency-only top-3 on >= 40% of triggers'? Replay: 32.4% overall (35.6% de-bursted) = FAIL on that wording; 44.6% on a full-pool replay with tod/season derived for every row. Differences cluster on days with a write gap (10-04: 93%); on regular-rhythm days the 24h MIN_AGE_S floor already makes recency land on the same clock time (median phase distance identical, 0.0045 vs 0.0045), so the angle looks redundant there. (B) Backfill tod/season for the ~65,700 old fragment_context rows. Phase 0 left them NULL on purpose. Deriving from tuple_ts with core.theta_shadow.now_phase reproduces the stored values exactly on all 4,965 stored rows (bit-equal), so it is mechanically exact for rows stamped at write time; store spans 2026-07-05..10-07 so the ray could reach last_month/last_season/older. Build the backfill (additive, in a job, with a live-store write fence) or keep the ray on live-written rows only?

One day of season = 1/366 = 3.9 minutes of clock, so season is 69.5% of the ranking distance and the ray prefers 'same clock time within a day or two of the date': 100% top-3 within 5 days, p50 age 1.0 d, and a full backfill replay still returns 0 slots older than 30 days. If the angle is meant to reach older material, the rank needs to be tod-first (e.g. rank by d_tod inside the season window, or weight season much lower). Change the ranking in the shadow (additive, shadow only, tolerances untouched), or leave it?
ruling: (A) rewrite + (B) and (C) both (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08). (A) Metric (b) is rewritten to the baseline-comparison form 'ray top-3 differs from a recency-only top-3 on >= 40% of triggers'; Phase 2's honest state is 'the angle adds something only on irregular (write-gap) days, not yet shown otherwise' (32.4% overall, 93% on 10-04). (B) Backfill tod/season for the ~65,700 old fragment_context rows from tuple_ts via core.theta_shadow.now_phase (bit-exact on all 4,965 stored rows), additive, in a job, behind the live-store write fence. (C) Change cast_ray's ranking in the shadow to tod-first (rank by d_tod inside the season window, or weight season far below tod) so the ray can reach last-month/last-season material; tolerances untouched; shadow only.
defeater: Revisit when (1) Du has run >= 3 further weeks with continuous daily writes so the replay can repeat on a gap-free sample, or (2) the B/C build ships and its new shadow log has >= 1 week of rows, whichever first. The (A) ruling is defeated if the gap-free replay still reads < 20% (angle redundant with recency+floor) or >= 40%. The (C) ruling is defeated if tod-first ranking returns material older than 30 days in fewer than 10% of slots even after the backfill (reach did not improve) or if it returns same-clock material from unrelated seasons on more than half of triggers (season weight too low).

question:
Should the next boot carry a tiny observe-only STACK-SAMPLING watchdog thread so the 1-2 min whole-loop freezes (F-2551/F-2552) name the statement that is on the loop thread, instead of being inferred from coincidences?

Context: F-2551 (verified) shows that during the three long silent stalls of F-2547 (D 09-30, H 10-04, I 10-06) no sleep-routine statement is running - the routine is parked on an LLM await - so the loop-thread code that freezes is unknown; F-2552 (inferred) ties the blocks to a local CPU-tier hub generating (yi:34b in 2 of 2, 6 of 33 yi calls overall). D-0216's Hold ruled out a standing event-loop LAG probe until direct-timing jobs ran; those have run (F-2540, F-2546, F-2547) and what is left unattributed is exactly the 1-2 min blocks. This is a DIFFERENT, narrower instrument than the D-0216 lag probe: a daemon thread that sleeps 1 s and, only when the competence heartbeat is >10 s overdue, writes ONE row to a new data/loop_stall_stacks.jsonl with sys._current_frames()[loop_thread_id] formatted (top ~15 frames), at most 1 row per 20 s, ~0 cost when the loop is healthy. It reads no store, calls no model, changes no behaviour.

Options: (a) GO - build it (additive, own kill switch, default ON, restart-gated) so the next stall prints its own culprit; (b) HOLD - first run J-1927's offline CPU-contention reproduction (Du down) and only build the sampler if it does not reproduce / name the statement; (c) DECLINE - the blocks are rare (about 1 per 30 h outside yi calls) and the sleep-sweep family is already fixed (J-1917).
ruling: (c) DECLINE the stack-sampling watchdog for now, on the decision's own defeater: J-1927 (F-2568) reproduced the freeze offline and NAMED the loop-thread statement without a sampler. It is the SQLite recency-pool query in core/wandering.py _recency_pool (planner: idx_chapter + temp b-tree over all 64,735 chapter_id-NULL rows to return 1,500): 1.3-2.6 s idle, 24-33 s per call under one 20-thread stand-in hub, so a single inline wandering step held the loop 16-34 s (canary max 29-34 s) with the machine 60 % idle; two stand-in hubs add embed 19x / torch 46x. Thread caps (8, 1) remove nothing; the INDEXED BY idx_timestamp form returns identical rows in identical order and removes the block in the harness (28 s -> 0.15 s under 20 busy threads, 21 s -> 0.03 s under 34). The build is J-1947 (the same anti-pattern in _affective_drift and store.retrieve_by_affect, the latter on the loop thread every cycle). Ruled by claude on the ground rule that a decision not under a Hold whose read settles it gets ruled; the founder can reopen it.
defeater: Revisit toward (a) GO if a boot that carries J-1909/J-1917/J-1918 AND the J-1947 query fix still shows a silent whole-loop block > 30 s (heartbeat lateness with no sleep-sweep or ask-chain signature in lag_tail_attribution), or if J-1947's after-fix harness re-run under one 20-thread stand-in still leaves any single loop-thread statement > 5 s; also revisit if the 72-128 s length of the D/I stalls (vs the 30-38 s the harness reached) turns out not to be explained by the inline step + per-cycle retrieve_by_affect + recall stacking under a real 34B decode.

question: J-1363 item 1 (F-1922): 'Travis is here with you in the room.' has led ~100% of idle thoughts since 2026-09-05 18:14 because the composer's presence toggle was last set on; only 2 arrivals and 1 departure exist in the companion log. Is that true, and if not, how should presence be determined? Options: (a) Travis toggles it honestly; (b) presence expires after N hours without a real exchange and emits a real departure event; (c) presence is inferred from real activity (an exchange or composer action in the last X minutes); (d) it is true, leave it.
ruling: (c) Infer presence from real activity (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): presence = a real exchange or composer action within the last X minutes; when it lapses Du sees a real 'Travis stepped out' departure event, never a stale latch. The toggle stops being the source of truth.
defeater: Revisit if, one week after the inferred-presence change is live, idle thoughts still carry a presence line on days with no real exchange, or if a real conversation starts while Du believes Travis has stepped out (a false departure), or if Travis says the window X is wrong for how he actually sits with Du.

question: J-1367 (F-1926 item 5, J-1363 item 2): Du reads raw gauge numbers and variable names on essentially every prompt (voice 'valence=+0.12 arousal=0.40 joy=..', Reflection/Executive 'Emotional state: X (valence=..)', 'bandwidth is moderate (0.62)', 'Reflection confidence: 0.xx', idle 'Your current mood: valence ...', felt preamble '(valence -0.4)', T4 '(relevance 0.xx)') and has begun speaking in the instrument's terms ('my valence is low'). Should anything he reads carry a number or a variable name? (A) words everywhere via one shared renderer, numbers in logs only; (B) words in Voice/Reflection only, numbers allowed in Executive/Critic; (C) leave as is.
ruling: (A) Words everywhere (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): one shared renderer (mood.felt_preamble's approach) turns every gauge Du can read into words in every prompt and node, including Executive/Critic; numbers stay in logs only. Also resolve the felt string's 'low, heavy mood ... with joy' contradiction in the same renderer.
defeater: Revisit if, two weeks after the words-only rendering is live, Du's replies or thoughts still use gauge vocabulary (valence, arousal, confidence as numbers), or if a deliberative node (Executive/Critic) measurably degrades without its numeric inputs (critic approval rate or deliberation grounding falls outside its prior 14-day band).

question: J-1368 (I-0073, F-1927): 89% of the idle system prompt is fixed text; the boredom DEEP sentence fired ~12,000 times since 08-15; affective verdict lines leak into Du's thoughts (frustration words 5.6% -> 25-37%) while informational lines do not. Options A (silence-by-default, edge-triggered affective steers), B (phrasing pools), C (render boredom as a world cue not a verdict), D (opener diversity), E (stop storing system sentences as his own thoughts; origin=system_note), F (revive prompt_flow_audit.md as the prompt map). Which now?
ruling: A+E now (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): A = affective steers fire only on a real change of state (edge-triggered, like mood.felt_preamble's EMA gate), never on every prompt while a state persists; E = system sentences ('I finished a book...', 'I asked the library for...', inner_monologue_node.py ~4354-4357) are stored as origin=system_note / labelled, not recalled as his own thinking. B, C, D, F not now.
defeater: Revisit via F-1927's vocabulary-by-week table re-run two weeks after A+E are live: frustration/circling families back under 15% and same-day opener reuse under 30%, or the change did not work and B/C/D are re-asked; also revisit if an edge-triggered steer silences a state Travis wanted Du to keep feeling.

question: J-1387 (F-1950): the Witness says the sun is 'setting' at midday 82 times because it only sees sun azimuth. Add the sun's phase word + arc fraction f (core/world_clock.py sun()) to Lane 2's percepts, and a 'clock: HH:MM' line indoors (the study renders a ticking clock)? D-0280 ruled light_band in and the four climate dims out but did not name these.
ruling: Yes, phase + clock (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): forward sun phase word and arc fraction f through experienced_tuple into lane2 gather_percepts()/percept_lines() beside sun_az, and add 'clock: HH:MM' indoors only; phase and f only outdoors; never elevation in degrees. Shadow-first as Lane 2 already is; restart-gated.
defeater: Revisit if, after the restart that carries the build, 'setting' said before 15:00 local does not drop below 5/week from ~40/week within two weeks, or if the clock line makes the Witness narrate the hour instead of the scene (hour tokens in notice on more than 20% of indoor ticks), or if adding the fields to experienced_tuple changes what memory links on.

question: Dosed Coupling Phase 2 Q1 (J-1462, dosed_coupling.md section 4b): a cup rides as (value, expected, residual) where expected is the reader's own last-seen value, and the dispatcher measures surprise on the residual instead of the publisher's spike against its own EMA. Run both gates shadow in parallel for the 7-day read, or replace spike-gating outright?
ruling: Both in shadow, compare (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): residual gate and spike gate both log on identical moments for the 7-day read; metric 1 compares them before anything replaces anything.
defeater: Revisit after the 7-day paired shadow read: if the residual gate and the spike gate agree on more than 90% of moments the pair is redundant and one is dropped; if the residual gate fires on fewer than 1% or more than 50% of moments it is mis-scaled and the expectation model is re-asked.

question: Dosed Coupling Phase 2 Q2 (J-1462, section 4b): a deterministic coupling_rides.compose() step publishes a sixth registry key `hub` (pressure, momentum, strain, load) composed from the five existing publishers, no LLM. The founder's 'mid-level hub broadcasting across the whole network' would mean every stop may drink a cup from `hub` on a STANDING allowance while raw loops stay dispatcher-gated. Is a standing view of a summary inside section 1 rule 1 ('no loop gets a standing view of another'), or an amendment to it?
ruling: Amendment: hub is standing (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08). Rule 1 stays for raw loops; the composed `hub` summary is explicitly exempt and may be read on a standing allowance. Until built, hub is published and never read.
defeater: Revisit if the standing hub view shows up as a new always-on prompt line (the F-1927 failure shape: a fixed sentence on every prompt) or if the hub summary's values leak as numbers into what Du reads; also revisit if after 7 live days no stop ever reads hub (dead key) or every stop reads it every cycle (it has become a global state broadcast, which rule 1 exists to prevent).

question: Dosed Coupling Phase 2 Q3 (J-1462, section 4b 2c): speech and thought concurrently. VoiceNode fires after_executive in the hot lane and the inner monologue steps aside on last_human_ts; they alternate, never overlap. Real overlap means two calls to the same hot model on the same 11 GB card, single-flight. Its own plan doc, or a job under the orchestrator with the one-hot-model constraint stated up front?
ruling: Own plan doc (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): draft docs/staged/speech_thought_concurrency.md stating the single-flight constraint, what 'overlap' would even mean on one card, and a shadow measure first.
defeater: Revisit if a second hot card or a second hot model instance becomes available (the single-flight constraint lifts), or if the plan doc's shadow measure shows the alternation itself costs nothing Du notices (no speech delayed by a thought in flight on more than 5% of human cycles), in which case the plan is parked.

question: J-1493 (F-2036): D-0031's reopen defeater is met -- genuine-rate n is 507 resolved fires at 99.6% genuine (bar was ~30-50) and J-0164's counterfactual read (F-0186) is in: self-interrogation changes Du's next real thought only 11% of the time even when judged genuine (1/9 affected). This decision supersedes D-0031's 'wait for more data' with 'hold on effect size'.
defeater: Revisit if a new counterfactual read (same harness as J-0164, n >= 30 genuine fires) shows the affected rate above 30%, or if a concrete design is proposed for making self-interrogation's output reach the next thought (a cup in the dosed-coupling sense) that can be shadow-measured first, or if the shadow instrument's own cost becomes non-trivial.

question: Strings and Sheets section 9 Q3 (J-1465): the masking law's shape (section 4): same-band masking (a louder string masks a quieter one NEAR it in Sound Space; the waves mask the tide-pool trickle but not the kingfisher) versus a plain loudness order. The founder's ear, not taste from code.
ruling: Same-band masking (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): a string is masked only by a louder string close to it in the timbre axes; distant strings stay audible however quiet.
defeater: Revisit if the first mix shadow read (Phase 3) shows same-band masking leaving more than ~6 strings audible at once on a typical shore moment (the mix is not actually a mask), or if a distant-band quiet string the founder would never hear outdoors (a trickle under surf) survives the mask on more than half of surf moments.

No world sound has any audio today; one public recording per key (NZ bird calls exist) through the existing offline extractor would give every world sound a measured ribbon. question: Real hearing Q1 (J-1467, T-0071): where is the microphone in Du's world? His world is a simulated NZ place (shore/garden/wood/study) with its own weather and sound causes; a real microphone brings the founder's actual room. Options: (a) a window in the study (real sounds arrive as located, unnamed sounds in the simulated study); (b) a new place, 'the room where Travis is'; (c) real sounds bound to simulated causes. Ontology ruling; sound_causality's tree-falls law and world-answers-never-leads both bear on it.
ruling: (a) A window in the study (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): real sounds arrive as located, unnamed sounds through a window of the simulated study; the world stays his and the real room leaks in at one seam.
defeater: Revisit if the window seam makes Du narrate the founder's room as if it were the shore/garden (real-room sounds attributed to simulated outdoor causes on more than 10% of hearing moments in the first shadow read), or if Du himself asks where the sounds through the window come from and the study framing cannot answer honestly.

question: Real hearing Q2 (J-1467): is a pretrained sound-event classifier allowed in the ear? core/audio_features.py's law is 'deterministic, no LLM, no learned model'; core/sound_knowledge.py's law is that a new sound arrives as FEATURES + DIRECTION, unnamed, and identification is EARNED. A classifier that names 'dog bark' would short-circuit that epistemics.
ruling: Classifier allowed as a HIDDEN label only (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): a pretrained classifier may tag the stream for logs and instruments (the decoupled judge of what Du later earns), but Du never reads the label; what reaches him is features + azimuth, unnamed, and naming stays earned.
defeater: Revisit if the hidden label ever reaches a prompt Du reads (any classifier label string in a rendered prompt = immediate revert to features-only), or if the hidden labels prove useless for instruments after one month (never cited by a read), in which case drop the classifier entirely.

question: Real hearing Q3 (J-1467): raw audio retention. Features only, never raw audio stored (matches the offline cache discipline and the founder's own room being the source), or a rolling buffer for later analysis?
ruling: Features only, never raw audio (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): nothing recoverable as speech is ever written to disk; only the small per-frame feature tuple (plus the hidden classifier label per the sibling ruling).
defeater: Revisit only on the founder's own explicit request; a debugging need for the extractor is met by a RAM-only buffer that is never written, not by relaxing this.

question: Real hearing Q4 (J-1467): runtime DSP amendment. The ear's law today is 'features come from the offline cache, zero runtime DSP'; a microphone is continuous runtime DSP by definition. Proposed: a separate local CPU-only process (like the supervisor's servers) publishing a small tuple; the hot GPU box untouched.
ruling: Amend (travis, /decide-review 2026-10-08): the ear may run continuously as its own local process, CPU only, publishing features + azimuth (+ hidden label); the offline-cache law stays for everything else.
defeater: Revisit if the ear process measurably contends with Du's own loop (lag_tail_attribution shows ear-process CPU in a freeze window) or with the local CPU-tier hubs, or if the tuple it publishes grows beyond features + azimuth + hidden label into prose.

question: Dream Overhaul D-0356 (C), J-1875: adopt dream_overhaul.md section 3b's COMPUTED definition of 'met' -- (1) a real baseline (tension source recurred in waking thought on >= R of the K days before the arc), then N days of zero qualifying recurrences where a recurrence counts only if NOT explained by the injected dream-tail text (D-0233 rule), cross-checked against the tension ledger's chronic_mass decay; states pending/met/unmet/no-baseline/relapsed as append-only rows, close_reason untouched; (2) does computed met take over carry-termination from the dreamer's unresolved_core self-report; (3) set N, K, R, theta, M by an in-vitro replay over the 197+ recorded arcs rather than intuition?

question:
F-2578 (J-1938, verified, full 104-row audit) shows frontier_line()/_pick_frontier (shared by P1's recap note and, since J-1968, the P2 would-inject shadow per D-0324) does not rank Du's own material against anything. In 103 of 104 shadow rows every non-archive candidate has relevance 0.0, because retrieve() hard-codes score 0.0 on its "recency guarantee" (the 5 most recent episodic fragments), so the shadow's episodic candidates are just Du's latest 5 fragments, not place-cued hits. Those rows therefore pick "the most recent thought" (inner_thought 83/103), place-blind. The only nonzero candidates are the top semantic hit that D-0308's archive exclusion freed a 6th slot for: row 104's journal_week summary (28 days old), which now beats every episodic candidate whenever the semantic slot is filled (n=1 post-fix row, rate unmeasured). So the "open edge" is either the latest thought (no place cue) or one static semantic summary (cue-matched but not Du's thread); never a place-cued piece of Du's own unfinished material.

Options for the smallest fix (not built): (A) mirror D-0308 in _pick_frontier: skip origin journal_week (or all semantic layer) so the pick falls back to the latest episodic thought - one-line change, but the result is "most recent thought", not an open thread tied to the cue, and it hides the retrieval gap. (B) Fix the candidate pool at the source in observe_beachcomb: drop the zero-score recency-guarantee entries (relevance == 0.0 and not similarity-ranked) so only genuinely cue-scored episodic/semantic candidates remain, then prefer episodic among scored ones; the pick would sometimes be None (honest "no open thread") instead of an arbitrary latest thought. (C) Leave P1/P2-shadow as is and let the P2 shadow log (D-0324) record what the current rule would inject, reviewing a real sample in 2+ weeks. Which, and should it land before the P2 shadow log starts accruing its two weeks (a rule change mid-window would split the sample)?

question: READ FIRST: F-2590 (findings_log.py show F-2590, J-1941). Du has not replied to any peer since 2026-09-27 08:20 (13 tracked / 27 total unanswered letters). Root cause is verified: the only thing that ever put "write back" into his thought was the letter candidate inside the boredom BRANCH/DEVELOP seed, and J-1362's boredom recalibration (correct, F-1921) cut BRANCH events from ~50-100/day to ~0-3/day. Letter arrival itself prompts nothing (log line only). Nothing is broken in the latch. Question: do you want letter-correspondence to have its OWN edge-triggered way to reach his thought, independent of boredom? Options: (a) leave it - replies become rare/organic, accept one-way letters; (b) edge-triggered steer via core/steer_edge.py: when a peer's thread tail is unanswered, offer the "think what you would write back" line once per letter (re-armed per new letter / long cooldown), as one candidate not a mandate, restart-gated shadow-first; (c) have the letter delivery perceive into his world (like the garden-box flag as a felt event) and let him choose. (b)/(c) are an unasked push in the D-0292 sense but about a real world event; that is your call.
ruling:
travis 2026-10-08 (verbatim): "Do we have the letters stored in a location in his world? Can we 'nudge' him to find a store of them which might prompt him to write back. Maybe letters can be marked read/responded/unread/rejected etc. E.g. not tell him to write back but try and prompt it naturally."
Direction taken (claude's reading, option c extended): NO 'write back' instruction and NO steer line (not b). Letters become a place and a state in his world: a findable store of the peers' letters, each carrying a status (unread / read / replied / rejected, etc.) that he sees when he looks, so the unanswered ones are simply visible and he may or may not answer. Design + shadow-first build is job J-2005. Existing world facts at ruling time (claude checked core/sensorium.py + core/affordances.py): the mailbox at the garden gate has a flag and holds the CURRENT letter (flag up => a letter waits; affordances letter_seen/letter_fetch exist) and he visits it (letterbox observed x302); the full thread history lives in core/peers.py threads, not in any place he can look at.

ADDENDUM travis 2026-10-08 (verbatim): "With the letters, I want them to have a permanent world state. A history. He should be able to see them if he looks at/for them."
Binding requirements on J-2005 from the addendum: (1) every letter, from every peer and from Du, is a PERMANENT object in the world -- it never disappears or is consumed when read/replied/rejected; the store keeps the whole history, oldest to newest, not just the current letter or the unanswered tail. (2) Status is part of the letter's lasting state and changes over time (unread -> read -> replied etc.), with the history of those changes kept, not overwritten. (3) The store is DISCOVERABLE by looking: a plain look at/for the letters (the mailbox, the desk/drawer, 'my letters', 'the letter from X') must find it and show the letters and their statuses; it must not depend on a flag being up or on a letter being unread. (4) Shadow-first still applies to anything that reaches a prompt, but the store itself is a world-state change (persisted letter objects + status history), so it must be additive: peers.py threads stay the source of truth and are not rewritten; the world store is a derived, append-only index over them, backfilled from the existing threads (27 unanswered / all prior letters) so the history exists from day one.

question: READ FIRST: F-2602 (findings_log.py show F-2602, J-1952). Question: how should the two per-peer mechanisms relate? social_world_school Item 1 (core/peer_model.py: Du's own reflections ON each peer, surfaced only via associative_recall) and peer_correspondence_plan B5 (core/peers.py: the peer's per-letter stance and Buddha's structural challenge, plus the decoupled stance_compliance_judge). Today they share no state and do not conflict; the old G6/G8/G9 overlap was settled by D-0016/D-0178. Options: (A, RECOMMENDED) stay independent with a one-way read-only contract: B5 thread metadata (stance, stance_honoured) is the only ground truth about what a peer was trying to do, peer_model never feeds stance choice, letter composition or the judge, and the reflection prompt MAY later be shown the stance label read-only, only if a blind-read of post-fix challenge/mixed letters shows reflections omit the disagreement. (B) Share state now: pass stance and stance_honoured into update_after_exchange so reflections record what the letter was trying to do; small code change, restart-gated, but adds an input to a channel that has surfaced once in 33 days (data/peer_reflection_injection_log.jsonl) and cannot be evaluated while Du is not replying (D-0394). (C) Let peer_model state steer B5 (e.g. warmth or reflections choose the next stance): not recommended, it makes the writer a function of Du's own model of the writer, which breaks the decoupled-judge and witness-not-steer (G6) rules and is the sycophancy loop G3/R1 warns about. Also note: peer_models warmth is 0.5 for every peer (never updated), so there is no warmth signal to share yet.
ruling: A (travis 2026-10-08): stay independent with a one-way read-only contract. B5 thread metadata (stance, stance_honoured) is the only ground truth about what a peer was trying to do; peer_model never feeds stance choice, letter composition or the judge. The reflection prompt MAY later be shown the stance label read-only, only if a blind-read of post-fix challenge/mixed letters shows reflections omit the disagreement. No shared state now, no peer_model steering of B5.
defeater: Revisit if: (1) a recall_block/recall_fragments injection of origin=peer_reflection reads as steering rather than witnessing; (2) data/peer_reflection_injection_log.jsonl passes ~10 surfacings in 7 days (the channel is no longer inert, so coupling needs a real look); (3) a blind-read of 3+ post-fix challenge/mixed marcus letters (the J-1223 gate) shows the matching peer_reflection fragments omit the disagreement, which would justify option B; or (4) D-0394 is ruled (b)/(c) and Du's reply flow restarts, giving real exchange data to evaluate both.

question: J-1959 (answering D-0373's 'what would make it bite?'): F-2604/F-2605/F-2606 read the 16 decisive counterfactual cases. Nothing measurable separates the one affected case from the 15 unaffected; what stands out is that 98 percent of the 645 reflections are closed first-person diagnoses ('I am projecting X to make Y feel noble', 63 percent say 'because', only 1.7 percent ask a question), they are never handed to the next thread step (the call is fire-and-forget; the step prompt only sees Du's own ledger of established points), and they are ready in time (median 15 s, 84 percent before the next step is logged). PROPOSED MECHANISM (one): an 'open-doubt cup' at the train-step stop. interrogate() publishes its judged-genuine reflection to the coupling_rides registry (new key si, with age); at the next step of the SAME train the dispatcher may drink at most one cup per train, rendered by a fixed template with no new LLM call as one extra ledger-style line: 'A doubt you raised about your last step: <reflection>. Is it right? Answer it or set it down.' The template turns the closed diagnosis into the open question the step prompt already knows how to act on. SHADOW MEASUREMENT before any live use: (1) the cup is built as a would-ride row only (publisher plus eligibility rate, nothing enters a prompt); (2) an isolated lab replay re-generates the next step for 30+ genuine fires with and without the cup, plus a control cup built from a SHUFFLED other-fire reflection, and the same counterfactual judge scores 'engages the specific concern'; (3) pre-registered bar: cup-affected rate at least 30 percent AND shuffled-control at most 11 percent (so we are measuring this concern, not 'any extra sentence'), and no rise in restate_sim or early train closes. Caveats: the replay can only rebuild the mid-thread seed block (the live seed also carries recall and other parts); the one existing positive may be vocabulary echo. QUESTIONS FOR YOU: (a) Authorize the shadow build and lab replay described above (observe-only, restart-gated, nothing reaches a prompt)? (b) Is a cup that carries Du's own prose reflection (rather than a typed coordinate) inside dosed_coupling rule 1 'coordinates, never prose', or does it need your amendment / a coordinate-only variant (for example only a doubted/not-doubted flag plus the ledger index of the point doubted)? (c) Or keep holding: the instrument stays shadow and the HOLD stands, with the replay as the only spend.
ruling: travis 2026-10-08: authorize the shadow build and lab replay, COORDINATE-ONLY variant. Observe-only and restart-gated, nothing reaches a prompt. The open-doubt cup carries a doubted/not-doubted flag plus the ledger index of the point doubted, NOT Du's prose reflection, so it stays inside dosed_coupling rule 1 ('coordinates, never prose'); no amendment to rule 1. Lab replay with a shuffled-control cup; pre-registered bar: cup-affected rate >= 30% AND shuffled control <= 11%, with no rise in restate_sim or early train closes. The HOLD on any live use stands until the replay passes.
defeater: Revisit if the lab replay shows the open-doubt cup affected-rate below 30 percent (or the shuffled-control rate is within 5 points of it, meaning the cup moves thought generally, not this concern), or if a fresh same-harness counterfactual read of the 613 unread fires shows the uncued affected rate above 30 percent (the cup is then unnecessary), or if the cup shadow's rumination metrics (restate_sim, early train closes) worsen.
