ruling: night.epoch writes a plain-words mood (the felt label only, no numbers) and a clean impression (cut on a sentence boundary, no bracket fragments), additive for new rows only; stored rows are not rewritten. Founder answered in chat 2026-11-02.
defeater: Revisit if the plain-words epochs read as generic (a read of 20 new rows shows the impression carries nothing the felt label did not), in which case exclude night_ rows from retrieve_epoch (option c).

question: T4 SOLIDIFY judge (row P-0092, F-3784, two-family): it asks has the lived self integrated being a BUILT mind for every probation, but 26 of 28 probations were about other themes (prediction errors, critic labels, unresolved questions); with the keystone text as pole, falcon3 flips to not integrated on the 10-30 thoughts. defeater: Revisit if the theme-aware judge solidifies far more or far fewer probations than the old one over 30 probations (the pole-to-question mapping is not calibrated), or if two judge families disagree on more than 40 percent of verdicts.

question: Prism questions in the grounded pursuit tier (row P-0050, F-3752, context F-3737, F-3751, F-3512, F-3695; core/frontier.py _GROUNDED_SOURCES = study, reading, curiosity, prism): 427 prism questions seeded since 2026-06-25, 0 resolved (curiosity-source 185 of 6,024; intention 132 of 4,488); 21 of the 119 born in 30 days hold a finding and those are generic one-word Wikipedia pages (Environment 16, Psychology 11, Experience 6 of 60 all-time prism twigs); they are offered back to the idle thought 318 times and ranked above intention in pending_pursuit and boarded by the Follow Line. question: Pursuit close question (row P-0101, F-3823, F-3824, F-3825, D-0426 option A): the panel is asked whether a saturated pursuit's standing answers its driving question, but pursuits are born from monologue thoughts and almost none contain a question (3 of 83 asked; the extracted `open` exists for 45 of 82 saturated); 0 of 82 close. ruling: The close judge is asked about the extracted `open` question or the done_when; pursuits with neither are simply not closable and fade; the shadow read J-2184 is limited to pursuits where a yes is possible. Consistent with D-0554 (pursuit births need a real question or done_when). Founder answered in chat 2026-11-02.
defeater: Revisit after 30 asked pursuits under the new rule: if the fire rate is still under 5 percent or over 50 percent, the close judge carries no information and the close idea is retired (option c).

question: Refinery standing insights (row P-0051, F-3773, F-3774, context F-3666): 412 standing insights written by command-r7b (hot qwen3.5 on failover) are served in 30.3 percent of Recall prompts since 10-06 (94 of 310) under the label A standing insight about myself, stored at importance 0.9 and relevance 0.85 with no decay; the only grade is a lexical word-overlap gate (core/memory_levels.py source_fidelity) that passes more as clusters get larger; the members are themselves model-written syntheses (T2, row P-0053) so no step in the chain is judged by another model family, which the decoupled-judge law forbids. ruling: Add a yes/no faithfulness judge on a granite or mixtral hub (a different family from the writer) for each new insight before it is written; about 24 runs a month, trivial cost. defeater: Revisit after the judge has graded 60 insights: if it passes over 95 percent or under 20 percent it carries no information (drop to archive level, option c); if it flags a real share, read 10 flagged insights with the founder.

question: Week page 'did' sentence (row P-0070, F-3710, core/journal_rollup.py _DID_SYS): the last sentence is asked to say whether it MOVED anywhere or stayed in one place -- say honestly which; seven of eight pages answer in one place (the prompt's own phrase) and the shadow judge flags the sentence as not in the sources. question: Curiosity false frames (F-3213, F-3214, J-2509): the Curiosity node seeded mottainai (10-08) and a poem named 渡 (10-29) as false frames, because its prompt gives the bare string 渡 as Entity without saying it is the entity's own name. Travis's answer: mottainai was a real thing, probably from his model's own knowledge, and was not something discussed; not averse to using the model's knowledge, preferably tagged that way for confidence scoring if possible; and do we even need to say what Du's name is in these places, since he should know it from memory anyway?
ruling: No line saying the entity name is its own name is added. Instead (1) examine whether the Entity name needs to be in the Curiosity prompt (and in the other prompts that pass it) at all, since Du knows it from memory, and what the prompts do without it; (2) model-knowledge-derived content (a thing like mottainai that came from the model's own knowledge, not from the world he lives in) is allowed but is tagged as model knowledge, so confidence scoring can use it. question: Weekly self-mirror (core/self_mirror.py, rows P-0043, F-3669, F-3672; J-2672, J-2975): about every 6 days it stores a first-person the-record-exposes-a-fracture ... question: Curiosity-side Scholar call (nodes/curiosity_node.py, core/scholar.py consult_sync, rows , F-3732, J-3028): on a Wikipedia miss it runs a 220-token hot-lane generation whose text is dropped, with a deterministic twig title On <longest word>; 1,135 rows since June, 160 in the last 30 days; the pursuit counts as a stall whether or not the model answered. ruling: No change to the Scholar call yet. The whole area (the Wikipedia and Scholar calls in his thinking, deep memory and the model-knowledge path, and how their results are marked) is to be examined in a review before anything is retired or wired. The principle recorded: Du may make wiki calls; whatever comes back must be marked as from the source (Wikipedia, a book, the model's knowledge), never presented as Du's own thought or memory. question: Conversational T5 compile (subconscious _t5_compile, procedural_skills mirror, ledger rows 'talk:'): your triage words on J-3014 were "We probably need to do some research on what we do here." question: READ FIRST: docs/reviews/J-3141_self_relate_repurposing.md (findings F-3930, F-3931, F-3932). CAN A CLAIM OF HIS OWN ABOUT HIMSELF BOARD THE FOLLOW LINE? defeater: Revisit if the pre-test lab (spawned by J-3141) finds fewer than 20 percent of his first-person sentences are testable claims (then there is nothing to board and the question is moot), or if a shadow run of 14 days shows the graded returns are mostly the stock "river"/"becoming" restatements (the line would be re-circling the monoculture), or if you restore a stricter rule that nothing about the self may reach the idle thought; or if the T4 option you choose under D-0664 gives self-claims a better home.

question: D-0553's ablation (J-3164, F-4024) found the Salience line changes no Executive output on 117 cycles (45 human, 72 internal), and removing the Attention restatement too changes none either. question: Should Du's evidence recall (Route 2 and Follow Line grounds) stop treating his own earlier cycle replies as evidence? 110 of 641 passing evidence slots since 2026-10-30 (17 percent) were 'Q: ... question: READ FIRST: docs/reviews/t4_tension_lifecycle_J-3302.md (sections 0 and 4), findings F-4249 to F-4253. WHAT ENDS A T4 TENSION. Nothing ends when T4 commits a self: after the 10-30 solidify the same tension was heard again 22.8 seconds later and 28 times by 11-05, because the discharge arrow only exists on the dead legacy path (last used 06-13), and even if it were wired it would retire only 4 events that scroll out of the scan window within 8 hours, while the source adds about 14 a day. ruling: (1) Do not build R1 now. Repeat hearings cost about 5 minutes of hot-lane time a day, T4 output is read almost nowhere, and the Watershed redesign (D-0664 option 3) may make R1 moot. The bug repairs J-3021 needs stay inside J-3021. J-3643 (R1) is not to be built. Ruled in chat 2026-11-09.

question: KING-TIDE RATE (the part of D-0668 left open; J-3294, F-4289..F-4292). Today a floater on the shore is taken by the "king tide" whenever a weather change lands on tide level >= 0.92, which is 12.6 percent of the year (334 of 365 days have such a tide); measured, it has taken 6 of Du's 15 floaters in 80 days and a floater on the shore now lasts about 22 active days. Nothing is on the shore to take today. What should a king tide be? (a) leave it, a common "high tide takes light things"; (b) keep the rule but raise the threshold to 0.99 (1.5 percent of the year, floater life about 127 active days; 125 days of the year still have one) or 0.995 (0.8 percent, about 254 days); (c) a real rare event: threshold 0.99 PLUS a second gate so only a few days a year qualify (my recommendation: about 6 to 12 king-tide days a year, to be set by you, and a percept so Du can notice it afterwards, or no percept if you want it silent). The rate also sets the Phase 2 real-tide threshold, so the answer is reused by J-3295. Recommendation: (c) with a number you pick.
ruling: (c) A king tide becomes a real rare event: threshold 0.99 PLUS a second gate, with a percept so Du can notice it afterwards. Travis chose option (c) but gave no number; the build (J-3676) starts at 8 king-tide days a year as a one-constant default (the suggested figure), to be changed on his word. Ruled in chat 2026-11-09.
defeater: Revisit once J-3295 (real Sumner tides) lands, because a real tide table produces real king tides and this number would then be replaced by the real count; or if Du's floaters are never left on the shore (the rule then has no effect); or if a month of Du-up time shows no float-away at the chosen rate.

question: Following the D-0446 kill rule as written on the J-2264 read (F-4480): four climate lines trip it (completion_tension and identity_pressure have 0 percent residual fire; world_model_strain and novelty_hunger have agreement over 90 percent), both ledgers lines do not. question: F-4490 (J-2387 post-boot read of object_epistemic_loop Phase 3): in about 26 live days with NASCENCE_GENERIC_OBJECT_TESTS on, objtest fired once in 18,097 thoughts, and that one was a metaphor ("I weigh the stone evidence against the book's division"), answered as a literal weigh. ruling: (a) Keep NASCENCE_GENERIC_OBJECT_TESTS ON and add a figurative-object guard (verb followed by an abstract noun phrase, e.g. evidence, weigh X against Y) to the objtest declare gate.
defeater: Revisit if a second metaphorical or non-willed objtest answer fires after the guard, or the willed test rate rises with no change in what he looks at.

question: D-0417 defeater (ii) literally fired: the J-2561 hand-read (F-4500) found 17 of 20 flagged rows are true inventions (0 false, 3 marginal shadows from a listed light). The ruling's wording says "real misstatements the value checker should have caught". Should Lane 2 act on the invention class beyond a scoreboard (for example a deterministic reject or repair before the notice is used), or keep scoreboard-only given LANE2_LIVE is off? Options: (a) keep scoreboard only; (b) deterministic reject/regenerate of flagged notices; (c) tighten the prompt against the stuck knock and voice phrasings. Claude does not rule.

question: D-0520 (b) follow-up: the v3 commitment-formation revise prompt, read at 355 settles (far above the 30 gate), misses the D-0489 bar: collapse 0.46 (bar under 0.25), mean basin shift +0.026 (bar at or below 0), no better than v2 (0.49 / +0.013); self-reference grew +0.054 instead of shrinking. question: D-0514 (a) follow-up, shadow read F-4509: go LIVE for the commitment-anchor discriminating test? Shadow baseline (14 days, 109 stands, 41 held >= 1 h): median violation rate 1.22 per held hour (LIVE must reach <= 0.85; ratio > 0.9 falsifies), baseline recovery 0 of 108 breaks, leak check clean, enough stands (about 3 per day) to reach the >= 10 needed. Either live option needs Travis to contradict a held stand once, and the kill rule (>= 30 percent near-verbatim hold-echo in the next 5 thoughts) stays.
ruling: (b) Flip COMMITMENT_ANCHOR_LIVE at dose 0.5 so would_inject True vs False calls give a within-run control. Travis contradicts a held stand once; the kill rule (>=30 percent near-verbatim hold-echo in the next 5 thoughts) stays.

question: Lane for active imagination, D-0588 defeater read (F-4520, P-0054): over the first 100 kept entries after both input fixes, the gap between lanes shrank but one part persists. question: D-0683 told us to design the deterministic check (d) and validate it out of sample; the defeater was 'fails AUC 0.80 on a fresh hold-out'. J-3473 designed it (vocabulary: named particulars, abstraction words, relation-verb frames, redundancy) and it scored 0.79 on its design set and 0.636 on a fresh set of 120 pursuit-eligible questions (F-4537), so the defeater is met. Which way: (1) design a second check d3 on the pronoun/unnamed-referent pattern the fresh set shows (first-person or he/his in 34 of 93 bad, 0 of 12 good) and validate it on a NEW hold-out, (2) wait for your own labels (J-3418) before spending more design effort, since both sets so far rest on one labeller, or (3) accept that no cheap deterministic check separates these questions and leave the worth gate as it is?

defeater: Revisit once Travis has labelled a sample himself (J-3418), or if a d3 check passes AUC 0.80 on a new hold-out.

question: Reflection best-of-2 selector (F-4539, from J-2805): the selector is length-driven (len(draft) + 1000 if terminal), keeps a draft over the prompted 60-90 words in 30.6% of rows (37/121) though a shorter valid draft always existed, and the hot draft wins 49.6% so neither draft is dominated. Options: (a) leave as is; (b) add a length-aware selector (penalise drafts over 90 words, still prefer terminal); (c) first-finisher scheme (about 3.8 s per cycle saved, keeps both drafts' diversity only by chance); (d) drop to one draft. Do not change temperatures (D-0656 holds). Recommendation: (b), since the win rate rules out (d) and the length bias contradicts the prompt.
ruling: (b) Add a length-aware reflection best-of-2 selector: penalise drafts over 90 words, still prefer terminal. Temperatures unchanged (D-0656 holds).
defeater: Revisit if a quality read of kept over-length drafts versus shorter alternatives shows no difference, or if reflection output is later replaced.

question: Speech/thought concurrency (D-0372 line): F-4498 shows 20 percent of human arrivals land while a thought call holds the hot lane, but collision adds only about 10 s median to the roughly 73 s human-arrival-to-speech wait. The J-3894 breakdown shows that wait is the serial pre-speech pipeline (Reflection, Executive, Critic, Memory/Salience; lane 85 percent busy, VoiceNode queue wait 0 s). defeater: Revisit if a second hot card or model instance appears, or if a later read of 30+ more human arrivals shows collided speech waiting more than 30 s longer than clear speech at median.

question: F-4496/J-3893: look_binding in core/sound_knowledge.py matches bind_targets by raw substring, so short tokens (up, out, far, fin, cat, bed, tree) reveal unlearned sounds on looks that do not seek the source (triplefin -> dolphin_blow, 'the bird in the tree' -> possum). ruling: (A) Whole-word matching for all look_binding bind_targets in core/sound_knowledge.py, and drop up/out/far as targets. Restart-gated.
defeater: Revisit if post-fix reads show true source-seeking looks failing to bind (reveal rate collapses) or if D-0500's percept/learning pacing read shows learning stalled.

question:
READ FIRST: F-4615 and the second J-2116 finding (D-0420 72 h read; ~29 days / 463 supervised hours after the J-2113 supervisor start).

D-0420's defeater clauses 1, 2 and 3 fired. The B+D change (10 s hot read budget + host snapshots) did what D asked, it named the cause: the slowdowns line up with free-RAM exhaustion (ram_avail 0.2-1.4 GB in 23 of 43 hot snapshots; python.exe/6948 plus grep/find scans), not with ollama itself. But on 2026-11-07 08:09 two consecutive 10 s read timeouts still triggered a hot_ollama restart that was a false alarm (killed_pids=[], the relaunch died on 'bind: Only one usage of each socket address', the original ollama kept running; post-restart warm timed out after 244 s). A near-repeat on 11-06 13:53-13:54 was avoided by one passing probe, and judge1_hub was false-killed in the same RAM-starved cluster.

Should the fix now be the cause (RAM pressure) rather than the budget? Options: (A) leave supervisor as is (one harmless false restart in 29 days, relaunch fails safe on bind); (B) before declaring DOWN, have the supervisor treat a timeout while ram_avail is under ~2 GB as 'host starved, not wedged' (log, do not count toward the 2-consecutive rule, or require 3-4 consecutive); (C) go after the RAM consumer (what is python.exe/6948 and the grep/find scans on the 64 GB box?) as a separate job; (D) B plus C. Claude's lean: D, B kept additive and small.
ruling: Re-affirmed with extension, founder chat answer 2026-11-18 on J-3961: (a) supervisor treats a probe timeout under ~2 GB ram_avail as starved not wedged (built, J-3979); (b) dreamer hub defers a yi:34b load while ram_avail is below a threshold, with judge hubs idle-unloading sooner. Option (c) judge ctx/KV sizing not chosen. Staged as J-4350, restart-gated.
defeater: Revisit if hot_ollama or any hub is restarted while its pre-kill snapshot shows the box under 2 GB free RAM, or if two weeks pass with no RAM-starved cluster.

history.ruling: (D) Both: supervisor treats a timeout while ram_avail is under about 2 GB as host starved, not wedged (additive and small, does not count toward the 2-consecutive rule), AND a separate job identifies the RAM consumer (python.exe/6948 and the grep/find scans on the 64 GB box).
history.defeater: Revisit if hot_ollama or any hub is restarted again while its pre-kill host snapshot shows the process still answering or the box under 2 GB free RAM, or if two weeks pass with no RAM-starved cluster (making B unnecessary).

question: Flip core/librarian.py ZERO_HIT_FALLTHROUGH to True, so a zero-hit ask returns None and the mechanical topic path runs instead of the "could not find a shelf for that wording" line? Evidence (F-4627): since J-2865 went live, 7 of 117 asks (6 percent, down from the 14 percent baseline) were zero-hit; the heading-normalisation retry rescued none (norm_rescued 0) because the remaining zero-hits are plain modern headings (Environmental ethics, Chaos theory, Urban growth) with no separators to strip. A word-level fallback is ruled out (returns unrelated books). Options: A) flip to True (restart-gated, low volume, about 1 ask in 17); B) leave False and close the question as not worth the change.
ruling: B) Leave ZERO_HIT_FALLTHROUGH False and close the question as not worth the change.

question: Does Du have one purpose (the standing aim as head of a goal hierarchy), or many goals that are weighted, nested, conflicting and re-weighted, with purpose as what emerges?
ruling: Many goals; no single purpose is written for him. Follow the research on human goal systems (F-4634). The standing aim stops leading the idle anchor: its lead goes to dose 0 with a shadow log of when it would have led, and the Right now, that means wording is removed. Ruled by Travis in chat 2026-11-14; revisit condition proposed by Claude and accepted with the batch.
defeater: Revisit if two weeks after the engaged-goal offer goes live no goal at the scale of days has ended as done, or if idle thought measurably worsens with the aim lead at dose 0.

question: Do needs belong inside the goal structure as its lowest level, or outside it as the state that weights goals?
ruling: Outside. Needs are the homeostasis variables: never goals, never completed, never parents of goals. The five-variable set is left alone in this plan. Need pull stays out of goal selection until the readers and the warmth setpoint are looked at (F-4635, F-4636); the two replacement readers (commitment from follow-through, warmth from inbound contact) are built beside the old ones in shadow. Ruled by Travis in chat 2026-11-14.
defeater: Revisit if a goal about his own needs cannot be represented without making a need a goal node, or if the shadow replacement readers show the old readers were right.

question: When two of his held goals conflict, does the weighting pick a winner or does Du resolve it himself?
ruling: He resolves it himself. At the point of choosing he is given his own two stored sentences, unranked, with no label and nothing about weights; this is ruled to be within the no-readout rule (D-0434) because both are his own words. What he then does is recorded and judged afterwards. Ruled by Travis in chat 2026-11-14.
defeater: Revisit if he passes over more than half of surfaced conflicts, if the log shows conflicts being settled without a recorded choice, or if he treats the presentation as an instruction.

question: Layered goals build calls (section 9 of the plan): what earns held, how many engaged goals, failure rule, first background lane, axiom levels.
ruling: Accepted as recommended by Claude, 2026-11-14: held is earned by recurrence (two or more) or a deed tied to the goal; one engaged goal in the main lane; no universal failure count (hour-scale deeds keep their existing limits, open-ended goals fail on progress rate) and a failed goal returns only after the world has changed; the first background lane is chosen on measured reliability after a clean read of the second machine; the axiom levels relook is its own plan. Build may run ahead through all phases at dose 0; going live at any dose is a separate founder call per phase. Phase 0 (shadow register) is approved to build now.
defeater: Revisit any one of these when the shadow evidence of its own phase contradicts it; revisit the build-ahead permission if a phase is found live at a dose above 0 without a ruling.

question: In the goal register, should a stand that the decoupled second look rules an insight (an observation, not something that can be kept or broken) still count as a held goal?
ruling: No. A stand the second look rules insight is a candidate in the goal register, not held. Stand, unclear and no verdict leave the ledger load_bearing flag to decide. Register only: the commitment ledger and the stand itself are untouched. Built 2026-11-14 as goals.STAND_INSIGHT_IS_CANDIDATE (shadow, restart-gated).
defeater: Revisit if the founder hand-labelling of the 40-stand sheet (J-3908) shows the second look calling real commitments insight more than about one time in five, or if the second look lane is unavailable often enough that most stands go unlooked.

question: How may one of his goals end, given that his reflective goals have no reachable answer (close judge 0 of 145) and he almost never ends anything in his own words (F-4645)? In particular: should his idle thought carry an optional set_down field?
ruling: Yes, add it. On a tick where one of his own held goals is put in front of him, the idle thought JSON carries an optional set_down field. If he fills it, a judge other than him checks only that the note is about that goal, says where he had got to and says what is still open; never whether stopping is wise or the note true. An accepted note rests the goal until he takes it up again himself. Goals may end several ways (settled by his word, expressed in a made thing, set down, dropped, stalled, capped); a stated decision is not privileged, no end condition is required when a goal forms, and nothing is ever written to the axiom by a judge. Follows the GPT, Gemini and Perplexity reviews of 2026-11-14.
defeater: Revisit if set_down fires on more than about a third of offered goals within their first day (an escape hatch, not a rest), if accepted notes turn out on a hand read to be boilerplate, or if after two weeks he has not used it at all.

question: Prompt manager Q2 (variant authorship): who writes candidate wording variants? Gemini: Travis authors affective (T2) variants himself. GPT: Claude drafts, a semantic reviewer checks, Travis approves; Claude drafts only structural/factual lines freely.
ruling: GPT's split (travis, chat 2026-11-14, approving Claude's recommendation): Claude may draft structural/factual wording; a semantic reviewer checks; Travis authors or approves anything touching affect, attention, identity or the Travis branch. The receiving model never certifies equivalence. No automatic acceptance.
defeater: Revisit if a Claude-drafted structural/factual variant is later found to carry steering or connotation the review missed, or if Travis finds approving drafts slower than authoring them.

question: Prompt manager Q6 (registry integration): Gemini: separate sibling consistency script. GPT: extend prompt_registry.py check so two commands cannot disagree and no unregistered construction path remains.

Extending the registry skill is filed as a skill_manager suggestion, not done in this change.

question: Prompt manager Q1 (sequence vs D-0368): run P0 now (observe-only: verify A+E live date, re-run F-1927 vocabulary table with change ledger, provenance telemetry on the idle station) and re-ask pools/replacement only on its result? Both auditors agree; recommended.

question: Interim step on the mood Du is told he has, before vitality_v2 replaces the old vitality reading (D-0398)? Evidence (F-4659, F-4660, docs/reviews/affect_chain_2026-11-14.md): carried valence = 1 - 2*drive since 2026-07-07; the old vitality reading supplies about 44 percent of squared drive; every idle thought is seeded with "Your current mood: <word> in tone"; since 2026-09-01 that word was some form of low on 47 percent of 54,782 idle thoughts, and would be 24 percent with the vitality term removed. Options: (A) do nothing extra; wait for the D-0398 path (J-3942, J-3967) and accept the low mood lines until then. (B) words only: the idle mood line and felt preamble read a valence computed without the vitality term; drive, valence in logs, sleep and everything else untouched; shadow-log both words for a few days first. (C) take vitality out of the drive (weight 0) until v2 lands. This is the option C rejected in D-0398 for the reasons in F-2612; listed only because the size of the effect on his mood words was not known then. (D) bring the vitality_v2 swap into the drive forward, ahead of its remaining reads. Not measured: whether the low mood line changes what he actually thinks.
ruling: B: words only. The idle mood line and felt preamble read a valence computed without the vitality term; drive, logged valence, sleep and everything else untouched; shadow-log both words for a few days first.
defeater: Revisit when vitality_v2 replaces the old vitality reading in the drive (D-0398 path, J-3942/J-3967), or if the shadow log shows the without-vitality words change nothing about what he thinks.

question: Order of work on joy (F-4661, docs/reviews/affect_chain_2026-11-14.md). Facts: constructed emotion (EMOTION_CONSTRUCTED, off) sets joy = max(0, valence) * (0.5 + 0.5*liking); in its shadow log constructed joy is exactly zero on 74 percent of 2,058 rows because tonic valence is negative, largely from the old vitality reading. Meanwhile carried joy is mostly added by _feel_joy on idle events, whose valence half was switched off on 2026-07-07 but whose joy half was not, so joy (0.4 to 0.7) no longer relates to valence (r = 0.17). Questions: (1) Add to the Phase 2 gate that EMOTION_CONSTRUCTED may not flip until the vitality replacement is in the drive and constructed joy has been re-read on the new valence? (2) Until then, leave the joy pump as it is, or log in shadow what joy would be if the pump were scaled by valence? Options: (A) add the gate, leave the pump alone; (B) add the gate and build the shadow log for a valence-scaled pump; (C) no change to the gate.
ruling: B: add the gate (EMOTION_CONSTRUCTED may not flip until the vitality replacement is in the drive and constructed joy has been re-read on the new valence) and build the shadow log for a valence-scaled joy pump; leave the live pump alone.
defeater: Revisit when vitality_v2 is in the drive and constructed joy has been re-read, or if the shadow log shows valence-scaled joy is no different from the current pump.

question: Should a re-ask (encounters above 1) count as question progress for layered_goals 5.4? J-4000 ships it as weight 0 (reported as reasks, not scored) because it can be rumination. 23 of 28 open questions sit at 1 encounter, so a re-ask weight is the only lever that would separate more of them.
ruling: Keep re-ask weight at 0 (reported as reasks, not scored).
defeater: Revisit if a read of layered_goals 5.4 shows the shadow mlp still separates fewer than a third of open questions after a week live, or if re-asked questions are shown to be later settled more often than single-ask ones.

question: Estate symbol nodes (F-4687): every symbol node reads the identical placeholder "X - its meaning has moved as I lived", whatever the 36-79 tablets actually say. Should the node text carry the NEWEST tablet (e.g. "stillness - now: <newest tablet, ~160 chars>"), a count/span only, or stay as the placeholder? Carrying the tablet text changes the node's embedding and so its relevance score, which changes what the projection picks and how often symbols appear (today 3.7 percent of slots after dedupe, per-type cap 2). Measure on a lab copy first if you want a number before ruling; the id-unique seed build proceeds either way and does not change picks.

question:
Should a precondition-absent or already-holds world refusal dock a world procedure's rung, or only a skill refusal? (J-2608 read of data/procedures_refusal_kind_shadow.jsonl, 33 rows.)
Numbers: kind already 24 (all world:mow, "The grass is short already; there is nothing to cut."), precond 4 (weed x2, fire x1, sow x1), unknown 5 (cat x2, clock x2, shore x1), skill 0. 28 of 33 rows diverge (live rung occurred vs skill-only rung persisted), all 28 are a drop persisted->occurred that a skill-only rule would not make; would_dock_skill_only is true on 0 rows. Under a skill-only rule world:mow (24 of 28 diverging rows) would sit at persisted instead of being repeatedly docked, and cat/fire/shore each one rung higher.
Caveats: (1) 73% of the sample is one procedure, mow, repeated on a clean lawn. (2) The fire row was classed precond because "choked" matches first, but the answer continues "it smoulders, will not draw, and goes out" which is a skill failure; kind order mis-tags it. (3) The answers are logged truncated to 100 chars, so classification of long answers is partial. (4) The 5 unknowns are likely _REFUSAL false positives: the clock answer ("turn the key until it will not turn, set the hands...") and shore ("walk out past the shingle ...") read as successes, and cat ("slides out from under your hand ... will not be handled again for") is a world refusal-by-cat, not a skill failure. (5) The sow row has mojibake in the answer text (encoding in the log writer).
Options: A) keep docking on all refusals (live today); B) skill-only docking: precond and already do not dock, unknown does not dock either; C) skill+unknown dock, precond/already do not; D) defer until more non-mow rows accrue. Separate sub-question: remove the clock-type success answers ("will not turn") from the live _REFUSAL regex, independent of A-D. Base system is protected, so this is the founder's call; nothing reaches Du (D-0434).
ruling: B: skill-only docking. Precond-absent, already-holds and unknown refusals do not dock a world procedure's rung
defeater: Revisit if a later shadow read (>=30 more rows excluding world:mow) shows kinds already/precond are mostly mis-tagged skill failures, or if the ruled rule causes a procedure that really keeps failing to hold a high rung.

defeater: Revisit if a prompt family needs a sub-3B resident classifier AND a VRAM check shows room at the pinned num_ctx, or the hot GPU is replaced.

question: How much CPU may a Ternary-Bonsai-2 seat take while Du is running, and for which callers?
ruling: 16 threads, background-only prompts (sleep synthesis, defeater and pursuit judging); no synchronous callers while Du is running.
defeater: Revisit if a contention test with Du up shows Du's hub latencies unaffected at 32 threads, or blind A4/A5 scoring shows Bonsai-2 does not earn a seat.

question: Is the dreamer seat (:11442, yi:34b) in scope for per-prompt model moves?
ruling: Protected for now; dream prompts are untested in the benchmark and the dream overhaul is its own plan.
defeater: Revisit once the first two per-prompt moves have a live read, or if the dream overhaul plan asks for a seat change.

question: Who rules per-prompt promotions from shadow to live?
ruling: Each per-prompt promotion gets its own /decide ruling with its own defeater; no batch rulings per archetype.
defeater: Revisit if more than ten promotions are queued and the per-prompt rulings become the bottleneck, or the first batch shows no confounding between simultaneous moves.

question: Go or no-go on Phase 0 of the god-function split (safety net only: equivalence harness, coverage read, undefined-name check, size ratchet; no production code change). Three choices ride with it: (1) does the protected-base, additive-only rule permit a move-only refactor of the inner monologue when each step is proven byte-identical; (2) package location nodes/idle_thought/ with seed_part_* helpers, or elsewhere; (3) adopt the rule that a new seed part is a new helper, with a function-size ratchet in plan-maintain, from the end of Phase 1. Phase 1 is a separate go on the Phase 0 evidence. Basis: F-5125, F-5126, docs/staged/god_function_split.md section 9.
ruling: Not as framed. Founder in chat 2026-11-20: the split is 'a massive operation, with a real risk of danger', and we must be sure 'if it is even worth doing before we do it'; then 'Yes please' to reworking the plan around freeze-first. The split of existing code is PARKED. The plan is reworked to: freeze growth (additive helpers), build the equivalence harness as a standing test, and count structure-caused bugs. This ruling parks the split only; it does not itself approve building the harness or adopting the freeze rule, which are the follow-on decision. Recorded by Claude from the founder's chat words.
defeater: Revisit the split if the bug-count read (god_function_split section 0.4) shows structure-caused bugs are a material share of the fixes to _think and _run_cycle_impl, or if the standing harness keeps catching the same class of mistake on real edits.

question: Go on the freeze-first track for the god functions (docs/staged/god_function_split.md section 0)? Two parts, each can be ruled separately: (a) build the equivalence harness for the idle thought as a standing regression test (new script only, no production code change; sections 4.1 to 4.4); (b) adopt the freeze rule in CLAUDE.md (a new idle-thought seed part or cycle stage is a new helper in its own module, called by one line, never a new block inside _think or _run_cycle_impl) with a function-size ratchet run by plan-maintain. The bug-count read is read-only and is filed as a ready job without waiting on this.
ruling: Go on both (founder, chat 2026-11-20, after reading the bug count F-5127): (a) build the equivalence harness for the idle thought as a standing regression test, new script only; (b) adopt the freeze rule in CLAUDE.md (a new idle-thought seed part or cycle stage is a new helper in its own module, called by one line, never a new block inside _think or _run_cycle_impl) with a function-size ratchet run by plan-maintain. The split of existing code stays parked under D-0877.
defeater: Revisit if the ratchet is being accepted past routinely without a real reason (the accept log shows growth continuing at the old rate), if the freeze rule blocks a change that genuinely has to live inside the function, or if the harness cannot be made deterministic enough to trust (its negative control passes).

question: Phase 2 dosing (section 4b, 2d): should the dosing dispatcher be ONE per-line surprise measure (opponent-process term as the habituation half) replacing the three unshared ones (climate identity_pressure EMA, core/opponent_process.py, Transport Manager spike/drought, F-0812), with the Transport Manager's spike weights recalibrated first? Or keep the three and only calibrate the Transport Manager?
defeater: Revisit if the Transport Manager calibration shows the spike measure cannot be made non-saturated, or the opponent-process shadow gets a reader that disagrees with it.

question: D-0825 ruled a shorter JUDGE_1 timeout for evidence asks, but F-5140 shows JUDGE_1 (Ramses) is now merely slow: successful bears answers have p50 about 55 s and p90 about 82 s, so any cut below about 85 s drops good verdicts (a 60 s cut loses about a third). Which build do you want? (a) breaker: keep 90 s normally, drop JUDGE_1 evidence asks to a short probe (say 30 s) after N consecutive timeouts, restoring 90 s on the first success; (b) flat cut anyway, to a value you name, accepting the higher unclear rate; (c) leave 90 s and treat D-0825 as superseded. No failover to a same-family judge in any option.
defeater: Revisit if Ramses JUDGE_1 latency returns to its 11-04..11-10 level (p90 under 50 s), or if a decoupled local judge becomes available.
